item.title: Outdated rental listings leave Dhaka tenants wasting time and money
item.description:
Finding a rental home in Dhaka can be time-consuming, with prospective tenants increasingly turning to websites and mobile applications to search for properties. However, outdated advertisements, inactive phone numbers, and unclear refund procedures have raised concerns about the reliability of online rental services.
One user searching for a home in Dhaka called a number listed in an online advertisement and learned that the property had been rented out several months earlier. After spending credits to contact another advertiser, the user received no answer. At a third listing, the user followed the address but found no information about a property available for rent.
Similar complaints have emerged from users of online rental platforms, who say incorrect or outdated advertisements waste their time and, in some cases, leave them struggling to recover money or credits spent to access contact information.
There are no comprehensive statistics showing what proportion of online rental advertisements in Bangladesh are incorrect, outdated or inactive. However, reviews on the Google Play Store pages of rental applications include complaints about old listings, inactive phone numbers and difficulties obtaining credit refunds.
As of October 25, 2026, Bikroy's website displayed around 3,109 advertisements for houses and apartments for rent across Bangladesh. The number of advertisements in individual categories can change as listings are added or removed. Figures for properties costing less than Tk15,000 per month and two-bedroom properties require confirmation against a dated record of the website before publication.
Kohinur Akter, a working professional who was looking for a two-room flat in Dhaka's Azimpur area, said she paid to access contact information after reviewing property photographs, rents and addresses.
“I bought credits to access contact information after checking the pictures, rent and addresses of properties online. When I called several numbers, I learned that the properties had already been rented out. One phone was switched off. My question is, why was the advertisement not removed if the property was no longer available? Will I ever get back the money I spent to access the information?”
She added: “Finding a home already takes a lot of time. It is not easy to travel from one place to another after office hours. If I cannot get reliable information even after paying online, what is the benefit of this system?”
Similar complaints appear in reviews of rental applications on the Google Play Store. In a review dated August 27, 2026, a user complained that many advertised properties had already been rented out and some phone numbers were inactive. The review said accessing each advertisement cost 20 credits.
Another review, dated July 15, expressed dissatisfaction with credit prices and the process of obtaining refunds.
These reviews document individual complaints but do not establish how frequently such problems occur across the online rental market. No comprehensive public figures show the proportion of outdated or incorrect advertisements or the number of users who have experienced financial losses.
Online rental platforms have different procedures for handling complaints and refund requests. Some require users to report problems within a specified period after accessing an advertisement, while others outline conditions under which credits or service fees may be refunded if a property is unavailable or an advertiser cannot be reached.
THE TOLET, a rental application listed on the Google Play Store, responded to a user review on August 9, 2026, saying users could request credit refunds through their user panels within 72 hours if a property was unavailable. The response also directed users to the platform's support email for assistance.
The response establishes what the platform publicly stated about its refund procedure but does not show how many users have received refunds or how consistently the policy has been implemented.
Published terms of online rental services may also require landlords or agents to keep property information, photographs and availability details up to date. Some platforms state that they do not guarantee the accuracy of information supplied by advertisers.
However, publicly available information does not provide a comprehensive picture of the number of complaints rental platforms receive, advertisements they remove or refunds they approve. Without such data, it is difficult to assess how effectively their complaint procedures address users' concerns.
Another concern is the publication of property photographs or details without the owner's permission. Such advertisements can lead to unnecessary calls to property owners, while prospective tenants may lose money by contacting the wrong person.
Sharif Khandaker, a property owner in the Jigatola area, said an advertisement for his property remained online after it had been rented out.
“I posted an advertisement for my property on a website to rent it out. Even after the property was rented, people continued calling because the advertisement remained online. Someone also used photographs of an acquaintance's house to post an advertisement.”
He added: “There should be a system to verify the owner's identity when an advertisement is published and to remove the post once the property has been rented. Incorrect advertisements create problems not only for tenants but also for property owners.”
Several websites and mobile applications in Bangladesh publish rental advertisements for houses, apartments, rooms, sublets, hostels, offices, shops and other properties. Their services and policies vary, particularly regarding advertiser verification, listing updates, complaint procedures and refunds.
Some services also offer demand-based property searches, attempting to find accommodation according to users' budgets, preferred locations, property types and other requirements. These services may charge separate fees for finding suitable properties, with refund conditions depending on the service provided.
One rental website's published demand-search policy lists fees of Tk1,500 for rooms, beds and hostels; Tk3,000 for houses, apartments and offices; and Tk5,000 for shops and land.
According to the policy, if the company fails to provide a suitable property or an effective solution within 8 days, 80% of the service fee will be refunded after deducting 20%, subject to the applicable conditions. The policy applies specifically to its demand-search service.
The same website's disclaimer states that property owners or advertisers supply information about rent, size, rooms, addresses, photographs and contact numbers. The company says it does not physically inspect every property and cannot confirm every detail in each advertisement. The disclaimer also acknowledges that owners may take time to update listings after renting out their properties.
The website's “About Us” page describes its listings and contact information as verified. However, publicly available information does not clearly establish whether verification covers only telephone numbers and advertiser identities or also confirms a property's existence and current availability.
Other rental websites outline different procedures for collecting and verifying property information. One website's published disclaimer states that its agents collect information with owners' permission and verify details before publishing advertisements. However, outdated listings may remain online if owners fail to update their information after renting out their properties.
Under that website's published refund policy, users can apply for credit refunds if a property has already been rented out, an advertiser cannot be reached despite repeated attempts, or an advertised location does not match the actual location.
Applications must be submitted within 72 hours of unlocking an advertisement. The policy excludes advertisements more than 3 months old. It also states that credits cannot be refunded as cash and that approved credits are returned to users' accounts.
Other property websites publish advertisements for houses and apartments for rent and sale. Their terms may address listing accuracy, continued availability and refunds for paid advertising packages. Some place responsibility for maintaining accurate and updated property information on advertisers, while payments for certain promotional features are described as non-refundable unless otherwise specified.
Rental platforms also advertise different types of accommodation, including sublets, hostels, offices and shops. However, publicly available information about their verification procedures, the time taken to remove outdated listings and the resolution of complaints is insufficient to establish how consistently these practices are followed across the sector.
Differences in policies can make it difficult for prospective tenants to understand what level of verification they can expect before paying to access contact information or other services. The term “verified” may refer to an advertiser's identity, a telephone number or details about a property. Platforms can help users make informed decisions by clearly explaining what they check and what they do not.
The lack of comprehensive public data also makes it difficult to assess the scale of the problem. Information on the number of complaints received, outdated advertisements removed, refunds approved and complaints resolved would help users evaluate the reliability of online rental services.
Trust in digital advertising platforms depends on the accuracy, currency and verifiability of their information. When renting a home, incorrect information can affect users' time, money and safety.
Shahnaz Sultana, deputy director of the complaints sub-division at the Directorate of National Consumer Rights Protection (DNCRP), said verifying advertisers' identities, promptly removing outdated listings and maintaining transparent complaint resolution systems were primarily the responsibility of platforms.
“If users have to pay to access contact information, the platforms must clearly explain the nature of the service and the available remedies in cases involving incorrect information,” she said.
She added that regularly publishing information about the number of complaints received, advertisements removed and complaints resolved would help users assess the reliability of online rental services.
In September 2026, DNCRP Director General Md Zahirul Islam said at a workshop that the Consumer Rights Protection Act, 2009, did not explicitly include digital commerce. He also said a proposal to amend the law to address fraud involving online transactions had been sent to the Ministry of Commerce.
On September 30, 2026, the ministry published a draft amendment to the Consumer Rights Protection Act, 2009, proposing changes that included digital commerce. The draft was made available for public feedback for 30 days.
The director general's remarks reflected the directorate's broader position on digital commerce, but he did not specifically explain how the law would apply to online rental advertisements.
Users who encounter false or misleading online advertisements can contact the DNCRP for guidance on filing a complaint. The directorate's official website lists dncrp.com as its online complaint portal and 16121 as its hotline.
Keeping screenshots of advertisements, contact information, proof of payments or credit deductions, and conversations with the platform can help users provide supporting evidence when filing complaints. These records may help establish what information was advertised, what the user paid for and how the platform responded after a problem was reported.

item.title: Gas shortage halts Jamuna Fertilizer Factory again
item.description:
Production at the state-owned Jamuna Fertilizer Company Limited (JFCL) in Sarishabari, Jamalpur, was suspended again on Sunday due to a gas supply shortage, just two days after operations resumed following repairs to a boiler leak.
The shutdown occurred around 5am after Titas Gas Transmission and Distribution Company Limited and Petrobangla stopped supplying gas to the factory.
The plant resumed production at around 10am on Friday after remaining closed for 15 days to repair the boiler leak. However, officials had warned that inadequate gas pressure could force another shutdown.
The factory has faced repeated disruptions over the past two and a half years due to gas shortages and mechanical problems.
JFCL Additional Chief Engineer (Chemical) Md Fazlul Haque said the factory requires 42-43 million cubic feet of gas daily to maintain uninterrupted urea production.
He said production could resume once gas supply was restored, provided the required pressure was maintained.
The factory has a daily urea production capacity of around 1,700 tonnes and can produce 1,400-1,500 tonnes under favourable operating conditions.
Its urea supplies serve 19 districts, including Jamalpur, Sherpur and Tangail. Prolonged shutdowns could disrupt fertiliser supplies, particularly during the upcoming Boro rice cultivation season, increasing dependence on imports and putting farmers under pressure.

item.title: Tongi madrasa abuse case: Accused teacher visits child’s home with sweets, caught on CCTV
item.description:
The accused teacher, Moslem Ahmed (30), visited the home of the 7-year-old child in Tongi, Gazipur, with a packet of sweets the day after he was accused of sexually abusing the child. The incident was captured on CCTV cameras in the building.
The visit came in the middle of a case that had already drawn nationwide attention.
The footage shows Moslem Ahmed, wearing a panjabi and carrying a red bag containing a packet of sweets, entering the ground floor of the building at 12:38pm on October 20, the day after the incident. After speaking with the security guards, he heads towards the lift and is seen getting into it at 12:39pm. A short while later, he takes the lift upstairs. However, the door of the flat he intended to visit is not opened.
After about 10 minutes, he comes downstairs and leaves the building. He has the bag with him throughout. Another footage shows a packet of sweets inside the bag.
Speaking to the child’s family revealed that, after failing to meet them, the accused teacher sent a message to the child’s mother’s WhatsApp number at 12:45pm on October 20. The message read: “Sister, I am standing in front of your door. I have come to meet you briefly.”
The child’s father was not at home at the time. Moslem eventually returned to the madrasa without meeting any member of the family.
It was not possible to obtain his statement on why he went to meet the child’s family with sweets the day after the incident.
Meanwhile, the child’s family has alleged that they have been receiving threats in various ways since the incident. As the mobile phone numbers of family members have been circulated, people are contacting them from different numbers. The child’s father also claimed that they are being pressured to withdraw the complaint and remove videos posted on social media.
The child’s father said: “My mobile number and those of my family members have been circulated everywhere. Taking advantage of this, people are threatening us over the phone in various ways. They are telling us to withdraw the complaint and remove the videos that have been uploaded. We are living in constant fear.”
He added: “I want to make it clear that my protest is not against the community of Islamic scholars. My protest is against those who wear religious attire but do not uphold its values.”
The father alleged that he had approached law enforcement agencies seeking justice for what had happened to his child. However, he said that, because he had sought justice, he and his family were now facing pressure instead.
Police have said they found preliminary evidence supporting the allegation that the child was sexually abused. On Saturday, Arifur Rahman, officer-in-charge (OC) of Tongi West police station, said: “We visited the scene and collected various pieces of evidence. These preliminarily confirmed the incident (that the child had been abused). The investigation is still ongoing.”
Asked about the family’s allegation that they had received threats, the OC said: “Both parties have verbally complained to the police station that they are being threatened. However, no written complaint regarding the threats has been received so far. Action will be taken if a complaint is filed.”

item.title: Sajek blockade enters fifth day
item.description:
An indefinite road blockade in Sajek, Rangamati’s Baghaichhari upazila, entered its fifth day on Monday, disrupting tourism and bringing tourism-dependent businesses to a standstill.
The popular Sajek Valley remains closed to tourists as authorities seek to resolve the crisis through talks with local leaders.
A meeting between a three-member committee and local headmen and karbaris began at the Baghaichhari Upazila Parishad at 11am.
The blockade was jointly organised by the Sajek Public Rights Protection Committee and the Sajek Karbari Association to press five demands, including the withdrawal of armed members of the Parbatya Chattagram Jana Samhati Samiti (JSS), led by Santu Larma, from Sajek and ensuring the security of local residents.
The protesters have also demanded punishment for those involved in attacks on demonstrators, withdrawal of cases, compensation for traders affected by vandalism and looting at Ujho Bazar, and coverage of medical expenses for injured people.
Their other demands include the withdrawal of army and police personnel from Ujho Bazar, an end to violence, extortion and harassment in Sajek, and a halt to arrests, harassment and searches of protesters’ homes and businesses.
On Sunday, an emergency meeting at the Rangamati deputy commissioner’s office decided to form a three-member committee to negotiate with the protesters. Monday’s meeting in Baghaichhari followed that decision.
The suspension of tourist visits has raised concerns over financial losses for resorts, cottages, transport operators and other tourism-related businesses.
The Rangamati district administration announced on October 22 that tourist visits to Sajek would remain suspended until further notice.
Although no protesters were seen at several points along the roads, law enforcement personnel were patrolling key locations.
Rangamati Superintendent of Police Muhammad Abdur Rakib said the situation was under control and that efforts were underway to resolve the crisis through discussions.
No final decision on the protesters’ demands or the withdrawal of the blockade had been announced by on Monday afternoon.

item.title: Milon: Religious education key to building moral generation
item.description:
Education and Primary and Mass Education Minister Dr ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon on Monday said there is no alternative to religious education in building an enlightened generation with moral and human values and eliminating moral degradation from society.
“Teachers, religious education must play the most important role in preventing moral degradation in the present social system.
Students who memorise the Holy Quran remain away from wrongdoing by keeping the Quran in their hearts. Incorporating religious values into education is essential to building the Bangladesh of tomorrow”, he said.
The minister made the remarks while addressing the third session of the “14th Hifzul Quran Award and Quran Festival 2026”, organised by Tanzimul Ummah Foundation at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Centre in the capital.
The minister said a strong foundation in religious education, starting from village maktabs alongside general education, could help prevent young people from going astray. Modern science and technology must be integrated with religious and moral values in the education system, he said. He said the government had already taken initiatives to introduce a time-befitting education system by narrowing the gap between madrasa and general education.
The disparity between the two streams is gradually decreasing through the inclusion of science, arts, commerce and technical education in madrasas alongside religious studies, he said.
He noted that the modernisation of this education system had begun during the tenure of Shaheed President Ziaur Rahman.
The education minister also said the government had taken a firm stance against irregularities in some institutions in the name of receiving Monthly Pay Order (MPO) facilities and against substandard teaching.
He added that the government is committed to addressing the shortage of Islamic studies teachers and ensuring the recruitment of qualified teachers.
Former principal of Tamirul Millat Kamil Madrasa and Secretary of Tamirul Millat Trust Maulana Zainul Abedin presided over the programme, while Principal of Tanzimul Ummah Alim Madrasa Maulana Abdullah Al Mamun delivered the welcome address.
Former Religious Affairs Adviser Dr A F M Khalid Hossain, lawmakers Barrister Najibur Rahman Momen, Hafez Rashedul Islam and Sayed Uddin Ahmad Hanzala, along with prominent Islamic scholars and thinkers, attended the event as special guests.
At the day-long programme, 1,759 meritorious students who had memorised the Holy Quran from different branches run by Tanzimul Ummah Foundation were awarded crests, certificates, turbans or scarves and awards.
Their proud parents were also given special recognition in appreciation of raising their children as Hafiz-e-Quran.

item.title: Dengue: Five more die, 1,546 hospitalized in 24hrs
item.description:
Five more people died of dengue and 1,546 new patients were hospitalized across the country in the 24 hours ending at 8:00am on Monday.
With the latest fatalities, the dengue death toll in the country has risen to 389 this year, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
Among the new deaths, one each was reported in Dhaka, Chittagong, Khulna, Rajshahi and Barisal divisions.
Since January 1 this year, a total of 126,166 dengue patients have been admitted to hospitals across the country. Of them, 119,393 have recovered.

item.title: Police HQ clarify IGP’s crossfire remark, deny reference to extrajudicial killings
item.description:
The Police Headquarters has clarified Inspector General of Police (IGP) Md Ali Hossain Fakir’s remarks on “crossfire”, saying he used the term literally to describe strict law enforcement, not to suggest extrajudicial killings or punishment outside the judicial process.
In a clarification issued on Monday, police headquarters said it had taken note of media reports and headlines about the IGP’s comments at the inauguration of Community Bank’s Islamic banking branch in Chawkbazar, Dhaka, earlier in the day.
The clarification was issued to address public confusion, it said.
According to the statement, the IGP reaffirmed the police force’s commitment to taking effective action against drug dealers, criminals, extortionists and others who threaten public safety.
Bangladesh Police, the country’s principal law enforcement agency, is responsible for preventing crime, arresting offenders, maintaining public order and protecting people’s lives and property, the statement said.
It added that police personnel sometimes face direct resistance and attacks from criminals, organised groups and individuals who defy the law while carrying out their duties.
Police headquarters said 176 attacks on police personnel had been reported in the first 10 months of this year while they were maintaining law and order, arresting criminals, preventing illegal activities and performing official duties. Four police personnel were killed and 370 seriously injured in these attacks.
The clarification also cited the Penal Code, 1860, the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 and the Police Act, 1861 as laws that recognise police officers’ right to self-defence.
Police Headquarters also addressed confusion over the IGP’s comments about journalists at the same event, saying he had not intended to make sweeping remarks about them and that the comments were made inadvertently.
At the event, the IGP said: “If we beat people with batons, you will call us fascist police. If we remain silent, you will call us weak police. So, I must be given an environment to work in. We must be empowered.”
He also said police could resort to “crossfire” if the government authorised it.
Following the remarks, the Human Rights Support Society (HRSS) expressed concern and condemned the statement. The organisation called on the government to clarify the IGP’s comments and state its position on extrajudicial killings.
Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB) also condemned the remarks, demanding their withdrawal and accountability for the IGP. It also called for accountability over statements that contradict the government’s declared position against extrajudicial killings.
In its clarification, police headquarters said Bangladesh Police remained committed to protecting people’s lives and property and upholding the rule of law while performing its duties professionally and impartially, with respect for human rights.

item.title: TIB condemns IGP’s crossfire remarks, demands accountability
item.description:
Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB) has condemned remarks by the inspector general of police (IGP) that police would resort to crossfire, if necessary, to maintain law and order with government approval, calling them a dangerous message that could legitimize extrajudicial killings.
The organization said the remarks presented extrajudicial killings as an acceptable means of crime control instead of addressing failures in maintaining law and order and institutional weaknesses. Describing the statements as showing utter disregard for the Constitution and the rule of law, TIB demanded their immediate withdrawal and accountability for the police chief's declaration, which it said contradicted the government's stated position against extrajudicial killings.
TIB Executive Director Iftekharuzzaman said: “Is the police chief seeking to use the discredited practice of crossfire as a shield for the police’s failure to maintain law and order? Does seeking to legitimize extrajudicial killings by making them conditional on government approval amount to an admission of failure to combat crime through lawful means?
“The responsibility of the police is to conduct professional investigations, identify offenders and bring the accused to trial on the basis of admissible evidence. Presenting crossfire as an alternative cannot resolve institutional weaknesses; rather, it is an example of professional bankruptcy.
“In the same remarks, the IGP spoke of discharging duties in accordance with the law and the Constitution, while also saying that the police would resort to crossfire if the government approved it. These 2 positions are contradictory. No government approval can legitimize an extrajudicial killing.
“The rights to legal protection and to life and personal liberty guaranteed under Articles 31 and 32 of the Constitution cannot be set aside by executive decisions. Regardless of the seriousness of an allegation, the police have no authority to kill anyone by bypassing due process.”
Recalling past cases involving law enforcement agencies, Iftekharuzzaman said: “The conviction of police officers in the Sinha murder case, along with allegations reported in connection with the verdict that crossfire was used to extort money, torture people and kill them, serves as a reminder of the horrific nature of this practice.
“The killing of Teknaf municipal councillor Ekramul Haque in a purported gunfight also raised serious questions, particularly following the release of an audio recording by his family and allegations of murder.
“The convictions of former Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) officials in the Narayanganj seven-murder case provide another judicially established example of the criminal abuse of power by law enforcement agencies.
“Despite thousands of such experiences, and amid public expectations for police reform and broader state reform, the police chief is once again raising the prospect of crossfire. He must answer the question of what lessons the police have learned from past crimes.”
Iftekharuzzaman further said: “Such reckless and ill-considered remarks by the police chief could be perceived as an implicit license for unlawful use of force at the field level. When the person responsible for ensuring that the force operates within the law presents crossfire as an alternative, questions about his sense of responsibility and suitability for leadership inevitably arise.
“How can the public trust that, under his leadership, citizens’ lives and legal protections will be safeguarded?
“On the other hand, on September 14, the Law Minister stated that the government would not resort to crossfire to combat terrorism and that existing laws were sufficient to tackle terrorism. Why, then, is the police chief raising the prospect of crossfire subject to government approval?
“The government must clearly explain this inconsistency and specify how accountability will be ensured for implementing its declared position.”
TIB said any use of force by police must be lawful, necessary and proportionate. Under international standards, the intentional lethal use of firearms is permissible only when strictly unavoidable to protect life. The organization said there was no scope to portray this narrowly defined exception as authorization for extrajudicial killings.
Regarding allegations that journalists criticize the police because they have not received money, TIB said that any specific allegations of criminal conduct against a journalist must be addressed through lawful action based on evidence.
Sweeping allegations, the organization said, undermine the role of a free media in oversight and accountability and risk discouraging independent journalism. The need to ensure a conducive working environment and adequate capacity for the police cannot be used to justify evading legitimate criticism.
TIB called on the government to obtain a formal explanation of the IGP’s remarks, ensure their withdrawal along with an unconditional public apology, and hold the police chief administratively accountable. It also called for his removal from office until accountability is ensured.

item.title: Sakhawat: Govt plans major expansion of cancer care, radiotherapy facilities
item.description:
Health and Family Welfare Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Husain on Monday said the government has taken steps to expand cancer treatment facilities across the country, with procurement of new radiotherapy and robotic surgery equipment underway.
“We are working fast to establish eight cancer institutes in the eight divisions and expand radiotherapy services at district level to ensure cancer treatment at the grassroots,” he said.
The minister made the remarks while speaking as the chief guest at the inaugural ceremony of the Medical Physics Program at Brac University in the city’s Merul Badda, Dhaka.
The Mathematics and Physical Sciences Department of Brac University introduced the two-year master's program for the first time in Bangladesh to meet the country’s growing demand for medical physicists.
About the government's commitment to ensure treatment for cancer, Sakhawat said the government has planned to procure 17 linear accelerators to make cancer treatment available across the country.
“We are also going to bring five major robotic surgery machines for the first time,” he said, emphasizing early detection and public awareness as critical components of the government’s cancer-control strategy, particularly for breast and cervical cancers.
He said the government would intensify HPV vaccination campaigns and promote breast cancer self-screening and awareness among women.
“Without awareness, we cannot save people from cancer,” Sakhawat said, urging health professionals and educational institutions to help spread awareness at the grassroots level.
Coming down heavily on the previous ‘fascist regime’, he said the ‘previous fascist government’ had destroyed the country’s health sector, which had been marred by corruption and plundering.
However, after assuming office, the present government has taken robust steps for the development of the country’s health sector, he said, adding that once the projects are implemented, the country would witness a revolutionary change in the health sector within the next two years.
“Under the leadership of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, we are taking the healthcare services to village level,” the minister said, adding that the government planned to establish Family Wellbeing Centers in every three wards of each union and transform existing community clinics into Health Wellbeing Centers.
“These centers will provide primary-level services, including blood analysis and breast cancer screening,” he said.
Noting that every upazila hospital is going to be transformed into a 150-bed facility, the minister said the government will strengthen dialysis, physiotherapy, and maternal and newborn care at upazila-level hospitals to reduce pressure on tertiary healthcare facilities.
Stating that the government is going to appoint 5,000 doctors soon, Sakhawat said the government is also working to increase the number of hospital beds and recruit around 41,390 health workers, including 25,000 midwives, to strengthen healthcare delivery.
About the newly introduced program at Brac University, he assured government cooperation in developing medical physics education and manpower, saying the government would recruit medical physicists according to the needs of the expanding cancer treatment facilities.
“Medical physics is a very important part of treatment. You do your best and improve yourselves. From the government side, we must extend our hand of cooperation to you,” the minister said.
He said medical physicists play a crucial role in radiotherapy, as the accuracy of radiation dosage is vital for ensuring patient safety and the effectiveness of treatment.
“If the dose is wrong, the patient is gone. If the dose is wrong, the doctor’s credibility is gone,” he said, stressing the need to create adequate numbers of trained medical physicists.
He urged Brac University students, teachers and researchers to contribute to strengthening medical physics and cancer care in Bangladesh.
Professor Emeritus at Dhaka University Dr AFM Yusuf Haider, Additional Director General of the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) Professor Dr Jalal Uddin Mohammad Rumi, Bangladesh Medical University (BMU) Clinical Oncology Department Chairman Professor Dr Syed Md Akram Hussain, National Institute of Cancer Research and Hospital (NICRH) Director Professor Dr Mostafa Aziz Sumon and Project Director of Establishment of the Integrated Cancer, Kidney and Heart Treatment Centers across Bangladesh's Eight Divisional Cities Dr Md Toufiq Hasan Firoz spoke as special guests at the event.
Brac University Vice-Chancellor Professor Syed Ferhat Anwar chaired the program, while Mathematics and Physical Sciences (MPS) Department Chairperson Professor Hasibun Naher and Registrar and Controller of Examinations of the university Dr David Dowland delivered the welcome address.
Former Director and Chief Medical Physicist at Gummersbach University Hospital, University of Cologne in Germany, and Adviser and Coordinator of MPS at BRAC University, Professor Dr Golam Abu Zakaria presented the keynote paper, while Medical Physics Program Coordinator Professor Hasin Anupama Azhari presented an overview of the newly introduced program.

item.title: Fire breaks out at scrap fabric warehouse in Gazipur
item.description:
A fire broke out again at a scrap fabric warehouse in Konabari in Gazipur City Corporation on Monday evening.
Four units of the Fire Service and Civil Defence are working to bring the blaze under control.
Ayub Ali, station officer of the Konabari Modern Fire Service, said they received the report of the fire at 5:55pm.
Two units from the Konabari Modern Fire Service station joined the firefighting operation after receiving the report. Two more units from the Sarabo Modern Fire Service station later joined them, he said.

item.title: Woman who said she 'suffered after voting for BNP' sent to jail
item.description:
A court in Mymensingh on Monday sent a woman entrepreneur to jail after denying her bail in a case filed under Section 151 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 following tensions sparked by her Facebook Live videos in Bhaluka.
Sathi Akter, 30, was detained on Sunday night after local BNP leaders and activists surrounded her business establishment, demanding action over remarks she made during the live broadcasts.
Police produced her before the Mymensingh Chief Judicial Magistrate Court on Monday afternoon. Senior Judicial Magistrate Sajedul Islam denied her bail and ordered her to be sent to jail around 3pm.
Mostasinur Rahman, an inspector at the Mymensingh court, confirmed the matter to Dhaka Tribune.
He said Section 151 of the Code of Criminal Procedure allows police to make preventive arrests without a warrant if they suspect someone is planning to commit a cognizable offence.
However, police said they found no anti-government remarks in the videos after reviewing them.
Mohammad Zahidul Islam, officer-in-charge of Bhaluka Model Police Station, said he had reviewed the full videos four times but found no statements against the government or criticism of it.
The OC said several traders at the market approached Sathi after the videos were posted, but she behaved aggressively towards them, creating a tense situation. Police took her into custody to protect her from the agitated crowd before showing her arrested under Section 151 and producing her before the court.
Asked why she was arrested despite police finding no anti-government remarks, Zahidul said Sathi had expressed her personal feelings during the live broadcasts without targeting any individual or the government. He said there was no scope for filing a major case against her on that basis.
Senior lawyer AHM Khalequzzaman, a senior member of the Mymensingh District Bar Association, said Section 151 allows police to arrest someone without a warrant or a magistrate's order to prevent a potential offence.
Sathi, who owns Sathi Beauty Parlour at Khadija Palace Market in the Square Masterbari area of Bhaluka upazila, went live twice from her Facebook account, Sathi Makeover, at around 2pm on Sunday.
In the videos, lasting five minutes and 22 seconds and eight minutes and eight seconds, she expressed anger over a theft at her business establishment. At one point, she was heard saying: “I am now suffering after voting for the BNP government.”
After the videos spread online, local BNP leaders and activists surrounded her business establishment and demanded action, triggering tension in the area. Police took her into custody at around 8:30pm on Sunday.

item.title: Bangladesh to showcase jute products at COP31 in Turkiye
item.description:
The government plans to showcase Bangladesh’s traditional jute and jute-made products at the UN climate conference COP31 in Turkiye to promote them in international markets.
A special exhibition of Bangladeshi jute products is planned at the Bangladesh pavilion during the conference, scheduled to take place in Antalya from November 9 to 20.
The initiative aims to promote jute as an eco-friendly alternative to plastic and highlight the commercial potential of Bangladesh’s jute industry.
Preparations are underway to display a range of jute products and related technologies at the pavilion. An exhibition display has been set up at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs as part of the preparations.
The exhibition will showcase products such as jute bags, home décor items and handicrafts to international buyers, investors and policymakers.
Stakeholders believe growing global awareness of environmental pollution and the need for alternatives to plastic presents an opportunity to expand international markets for jute products.
As a natural, renewable and biodegradable fibre, jute has significant potential in environmentally friendly production and consumption.
At a meeting at the Foreign Ministry on October 15, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam highlighted the potential of Bangladesh’s jute industry during discussions on preparations for COP31 with climate experts and relevant stakeholders. The meeting emphasised promoting jute as an eco-friendly alternative to plastic.
If implemented, the initiative could help showcase the diverse uses of jute, explore new markets and strengthen commercial ties with foreign buyers, while bringing Bangladesh’s traditional “golden fibre” industry into the international spotlight.

item.title: More than 40 killed by armed men in Oromia, Ethiopia
item.description:
More than 40 people were killed in attacks on Orthodox Christian churches and villages in Ethiopia’s central state of Oromia on Saturday, two residents and a priest told AFP on Monday.
Oromia, Ethiopia’s largest state, has faced a long-running insurgency and ethnic tensions, with armed groups using religion to inflame divisions.
“My sister and uncle were killed, and several of my relatives were taken hostage in Chole ward of Shirka district,” one resident told AFP by phone, asking to remain anonymous.
They said 44 people were killed in the region, while another resident put the toll at 51.
Verifying information in Ethiopia is highly challenging due to heavy restrictions on media access.
The state-run Ethiopia Human Rights Commission said only that it was “following the situation.”
“Religious tensions remain very high in the area and could escalate into a wider crisis if left unaddressed,” the first witness said.
The witnesses said two churches in the region had been attacked.
“Several homes belonging to targeted residents were also destroyed,” one witness said.
Ethiopia is a deeply fragmented nation in the Horn of Africa, facing multiple internal conflicts, including heavy fighting that broke out last month in its northern Tigray state.
Oromia, a state of around 40 million people in the center of the country, is home to a mix of Muslim, Protestant and Orthodox communities. While concerns over political and ethnic representation have been the main drivers of its conflict, religion has been used to mobilise fighters.
“We are deeply shocked by these tragic killings and are appealing to the government to intervene and restore security,” said a deacon of one of the attacked churches, who put the death toll at 46.

item.title: UN probe accuses Israel of ‘extermination’ in West Bank
item.description:
Israel has committed the crime against humanity of “extermination” in the West Bank, while continuing to commit “genocide” against Palestinians in the Gaza Strip, United Nations-mandated investigators said Monday.
The UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry said Israeli forces had also committed other crimes against humanity and war crimes in the West Bank, which Israel has occupied since 1967.
The commission, which does not speak for the UN itself, first determined in a September 2025 report that Israel had committed “genocide” in the war in Gaza following Hamas’ October 7, 2023 resistance campaign on Israel - a finding Israel flatly rejects.
In a new report -- which comes the day before Israel’s general election -- the investigation found that in the West Bank, through military operations reinforced by sustained settler violence, Israel has waged a “widespread and systematic attack” against civilians.
“The Israeli authorities and forces have committed the crimes against humanity of extermination, torture, rape and other forms of sexual violence in the West Bank, as well as persecution based on intersecting discriminatory grounds, with nationality, race and ethnicity at its core,” it said.
Israel’s mission in Geneva said the report was part of the inquiry’s “misinformation campaign to demonise the State of Israel and portray its very existence as criminal.”
“The international community must reject these distortions, repudiate the commission’s findings and demand its immediate dissolution,” it said in a statement.
The three-member investigative team was established by the UN Human Rights Council in 2021.
South African former High Court judge Navi Pillay, who chaired the investigation until November 2025, won the Nobel Peace Prize earlier this month.
The commission’s new report focused on killings and bodily and mental harm caused by both Israeli and Palestinian security forces since October 2023.
It found that the situation in the West Bank has deteriorated gravely since the Palestinian fighter group Hamas’s resistance campaign from Gaza that month.
The commission found that the Israeli authorities “intended to collectively punish” West Bank civilians due to the Hamas resistance.
“The targeting of Palestinian civilians across different locations in the West Bank indicates a high level of coordination and organized planning and is the product of state policy,” the report said.
The conduct of Israeli authorities indicates that “they knew and intended settler violence” to be part of the widespread and systematic attack in the West Bank, it added.
“The intentional killing and injuring of Palestinian civilians and destruction of homes in the West Bank combined with Israel’s persistent denial of responsibility form part of a broader strategy to exterminate and displace Palestinians and impose conditions of life that are unliveable,” said commission chairman Srinivasan Muralidhar.
“Attempting to equate Palestinian statehood with a threat to the existence of Israel is blocking any viable attempts to realize Palestinians’ right to self-determination,” the Indian judge said in a statement.
The report cited cases where the commission concluded that Israeli forces intended to seriously harm and kill civilians, in acts which amount to war crimes including wilful killing.
Israel’s military offensive, in response, has displaced nearly the entire population of Gaza and killed more than 74,200 people, according to Gaza’s health ministry, which is under Hamas authority but whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.
“The cases investigated for this report show that the Israeli authorities and forces continue to commit genocidal acts with the genocidal intent to destroy, in whole or in part, the Palestinians in Gaza,” the report said.
The inquiry urged Israel to “end the commission of genocide in Gaza” and act immediately on “obligations to prevent and punish genocide and incitement to genocide.”
Israel should “immediately end the unlawful occupation of Palestinian territory,” and remove all settlers and settlements.
Turning to the Palestinian Authority, the report said that “Palestinian state violence has targeted and continues to target members of opposing Palestinian armed groups and repress Palestinian civil and political opposition.”
The Palestinian Authority struggles with credibility and legitimacy, and “targets Palestinians who voice dissenting civil and political views... resulting in killings,” it said.
“The Palestinian Authority has also failed to conduct prompt, effective and impartial investigations into incidents of killings.”
There was no immediate reaction from the Palestinian Authority.
The commission is due to present its report to the UN General Assembly in New York on Monday.

item.title: The broiler chicken myth that refuses to die
item.description:
Broiler chicken has become a regular part of the diet in most households in the country. Because it is easy to find and relatively cheap, it is popular among ordinary people. However, rumors and widely held beliefs in the market have left many worried about its safety.
According to physician Dr Shahanaz, broiler chicken is not in itself an unhealthy food. Rather, it is an important source of high-quality protein, as well as vitamin B12, vitamin B6 and various minerals essential for the body. Its safety, however, depends on how it is raised on the farm, whether antibiotic-use rules are followed, and whether hygiene is maintained during slaughter and storage.
She said antibiotics are used on many farms to prevent or treat disease. But if they are overused without following prescribed guidelines, or if the required withdrawal period before slaughter is not observed, drug residues can remain in the meat. In the long term, this may increase the risk of antimicrobial resistance, meaning the spread of antibiotic-resistant germs.
Another widespread belief about broiler chicken is that hormones are used to make it grow faster. But there is no strong scientific evidence to support this claim. Broilers grow quickly today because of improved breed selection, balanced feed and modern farm management.
She added that if proper hygiene is not followed on the farm, or if there is carelessness during slaughter, transport, and storage, harmful bacteria such as Salmonella and Campylobacter may be present in the meat. This is why chicken must always be thoroughly boiled or cooked before eating.
Experts say properly produced broiler chicken is an excellent source of lean protein. It also contains important nutrients such as vitamin B12, vitamin B6, niacin (vitamin B3), phosphorus, selenium and zinc, which play key roles in the body's normal functioning.
Eating skinless broiler chicken regularly in moderate amounts can be part of a healthy diet. Both local (deshi) chicken and broiler chicken provide good-quality protein. Although deshi chicken differs in taste and texture, there is no major difference in nutritional value. What matters more, she said, is the quality of the chicken, safe production, and hygienic cooking.
Health experts have offered several tips for eating broiler chicken safely. They say chicken should be bought from trusted shops or approved farms. Meat with a foul smell or unusual color should be avoided. Raw and cooked meat should be stored separately, and the meat should be cooked thoroughly before it is eaten.
In the experts' view, broiler chicken that is produced according to proper rules, stored safely, and cooked well is a safe and nutritious food for ordinary people. Rather than being misled by misconceptions or rumors, buying chicken consciously from trusted sources and following hygiene rules is the safest and most sensible choice.

item.title: e-TIN holders may face Tk5,000 fine for unfiled returns
item.description:
Simply having an e-TIN registration does not mean everyone will face a Tk5,000 fine for failing to submit their income tax return.
According to the Income Tax Act, 2023, penalties are provisioned for failing to submit returns under specific conditions.
However, the amount of the fine depends on whether the taxpayer’s income was previously assessed and which provisions of the law apply to their case.
Recently, information circulated on social media suggesting that failing to submit an income tax return despite having an e-TIN could result in a Tk5,000 fine, causing concern among many.
However, according to the law, for individual taxpayers whose income has never been assessed before, the maximum fine under specified conditions is Tk5,000.
On the other hand, if income has been assessed previously, the calculation for the penalty may differ.
According to data from the National Board of Revenue (NBR), Section 266 of the Income Tax Act, 2023 provides for penalties for failing to submit income tax returns within the stipulated time.
However, this penalty is not automatically imposed on everyone; the respective Deputy Commissioner of Taxes can impose the fine in accordance with the law.
How much is the fine for not submitting a return?
According to Section 266(1) of the Income Tax Act, 2023, if someone fails to submit a return under Section 166, 172, 191, 193, or 212 without a reasonable cause, the respective Deputy Commissioner of Taxes may impose a penalty.
Under the provisions of the law, the fine can be set at 10% of the tax assessed on the latest determined income. In this case, the minimum fine is Tk1,000. If the failure continues, an additional daily penalty of Tk50 is also provisioned.
However, the law sets a maximum limit for the penalty:
This means that for individual taxpayers whose income has never been assessed before, Tk5,000 is the maximum penalty ceiling. This is not a predetermined or automatic fine for everyone. The conditions of the law and the taxpayer's situation are taken into consideration when imposing a fine.
Mandatory return submission just because you have an e-TIN?
The obligation to submit an income tax return is determined based on the Income Tax Act and related provisions. Not everyone is exempt from the obligation to submit returns simply because their income falls below the tax-free limit.

Therefore, making a final decision based solely on whether you have an e-TIN or whether your current income is taxable is not advisable.
When is the deadline for submitting income tax returns?
According to general guidelines published by the National Board of Revenue, the standard tax day for natural individual taxpayers is November 30. Returns must be submitted within this period.
However, if the NBR extends the deadline for a specific tax year, that extended deadline applies.
In the past tax year (2025–2026), although the normal deadline was November 30, it was gradually extended, eventually allowing taxpayers to submit returns without penalties up to March 31, 2026.
Failing to submit a return on time should not be neglected.
The applicable tax, additional charges, or penalty for late return submission must be verified.
Calculations may vary depending on the taxpayer's situation and applicable legal provisions.
Income is non-taxable—what should you do?
Many people register for an e-TIN for banking, taking out loans, property registration, or other purposes.
Later, their income might decrease, or they may no longer need those services.
In such situations, it is essential to check whether there is an obligation to submit a return.
You cannot assume that the obligation to submit a return has ended simply because your income has dropped below the tax-free limit or you currently do not owe tax.
If applicable conditions are met, you can apply to the relevant tax authority to cancel your TIN.
However, cancellation depends on the authority's verification and decision.
Canceling a TIN and the obligation to submit a return are two different matters.

Precautions before submitting online returns
When submitting a return, it is crucial to select the correct tax year and accurately provide information on income, investments, assets, and liabilities.
At the same time, details regarding applicable taxes, advance taxes, and tax deducted at source (TDS) must be verified.
Keep acknowledgment receipts or related records after submitting your return. Do not share your NID, TIN, password, or financial information with strangers or on unauthorized websites.
The NBR has issued directives regarding online return submission for natural individual taxpayers in the 2026–27 tax year.
However, approved alternative methods may apply to specific categories of taxpayers and under special circumstances.
If you have an e-TIN but have not submitted your income tax return, you should first check your tax-related status.
There is no need to panic over the Tk5,000 fine information circulated on social media, because under Section 266 of the Income Tax Act, 2023, determining the penalty amount requires considering the taxpayer's previous income assessment, the nature of failure to submit the return, and the applicable conditions of the law.

item.title: Bangladesh's foreign debt repayments increase in Q1 of FY27
item.description:
Bangladesh's External debt servicing has jumped to $1,351.23 million during the 1st quarter (July-September) period of the current FY27.
According to the latest data of the Economic Relations Division (ERD), Bangladesh paid back more than double the foreign assistance it received in actual disbursements during the first quarter (July-September) of FY27.
According to ERD data, external debt servicing costs soared to $1,351.23 million, while foreign aid disbursements reached $662.31 million.
During this July-September period, Bangladesh spent $1.351 billion on principal and interest payments on foreign loans during July-September of FY27, up 5.6% from $1.279 billion in the same period of the previous fiscal year, says the ERD data.
Of the total debt servicing in the first quarter, principal repayments stood at $858.92 million, up from $816.99 million during the corresponding period of FY26.
Interest payments also increased to $492.31 million from $462.96 million a year earlier.
The development partners disbursed $662.31 million in foreign assistance during the first quarter of FY27, down from $1.148 billion in the corresponding period of the previous fiscal year.
Of the total disbursement in July-September this year, $541.74 million came as loans and $120.57 million as grants.
Foreign commitments, however, showed a significant increase.
Development partners committed $1.273 billion in loans and grants during July-September of FY27, up from $910.67 million in the same period of the previous fiscal year - an increase of about 40%.
Of the new commitments, $1.148 billion was in loans, while $125.45 million came in grants.

item.title: Invest Bangladesh urges Unctad to highlight FDI successes in emerging economies
item.description:
Invest Bangladesh executive chairman Ashik Chowdhury has called upon the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (Unctad) to globally showcase successful examples of foreign direct investment (FDI) in emerging economies like Bangladesh.
Speaking at a ministerial roundtable discussion during the World Investment Forum in Doha, Ashik Chowdhury suggested that Unctad consider mechanisms to share investment risks, drawing on models utilized by the Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (Miga) and export credit agencies.
Highlighting the stark global disparity in capital flows, Unctad data reveals that over 80% of global FDI in 2025 went to just 20 economies.
Furthermore, between 2020 and 2025, low- and lower-middle-income countries secured less than 10% of greenfield investments in strategic growth sectors such as AI infrastructure, semiconductors, and clean energy.
Despite these global headwinds, the World Investment Report 2026 recognized Bangladesh as a leading recipient of greenfield investments among Least Developed Countries (LDCs) in Asia.
Ashik Chowdhury emphasized that investment impact should not be evaluated solely by dollar amounts, but also by job creation and production capacity.
"A $100 million investment in Bangladesh that creates 50,000 jobs can have a far greater developmental impact than a $1 billion project elsewhere," he noted.
In a separate session at the forum, Invest Bangladesh presented investment prospects in key sectors—including infrastructure and manufacturing—to an audience of nearly 100 institutional investors, international financiers, and representatives from global investment promotion agencies.
Nahian Rahman Rochi, executive member for Investment Promotion at Invest Bangladesh, delivered a presentation highlighting the country's vibrant young workforce and growing domestic market.
He outlined opportunities in solar energy, LNG infrastructure, proposed free trade zones, high-tech textiles, electronics, and medical equipment.
"Investors asked how they could participate in the projects we presented," said Rochi.
"Partners showed keen interest in opportunities within economic zones, ports, and dry docks. These investments can fulfill Bangladesh's rising domestic demand while boosting regional trade. We will continue discussions with interested parties to define how they can participate and how we can support them."
Alongside the main sessions, the Invest Bangladesh delegation held bilateral meetings with potential investors to advance project-specific discussions based on investor interests and project requirements.

item.title: IndustriALL seeks Tk32,000 monthly wage for RMG workers
item.description:
The IndustriALL Bangladesh Council has demanded a minimum monthly wage of $260 (Tk32,085 if US$1 is Tk123.41) for the readymade garment (RMG) workers, citing rising living costs.
The council, known as IBC, finalized the demand at an emergency meeting of its central executive committee on Saturday, it said in a press release.
IBC president Mir Abul Kalam Azad presided over the meeting with the present of other leaders.
IBC general secretary Salauddin Swapan said that the meeting discussed the soaring prices of essentials, rise in fuel oil prices and hike of the workers’ transport costs.
Moreover, medical and other living expenses had also increased, making it hard for workers to get by on current wages, he said.
The release added that the 100% to 142% pay rise for government employees had further destabilized the market, deepening the hardship of garment workers and other low-income people.
Taking these factors into account, the committee demanded the $260 minimum wage for garment workers.
IBC said it would soon finalize wage figures for the other grades.
Once a full wage board is formed, it would submit a written proposal to the board’s chairman and the workers’ representative.
The demand comes as the government moves to form a wage board for the sector amid renewed labour protests demanding a monthly minimum wage of Tk30,000.
The Department of Labour, under the Ministry of Labour and Employment, has asked garment manufacturers’ and workers’ organizations to nominate representatives for the proposed board.
The department sent separate letters to the Bangladesh Employers’ Federation and Jatiyatabadi Sramik Dal, asking each to nominate three representatives.
The minimum monthly wage for garment workers has risen in successive reviews, from Tk1,662.50 in 2006 to Tk3,000 in 2010, Tk5,300 in 2013, Tk8,000 in 2018, and Tk12,500 in 2023.

item.title: Beko reaffirms commitment to growth in Bangladesh
item.description:

The delegation included Polat Şen, president of the Consumer Durables Group at Koç Holding; Zafer Üstüner, chief commercial officer for Asia, Russia & South Africa at Beko and CEO of Arçelik Hitachi and Nihat Bayız, chief production & technology Officer at Beko.
Hosted by MHM Fairoz, managing director and CEO of Singer Bangladesh, a subsidiary of Beko, the visit highlighted Bangladesh’s importance within the group’s global operations.
Singer Bangladesh continues its transformation across manufacturing, retail and employee experience. Key milestones include the opening of a new manufacturing plant and concept stores, alongside the relocation of its headquarters to a facility aligned with Beko’s global workplace standards.
These developments reflect the company’s vision of bringing Koç Group and Beko’s expertise to Bangladesh to strengthen manufacturing capabilities and enhance both consumer and employee experience.
Continued investment builds on this foundation, enabling Singer Bangladesh to develop its capabilities and respond to the evolving needs of Bangladeshi households.
Koç Group’s presence also contributes to the longstanding economic ties between Türkiye and Bangladesh.

item.title: DRU gives IGP 24 hours to withdraw remarks, apologise
item.description:
Dhaka Reporters’ Unity (DRU) on Monday expressed deep concern and strong protest over the "objectionable" remarks made by Inspector General of Police (IGP) Md. Ali Hossain Fakir regarding journalists, issuing a 24-hour ultimatum for him to withdraw his statement and offer a public apology.
DRU President Abu Saleh Akon and General Secretary Mainul Hasan Sohel warned in a joint statement that the organisation would announce tough protest programmes if the police chief failed to apologise within 24 hours.
Speaking at an event in Old Dhaka's Chawkbazar earlier on Monday, IGP Ali Hossain Fakir alleged that journalists write reports declaring the police ineffective when they do not receive drug money.
Rejecting the statement, the DRU leaders called such generalized comments contrary to independent journalism and unacceptable coming from a top law enforcement official.
They stressed that if any police officer has specific allegations against a journalist, it should be resolved through legal channels with concrete evidence, rather than making broad negative statements that undermine the dignity of the profession and public trust in the media.

Trump blasts Norway over Nobel Peace Prize snub
item.description:
US President Donald Trump attacked Norway during a campaign rally, calling it a “shithouse country,” and said that Norwegian immigrants were not welcome in the United States because its Nobel Committee had not awarded him the Peace Prize.
“Frankly, Norway sucks. Norway has become a shithouse country, actually,” he said during Sunday’s speech.
Since returning to the White House in January 2025, Trump has made no secret of his desire to win the prestigious Nobel Peace prize.
Judge and former UN rights chief Navi Pillay of South Africa was this year’s recipient.
Trump has called the committee’s choice “a disgraceful and embarrassing decision” and argued that the award should have gone to him.
Trump said Sunday he would welcome immigrants from certain countries but not Norway “because I didn’t get the Nobel Prize.”
“So I don’t want anybody from Norway,” he said during the rally in the Michigan town of Port Huron ahead of crucial US midterm elections on November 3.
There was no official indication of a new US policy on Norwegian immigrants.
Norwegian Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide responded to Trump’s comments about the Nobel prize on Monday, maintaining that the committee is independent.
“He knows very well that the Nobel Committee is independent. We have reminded him of that, in case anyone is wondering - and that is still the case,” he told national broadcaster NRK.
Trump came under fire in 2018, during his first term, after using similar vulgar expressions to refer to Haiti and certain African countries.

item.title: France’s Macron to visit Marseille after protest violence
item.description:
The French government sought to draw a line Monday under weeks of protests that have been marred by violence, with President Emmanuel Macron headed to Marseille and the prime minister to meet with students demanding better school conditions.
France has been rocked by widespread anger over the rising cost of living, with nationwide demonstrations on October 17 degenerating into some of the country’s worst rioting in years.
The demonstrations have come at a critical moment for France, six months ahead of a presidential election to replace centrist Macron.
The frontrunner -- far-right leader Marine le Pen -- held an election rally in Orleans Sunday, a day after yet more demonstrations also saw some violent clashes on the sidelines.
She vowed to “restore the rule of law” if elected next year. Polls show the protests and ensuing disorder have boosted her support, as the government and Macron faced sharp criticism over the unrest.
Authorities have admitted to security and intelligence failures that paved the way for the clashes, large-scale looting and vandalism of public property that erupted on October 17, and had stepped up security for Saturday’s protests.
While Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said the outcome of Saturday’s rallies was more “positive” than a week ago, street violence still erupted in the French capital and a number of other cities including Marseille.
The Elysee said Macron would visit the city hall in Marseille, France’s second-largest city, on Monday, after it was damaged in the protest violence on October 17.
He was also due to meet shopkeepers who had fallen victim to looting and vandalism, the Elysee said.
“He will also pay tribute to and thank the internal security forces that helped restore republican order,” the presidency said.
After this weekend’s protests, many shopfronts in the city center were still boarded up early Monday, just hours before Macron’s arrival.
Macron’s visit was intended to demonstrate that “the state is present, standing firm and fulfilling its mission to protect,” an aide said.
A total of 1,435 people were arrested on the sidelines of the most recent weekend protests, Nunez said on Monday.
“The day was brought under control and there were no serious incidents,” he told broadcaster BFMTV.
“Nevertheless, we saw a very high level of violence directed at the internal security forces,” Nunez added.
He said that 267 police officers and gendarmes were injured, along with 150 protesters, including three who were seriously hurt in Toulouse, Reims and Clermont-Ferrand.
The unrest followed weeks of demonstrations by students campaigning for better learning conditions.
Several teenage protesters have been seriously injured and thousands arrested.
The police response to their demonstrations, which included blockades of schools, has been criticized as heavy-handed and sparked a broader movement against the cost of living and police violence.
In Paris on Monday, Lecornu was to meet student leaders, with National Education Minister Edouard Geffray and Higher Education Minister Philippe Baptiste joining him for the talks. Following that meeting, Geffray and Baptiste will hold a news conference.
Macron already met representatives of secondary school pupils last Friday, but they emerged from the talks urging students to keep protesting until the government put forward concrete proposals to address their demands.
On top of the protests, the country was last week shaken by a shooting that killed one person and wounded five, including a 12-year-old girl, outside Paris.
Macron has branded the shooting a “racist terrorist attack,” as most of the victims were from foreign backgrounds.

item.title: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill five including child
item.description:
Five Palestinians, including a young girl, were killed Monday in Israeli airstrikes across the Gaza Strip, medical sources and first responders said.
Civil defense spokesman Mahmoud Bassal said a total of 13 people had been killed and about 60 wounded by Israeli fire and airstrikes in Gaza in the past 24 hours.
“We transported three martyrs, including a child, following an Israeli airstrike targeting a camp for displaced people in the Al-Mawasi area, west of Khan Yunis,” Bassal told AFP.
Israel’s military told AFP it was “not aware” of any military activity in that area on Monday.
Nasser Hospital in the southern Gaza city of Khan Yunis confirmed the three deaths.
“Their bodies were torn apart by direct hits from shrapnel from the Israeli missile,” the hospital said, adding that several wounded people, including a child and a woman, had also come in for treatment.
The hospital identified the deceased as Hossam al-Zamli, Tamer Abu Sneima, and Jouri al-Soufi, a young girl. The Gaza education ministry gave her age as seven.
Gaza’s civil defense said a fourth person was killed in an airstrike on a tent housing displaced Palestinians near Khan Yunis.
In Gaza City’s Rimal neighborhood, a third airstrike killed one and injured three, according to the city’s Al-Shifa hospital.
A security source in Gaza told AFP that “several tanks and military vehicles, accompanied by a military bulldozer, advanced on Monday morning into the area west of the Yellow Line in the eastern part of Deir al-Balah,” in central Gaza.
After a US-brokered ceasefire took hold in Gaza in October 2025, the so-called Yellow Line was established to divide the areas under Israeli control -- more than 60 percent of the territory -- from those under Hamas control.
The military advance Monday coincided with “heavy gunfire by the occupation forces towards the eastern and northern areas” of Deir al-Balah, home to hundreds of displaced families, the source added.
Since the ceasefire began last year, more than 1,500 people have been killed in Gaza, according to the territory’s health ministry.
Israel responded with a massive military campaign that has destroyed much of Gaza and killed more than 74,500 people, according to the territory’s health ministry, which operates under Hamas and whose figures are considered accurate by the United Nations.

item.title: Houthis attack Saudi Arabia before high-stakes talks in Tehran
item.description:
Yemen’s Houthis have kept up their attacks on Saudi Arabia as senior officials from the kingdom, Turkiye and Pakistan are due to hold high-stakes talks with Iran in Tehran on Monday, following warnings of a return to war.
Fresh explosions rattled Riyadh overnight, along with a text message warning to residents, after the Iran-allied Houthis claimed a new attack on the Saudi capital’s international airport on Sunday.
Saudi Arabia, the world’s top oil exporter, has become deeply embroiled in the eight-month war since hostilities in its long-running conflict with the Iran-allied Houthis resumed in July.
Defense Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman is among the delegations travelling to Tehran, made up of officials from the three countries that signed a defense alliance in Mecca in August.
Their visit follows warnings by the United States, Iran and Israel that hostilities could resume.
Tensions have increased ahead of Israel’s pivotal election on Tuesday and next week’s US mid-terms, where US President Donald Trump’s Republicans are battling to keep control of both chambers of the US Congress.
Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei will take part in Monday’s meeting with Prince Khalid, Pakistani army chief General Asim Munir and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin, the deputy secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, Ali Bagheri Kani, told state TV.
“This historic meeting in Tehran may be the last chance before escalation spirals out of control, an attempt to impose a path of de-escalation before it’s too late,” Hesham Alghannam, a Saudi security analyst and researcher, posted on X.
“The presence of military and security figures at this level together means that the remaining time is extremely limited.”
On Sunday, as blasts rang out over Riyadh and authorities sent texts warning residents of a “hostile aerial threat”, the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said it struck missile launchers and storage facilities in Yemen.
The Houthis said they had attacked Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport once again. The repeatedly targeted facility has been largely closed since 13 people were killed and more than 300 wounded in a major attack this month.
Mediation efforts between the US and Iran have been led by Qatar and Pakistan. A Qatari delegation visited Tehran on Sunday, Iran’s foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said.
“Our region is in the grip of serious tensions, and neighboring countries are striving to convey a message and put forward initiatives,” Baqaei said on Monday.
Andreas Krieg of London-based risk consultancy Mena Analytica said Prince Khalid’s presence in Tehran was “hugely significant”, calling him the “strategic mastermind of Saudi Arabia.”
Prince Khalid, brother of Saudi de facto ruler Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, has emerged as one of Saudi Arabia’s key diplomatic interlocutors, dispatched on sensitive regional missions.
“For him to go to Iran directly in this very sensitive time is a very, very strong signal that the kingdom is not just... sitting and waiting for things, events to unfold,” Krieg told AFP.
“There’s a clear effort by the Mecca alliance to signal to Iran that they’re ready to work together to defend the kingdom and defend the kingdom’s borders,” he added.
“And so should Iran think to escalate, which they will likely do if Israel and the US strikes, and they will most likely strike Saudi Arabia, Iran will have to bear the consequences.”
Comments by senior officials have raised speculation about renewed hostilities.
Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Sunday “there has been talk of a new war” but that Tehran’s policies remain unchanged.
Trump said on Friday that Washington “may do another little Epic Fury”, referring to the US-Israeli campaign against Iran that began on February 28.
On Sunday, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu warned that Iran may try to disrupt the Israeli elections, where he is in a close-fought race to stay in power.
“We have intelligence signs that our enemies, Iran and its proxies, could challenge us with attacks in order to disrupt the elections,” Netanyahu said.
“Don’t test us. You will suffer disproportionate blows,” added Netanyahu, who has campaigned heavily on his security credentials.
The remarks came as Israel’s Channel 12, citing unnamed sources, reported a confrontation between Netanyahu and army chief Eyal Zamir over an unspecified new directive in the war with Iran, which the premier denied.

item.title: Hasnat slams IGP over crossfire remarks, urges police neutrality
item.description:
National Citizen Party (NCP) Chief Organizer (Southern Region) and Cumilla-4 MP Hasnat Abdullah on Monday criticized Inspector General of Police (IGP) Ali Hossain Fakir over his remarks on crossfire, accusing him of speaking like a thug and urging police to remain neutral.
“This government-appointed IGP is a thug. Like in the fascist era, he is now threatening crossfire. Let us see what action the government takes against him,” Hasnat said at an NCP public outreach program in Mugda in the capital in the afternoon.
He said the IGP's remarks are unbecoming of a police force meant to serve the people, comparing him with former IGP Benazir Ahmed and former Detective Branch chief Harun Or Rashid, who served during the Awami League government.
Hasnat also warned police against serving the interests of political leaders, saying, “You are not the home minister's police, nor the prime minister's police. The uniform you wear is bought with the people's taxes. Do not forget that. Neither the home minister in Eskaton nor the prime minister in Gulshan will protect you. The people will.”
Urging the police and administration to remain neutral in the upcoming local government elections, he said they should not work for any political party, be it the BNP, NCP or Jamaat. “Work for the people. Maintain utmost integrity to ensure a fair election,” he said.
The NCP leader claimed that people are now regretting voting for the BNP, referring to an incident in Mymensingh in which a woman allegedly went live on social media and hit herself with a shoe to express remorse for voting for the party.
He criticized the woman's arrest and demanded her immediate release. “The home minister has unjustly arrested her. She must be released.”
Hasnat also raised the case of Miraj Sheikh, who has reportedly been missing in Mongla for more than six months.
“The home minister's Coast Guard picked him up, and there has been no trace of him since then. The government must answer where Mongla's Miraj is,” he said.
Expressing doubts about the upcoming local government elections, the NCP leader alleged that the BNP is plotting to derail the polls. “We cannot trust the present government and administration,” he said.
Seeking votes for NCP-nominated Dhaka South City Corporation mayoral candidate Nasiruddin Patwary, he said, “Nasiruddin will be the people's mayor, the mayor of their hearts.”
Hasnat also accused the BNP government of nepotism in fertilizer dealership appointments and criticized what he described as an ongoing “syndicate” in the liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) market.
