item.title: Sexual abuse allegations at madrasas raise questions over oversight
item.description:
A series of allegations of sexual abuse involving students at madrasas across Bangladesh has raised questions about child protection, complaint mechanisms and institutional accountability, particularly in residential institutions where children live away from their families.
Recent cases in Gazipur, Kushtia, Chittagong, Pabna and Brahmanbaria have led to arrests and criminal proceedings against teachers and madrasa officials. Some cases involve allegations of repeated sexual abuse, while earlier incidents include the deaths of children.
The High Court has issued directives requiring educational institutions and workplaces to establish committees to prevent sexual harassment, receive complaints, investigate allegations and recommend appropriate action. However, reports of alleged abuse in both Alia and Qawmi madrasas have prompted questions about how effectively these safeguards are being implemented.
Alia madrasas operate under the supervision of government education authorities and the Bangladesh Madrasa Education Board. Qawmi madrasas, by contrast, largely operate under their own education boards and management structures.
The distinction has renewed debate over who is responsible for monitoring individual institutions, ensuring that complaints are investigated and holding authorities accountable when allegations are ignored.
In recent weeks, cases have been filed and arrests made following allegations of sexual abuse involving children at Qawmi madrasas in Tongi and Gachha in Gazipur. In Banshkhali, Chittagong, a madrasa headmaster was arrested over allegations of repeatedly sexually abusing an eight-year-old student.
In Daulatpur, Kushtia, a Qawmi madrasa teacher was arrested following an allegation that he attempted to rape a nine-year-old student. A separate case involving an Alia-stream Dakhil madrasa teacher in Brahmanbaria also resulted in an arrest over the alleged rape of a female student.
These cases have drawn attention to the safety of students, particularly children living in residential institutions, and the availability of safe and effective channels for reporting abuse.
On October 20, an allegation of sexual harassment was raised against Mosleh Uddin, vice-principal of Qari Ul Quran International Madrasa in Madhya Auchpara, Tongi, Gazipur, involving a seven-year-old student.
The child's family alleged that the teacher kissed the child inappropriately and threatened physical punishment if the incident was disclosed. After the child's father filed a case, police arrested the accused. A court subsequently ordered that he be sent to jail.
In Pakuria village under Pragpur Union in Daulatpur upazila, Kushtia, Sayeed Hossain, also known as Nannu, a teacher at Darul Abrar Madrasa, was accused of attempting to rape a nine-year-old third-grade student.
The child's mother filed a case on October 20. The teacher was arrested and subsequently sent to jail.
In Gazipur, police arrested teacher Oliullah Islam and madrasa director Mohammad Mizan following allegations that an eight-year-old residential student at Darul Hedaya Qawmi Madrasa in the Kalmeswar area under Gachha police station had been repeatedly sexually abused. Both were sent to jail on October 23.
According to the case statement, the child's family had reported the alleged abuse to the madrasa authorities, but no action was taken. The family also alleged that attempts were made to cover up the incident.
Three people were named as accused in the case, two of whom had been arrested, according to the report.
In Banshkhali, Chittagong, the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) arrested madrasa headmaster Muhammad Ramiz Uddin on August 3 over allegations of repeatedly sexually abusing an eight-year-old student.
He was arrested in the Bairag area near China Road, close to the Karnaphuli Tunnel in Anwara.
The child studied at Darussunnah Khairia Madrasa in Paschim Chechuria Ghonapara, Bailchhari Union, Banshkhali.
According to the case statement, the teacher allegedly took the child to a washroom and abused the student repeatedly, threatening the child to ensure silence. The alleged abuse was said to have continued from the time the child enrolled at the institution.
After the madrasa closed on July 23, another alleged incident reportedly took place in a classroom on the second floor of the orphanage's Hifz department, where students memorise the Quran.
The child's father filed a case on July 29 under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act.
Earlier incidents have also raised concerns about the safety of children in Qawmi madrasas.
In June 2019, a teacher named Hafizur Rahman was arrested in Sharsha, Jessore, over allegations that he attempted to sexually assault and subsequently murdered 12-year-old student. Police said the child was killed after the alleged attempt to sexually assault him failed. The teacher was arrested at a Qawmi madrasa in Dighalia, Khulna.
In March 2022, three teachers were arrested after the body of an eight-year-old student was found with his throat slit at a Qawmi madrasa in Boalkhali, Chittagong.
More recently, in Pabna Sadar upazila, Md Abu Yusuf, a teacher and director of Nure Madina Women's Qawmi Madrasa in Dari Bhaudanga, Bharara Union, was accused of sexually abusing and attempting to rape a student.
Local residents detained him on October 22 and handed him over to police. The following day, an angry crowd vandalised the madrasa and set it on fire.
Allegations of sexual offences have also emerged at Alia-stream institutions.
In Kasba, Brahmanbaria, Abul Bashar, a mathematics teacher at a Dakhil madrasa, was accused of raping a sixth-grade student. A medical examination reportedly found that the student was three months pregnant.
The teacher was arrested, and the student's father filed a case under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act. The student alleged that the teacher had threatened to kill her if she disclosed the incident.
According to data from Ain o Salish Kendra (ASK), 118 children were victims of rape, and 46 were victims of attempted rape in Bangladesh between January and May 20, 2026.
Data compiled by France-based human rights organisation JusticeMakers Bangladesh in France (JMBF) documented 171 victims across 131 incidents of sexual violence against boys between January and September 2026.
Of those incidents, 72 occurred in madrasas and involved 109 boys. The organisation recorded allegations against 81 madrasa teachers in 65 of the cases.
JMBF's data do not distinguish between Qawmi and Alia madrasas. ASK's figures, meanwhile, cover violence against children nationwide rather than incidents specifically involving madrasa students.
As a result, the available figures do not establish the total number of sexual abuse cases occurring in madrasas or allow a direct comparison between the two education systems.
Human rights organisations in Bangladesh monitor incidents of rape and other forms of violence largely through media reports and other available information. However, they do not maintain separate national statistics categorised by educational institution.
Consequently, there is no comprehensive monthly or annual count of rape cases specifically involving students at madrasas.
ASK recorded 641 incidents of rape involving women and children across Bangladesh between January and July 2026. The figure included 400 cases involving women and 241 involving children.
Abu Ahmed Faizul Kabir, a senior coordinator at ASK, told Bangla Tribune that the organisation did not categorise its records by institution and therefore could not provide separate figures for madrasas.
"We do not maintain records categorised by institution; therefore, there are no separate figures for madrasas. However, our observations suggest that incidents of rape and sexual harassment occur in educational institutions, including madrasas," he said.
He added that this did not mean such incidents were absent from other types of educational institutions. ASK had also observed cases in which boys were raped or sexually abused in madrasas, he said.
The absence of institution-specific data makes it difficult to assess the scale of the problem in madrasas, identify patterns and determine whether existing preventive measures are working.
On May 14, 2009, the High Court Division issued landmark directives aimed at preventing sexual harassment in workplaces and educational institutions.
The guidelines called for complaints committees to be established in public and private educational institutions and workplaces. The committees are required to be headed by a woman and include at least two members from outside the institution or organisation.
The directives were intended to remain in force until a separate law on sexual harassment was enacted.
The committees' responsibilities extend beyond receiving complaints. They are expected to examine allegations, conduct investigations and recommend appropriate action. Where a complaint is substantiated, the relevant authorities are required to take action in accordance with applicable rules.
However, the effectiveness of the system depends not only on establishing committees but also on ensuring that they are functional, accessible to students and capable of investigating complaints impartially.
Recent allegations involving madrasa students have raised questions about whether the directives are being implemented effectively, particularly in residential institutions.
On April 16, 2019, the Directorate of Madrasa Education issued a notice calling for committees to be formed to prevent sexual harassment and for oversight to be strengthened. On April 30 that year, the Bangladesh Madrasa Education Board issued a similar directive to its affiliated institutions.
Alia-stream madrasas operate within a government-supervised framework involving the Bangladesh Madrasa Education Board and relevant education authorities.
Qawmi madrasas, however, generally operate under independent education boards and management structures.
Al-Haiatul Ulya Lil-Jamiatil Qawmia Bangladesh, which brings together six Qawmi madrasa education boards, coordinates the recognition of Dawra-e-Hadith (Takmil) certificates and related academic activities.
Its role does not, however, extend to routine supervision of every individual madrasa or the direct investigation of allegations of sexual abuse at those institutions.
This distinction raises questions about the mechanisms available to monitor individual Qawmi madrasas, receive complaints from students and guardians, and ensure that allegations are referred to the appropriate authorities.
The two streams of madrasas should not be assumed to operate under identical administrative arrangements. Nevertheless, regardless of an institution's management structure, allegations of criminal conduct must be addressed under the applicable law.
Zahid Hasan Fahad, a Supreme Court lawyer and joint secretary of the human rights organisation Rise for Rights Foundation, told Bangla Tribune that the allegations in the Tongi case would have to be established through the legal process.
However, he said the allegation that madrasa authorities had failed to act after being informed of the incident warranted particular attention.
"If this allegation proves true, it suggests that the institution lacks an effective sexual harassment prevention committee, as mandated by the High Court," he said.
He described the matter as particularly sensitive because the institution caters to young children.
"If it is established that complaints were ignored or directives were disregarded, then not only the accused individual but also the institution and its head must be brought under the purview of the law," he said.
Fahad said the 2009 High Court ruling required educational institutions and workplaces across the country to establish committees to prevent sexual harassment. Yet, many institutions had either failed to form such committees or had committees that were ineffective, he said.
He added that those responsible should be held accountable if oversight of the directives' implementation was found to be inadequate.
Depending on the circumstances and available evidence, he said, there could also be grounds for initiating contempt of court proceedings.
Muhammad Mozammel Hossain Khan, director of administration and finance at the Directorate of Madrasa Education, told Bangla Tribune that the directorate regularly issued instructions aimed at preventing sexual abuse in madrasas.
The instructions included disseminating relevant guidance and holding periodic meetings with guardians to discuss the issue. Monitoring at the upazila level was carried out through upazila secondary education officers, he said.
However, the directorate did not have its own dedicated field-level monitoring mechanism, he added.
Mozammel said reports of such incidents had increased recently and that monitoring needed to be strengthened.
"We will work on this and place greater emphasis on the implementation of these directives," he said.
The Directorate of Madrasa Education said Alia madrasas were monitored at the field level by officials of the Directorate of Secondary and Higher Education, as the Directorate of Madrasa Education did not have its own dedicated field-level staff.
Maulana Bahauddin Zakaria, vice-president of Befaqul Madarisil Arabia Bangladesh and senior joint secretary general of Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam Bangladesh, said Qawmi madrasas operated under their own curricula and management systems.
Each madrasa had its own committee, and teachers were accountable to that committee, he told Bangla Tribune.
"I am not certain to what extent the High Court's directives apply to Qawmi madrasas. Nevertheless, even when isolated untoward incidents occur, the madrasa boards and authorities remain vigilant and play a proactive role," he said.
He added that madrasa authorities took action against individuals involved in wrongdoing, although such action often went unreported.
A professor in the Department of Arabic Language and Literature at Government Madrasa-e-Alia told Bangla Tribune that government educational institutions had committees to address drug abuse and sexual harassment.
He said similar committees should be established at private educational institutions and made fully functional.
Regular monitoring was also necessary to ensure that the committees could perform their duties effectively, he added.
Children may be reluctant to report sexual abuse because of fear, shame or social pressure. These barriers can be particularly difficult for students at residential madrasas, who live away from their families and may depend on teachers and administrators for their daily needs.
In the Gachha case in Gazipur, the child's family alleged that the madrasa authorities failed to act after being informed of the alleged abuse. Similar allegations have also appeared in a report by BBC Bangla.
The allegations must be established through an impartial investigation. However, claims that complaints were ignored highlight the need for reporting mechanisms that children and guardians can access without fear of retaliation.
Removing an accused teacher from an institution, on its own, is not enough to address an allegation. Authorities must ensure an impartial investigation, take appropriate legal action where warranted and put safeguards in place to prevent further abuse.
Students should be able to report concerns to a trusted adult or an independent authority, particularly when the person accused of abuse holds a position of power within the institution.
Those concerned with child protection say madrasas should establish or activate complaints committees and clearly communicate the names of committee members and their contact details to students and guardians.
Institutions should also provide safe and confidential channels for reporting abuse, including alternative ways to lodge complaints when a student cannot approach the institution's management directly.
When allegations are received, authorities should ensure impartial investigations, protect the confidentiality of complainants and take appropriate legal measures. Complaints should be documented, and residential madrasas should be subject to regular inspections.
Institutions must also be held accountable for attempts to intimidate complainants, suppress reports or shield accused individuals from investigation.
Teachers, students and guardians should receive guidance on child protection, recognising inappropriate behaviour and reporting concerns.
The responsibilities of education boards, government departments and madrasa management committees should be clearly defined for both Qawmi and Alia institutions. Effective oversight requires more than issuing directives or formally establishing committees: reporting channels must work, allegations must be investigated fairly, and those responsible for neglecting their duties must be held accountable.
Hefazat-e-Islam Bangladesh has said that six Qawmi madrasa education boards and institutions under their jurisdiction have been instructed to form or activate student protection committees to prevent abuse and immoral conduct.
In a statement sent to the media on Saturday night, the organisation's joint secretary general, Maulana Azizul Haque Islamabadi, said allegations of student abuse or unethical behaviour must be investigated and reports submitted within a maximum of seven days.
The statement also said the madrasa boards had been directed to establish monitoring cells and hotlines through which complaints could be reported.
Hefazat Ameer Allama Shah Muhibbullah Babunagari and Secretary General Allama Sajedur Rahman said Al-Haiatul Ulya Lil-Jamiatil Qawmia Bangladesh had issued the instructions on September 19.
The leaders said child abuse and other forms of misconduct in educational institutions were unacceptable, but stressed that people must not take the law into their own hands.
They called for fair investigations and appropriate action through administrative and legal channels to maintain law and order.
Describing child sexual abuse as a longstanding social problem, the leaders said it was not confined to any one community or type of institution, noting that abuse could occur in schools, madrasas and other settings.
They warned that institutions could face suspension or cancellation of affiliation if they failed to establish student protection committees, allowed committees to remain inactive or failed to act on complaints.
The statement also stressed that children's safety and emotional well-being must be prioritised. It called on schools and madrasas to follow the instructions issued by their respective authorities and warned that those found guilty of misconduct should face both institutional and legal consequences.
The leaders said there would be no compromise in dealing with such cases, emphasising the responsibility of educational institutions to provide children with a safe environment for learning and development.
Religious Affairs Minister Kazi Shah Mofazzal Hossain, also known as Kaikobad, described the reported incidents as "very sad and shameful".
He made the remarks on Saturday morning after the triennial council session of the Bangladesh National Imam Association in Agargaon, Dhaka.
"I have noticed that such incidents in the country are very sad and shameful. I believe this thing will not happen in future. We will do what is necessary in that regard," he said.
The minister added that imams had been instructed to raise awareness to help prevent such acts in religious institutions, including madrasas.

item.title: Offices reopen after five-day holiday
item.description:
Government, semi-government and autonomous offices across the country reopened on Sunday after a five-day holiday for Durga Puja and the weekend.
Banks, insurance companies, the stock market and private-sector establishments also resumed operations.
According to the official holiday calendar, October 20 was a holiday by executive order for Durga Puja (Maha Navami), followed by a public holiday on October 21 for Vijaya Dashami. Thursday, October 22, was also declared a holiday by executive order.
The holidays were followed by the regular weekend on Friday and Saturday, October 23 and 24, keeping offices and courts closed for five consecutive days.
With the holidays over, traffic and commuter numbers increased on the capital’s streets from Sunday morning as people returned to work.
Traffic congestion was reported in several areas, including Badda, Rampura, Mohakhali, Farmgate, Shahbagh and Tejgaon.
Rafiqul Islam, deputy commissioner of the Tejgaon Traffic Division, said the volume of people and vehicles had increased as offices reopened after the extended break.
He added that although traffic congestion occurred earlier in the morning, the situation had since returned to normal.

item.title: Govt defers proposal to buy LNG from JERAGM pending legal vetting
item.description:
The government has deferred a proposal seeking approval to purchase liquefied natural gas (LNG) directly from Japan’s JERA Global Markets Pte Ltd (JERAGM), pending legal vetting by the Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division.
The decision was taken at the 35th meeting of the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs held on Saturday, where a single proposal from the Energy and Mineral Resources Division was placed for discussion.
Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury presided over the meeting.
The proposal sought approval in principle to procure LNG from JERAGM through the direct procurement method under Section 68 of the Public Procurement Act, 2006, and Rule 99(2) of the Public Procurement Rules, 2025.
It also sought approval to sign the finalised formats of the short-term LNG Sale and Purchase Agreement (SPA) and the term sheet between Bangladesh Oil, Gas and Mineral Corporation (Petrobangla) and JERAGM.
The committee decided that the proposal will be placed before it again after obtaining vetting from the Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division.
No final approval for the proposed LNG purchase or signing of the agreements was granted at the meeting.

item.title: HSBC-BGMEA to promote manufacturing capabilities in BD apparel roadshow in Hong Kong
item.description:
The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited in Bangladesh and the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA), in collaboration with the Consulate General of Bangladesh in Hong Kong, is organizing “Bangladesh Apparel Roadshow” in Hong Kong on October 28 at the Island Shangri-La, Hong Kong.
The initiative will bring together global buyers, sourcing partners and industry stakeholders to showcase Bangladesh’s evolving apparel manufacturing capabilities, including product diversification, technical apparel, innovation and sustainable manufacturing.
As one of the world’s leading apparel-exporting countries, Bangladesh continues to advance its position in the global value chain.
Against the backdrop of evolving global sourcing strategies and changing market dynamics, the roadshow will provide a platform to highlight the sector’s expanding capabilities and explore opportunities for deeper international trade and collaboration.
The program will feature presentations on Bangladesh’s apparel capabilities, discussions on the global retail outlook and emerging sourcing trends, a panel discussion, and an apparel showcase highlighting innovation and technical apparel.
Senior officials from the HSBC Hong Kong team including Oliver T Jones, head of global network banking, Hong Kong, amongst many others will participate in the discussions.
The event will facilitate engagement between international buyers and industry stakeholders, supporting dialogue on emerging opportunities, and the evolving requirements of global apparel supply chains.
Through its international network, global trade expertise and longstanding presence in Bangladesh, HSBC continues supporting businesses in navigating international markets and pursue cross-border growth opportunities.
The roadshow reflects the bank’s commitment to facilitating international business connections and supporting Bangladesh’s participation in global trade.
BGMEA, as the apex trade body representing Bangladesh’s apparel manufacturers and exporters, brings industry expertise and representation to the initiative.
The collaboration also underscores the importance of strengthening international engagement to support the sector’s diversification, competitiveness and long-term growth.
Md Mahbub ur Rahman, CEO, HSBC Bangladesh, and Mahmud Hasan Khan, president, BGMEA, will co-host the event.

item.title: Gold prices cut by Tk3,324 per bhori in Bangladesh
item.description:
The Bangladesh Jewellers Association (Bajus) on Sunday cut gold prices by Tk3,324 per bhori, setting the price of 22-carat gold at Tk220,858, including valued added tax (VAT).
The revised prices came into effect at 10am on Sunday, according to a Bajus press release.
The organisation said it lowered gold prices following a decline in the price of pure gold in the local market.
Under the new rates, 21-carat gold will cost Tk210,943 per bhori, 18-carat gold Tk181,200 and traditional-method gold Tk148,016.
Bajus said making charges will apply depending on the design of the jewellery. As VAT is included in the selling prices of gold and silver ornaments, jewellers cannot collect it separately from customers.
For jewellery exchanges, 12% will be deducted from the price, excluding making charges and stones, while 18% will be deducted for purchases. VAT cannot be deducted separately in exchange and purchase transactions, the association said.
The revised prices will remain effective at all jewellery establishments until further notice.
Before Sunday's adjustment, Bajus last revised gold prices on October 23, slashing Tk2,158 per bhori to set the price of 22-carat gold at Tk224,182, including VAT.
At the time, 21-carat gold was priced at Tk214,093 per bhori, 18-carat gold at Tk183,883 and traditional-method gold at Tk150,232.
With Sunday's adjustment, gold prices have been revised 126 times in the domestic market so far this year. Prices have been raised 60 times, lowered 65 times, and adjusted once for VAT.
Meanwhile, silver prices remained unchanged in the domestic market.
Including VAT, 22-carat silver is selling at Tk3,849 per bhori, 21-carat silver at Tk3,674, 18-carat silver at Tk3,149 and traditional-method silver at Tk2,391.
Silver prices have been revised 76 times so far this year, with 36 increases and 40 decreases.

item.description:

“The next general election will be held under a caretaker government,” he made the remarks at a press briefing at the Ministry of Home Affairs following the successful and peaceful celebration of Durga Puja.
Emphasizing the government’s position on restoring the caretaker government system, he said that there was political consensus on holding the next general election under a caretaker administration.

item.title: Kishoreganj-Dhaka bus services halted over transport owners’ dispute
item.description:
Bus services on the Kishoreganj-Dhaka route have been suspended indefinitely since Sunday morning following a dispute between transport owners in Kishoreganj and Dhaka, causing suffering for commuters.
The Kishoreganj District Road Transport Owners’ Association announced the suspension, halting all private bus services on the route.
Association leaders said the newly formed committee took an initiative to improve passenger services by replacing old buses with new ones after assuming responsibility. Following discussions, transport owners in Dhaka also agreed to the proposal.
However, while Kishoreganj owners replaced their old buses with new ones, their Dhaka counterparts did not replace their outdated vehicles and instead added two more buses to the route, they said.
Tensions mounted between the two factions over the issue, culminating in a sharp dispute on Saturday.
Following the dispute, the Kishoreganj association suspended all private bus services on the Kishoreganj-Mohakhali route from Sunday morning.
The suspension left passengers travelling between Kishoreganj and Dhaka facing considerable inconvenience.

Over 6,000 cases pending with Women and Children Repression Prevention Tribunals in Rangpur
item.description:
More than 6,000 cases remain pending with three Women and Children Repression Prevention Tribunals in Rangpur, with over 300 rape and dowry cases awaiting trial for five to 18 years, leaving victims and accused trapped in prolonged legal battles.
Over 2,000 of the pending cases involve rape, while victims say repeated court appearances and mounting legal expenses have pushed many families into financial hardship.
A visit to the tribunals revealed the plight of litigants who have spent years seeking justice. Sharifa Yasmin, from Anandanagar village in Pirgachha upazila, said her husband and in-laws drove her out of their home because she could not pay Tk200,000 in dowry.
She filed a case six years ago, but the trial has yet to begin. With hearings scheduled roughly every two months, Sharifa said she had sold cattle, goats, ducks and chickens to cover travel costs and court-related expenses.
Other women, including Asma Begum of Pirgachha and Mariam Begum of Rangpur Sadar, also described similar experiences.
Asma, a poor woman, said her daughter was abducted and raped eight years ago, but the trial had yet to begin.
Sohrab Hossain of Bhandarbari village in Pirgachha said he had been attending court for 18 years in connection with a rape case filed against him. Working as a rickshaw puller in Dhaka, he returns to Rangpur every two months for hearings.
He said he could not afford to miss a hearing for fear of an arrest warrant, forcing him to spend money on repeated journeys while struggling to earn a living.
Human rights activists and legal experts blamed the delays on a shortage of judges, police failures to produce witnesses and a lack of diligence by those involved in prosecution.
Rumana Zaman, president of Rangpur district chapter of Bangladesh Mahila Parishad, said the law sets time limits for disposing of cases involving violence against women and children, yet many litigants spend years waiting for justice. She called for more judges to expedite trials.
Rights activist Monowara Begum warned that the failure to punish offenders was allowing violence, rape and dowry-related abuse to persist. She also urged authorities to increase the number of judges and ensure speedy trials.
Shafi Kamal, special public prosecutor at Tribunal-1, said nearly 2,000 cases were awaiting trial at his court. He cited the absence of complainants and witnesses on scheduled dates, along with other procedural complications, as reasons for the growing backlog. He said judges and prosecutors were working to ensure justice for litigants.
Moksedul Haque, special public prosecutor at Tribunal-2, said they were also trying to expedite proceedings.
Legal experts called for a dedicated cell to speed up the disposal of cases involving violence against women and children in Rangpur, alongside stricter monitoring by the High Court.

item.title: Health Minister: Community clinics to be renamed family welfare centres
item.description:
Health Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Husain on Saturday announced that all community clinics across the country will be renamed family welfare centres as part of plans to expand healthcare services at union level.
He made the announcement while outlining the government’s plans to improve healthcare infrastructure and services during surprise visits to several health facilities in Mymensingh.
Earlier in the day, the minister visited Fulbaria and Tarakanda Upazila Health Complexes before inspecting Mymensingh Medical College Hospital, where he expressed dissatisfaction over various irregularities, including medical equipment found in a garbage dump and doctors and nurses failing to report to work on time.
During his visit to the hospital around noon, he inspected the labour ward, measles isolation ward and dengue ward. He also examined the quality of treatment, the ward environment and the condition of washrooms.
The minister expressed anger after finding rubbish on the ground floor of the hospital's new building. He also ordered a swift investigation and the submission of a report into the discovery of used cannulas, syringes and other medical equipment in the hospital's garbage dump.
He said action would be taken against those found negligent in their duties, including staff who failed to arrive at the hospital on time. The minister also questioned why a patient in the gynaecology ward had to purchase saline from outside and instructed the hospital authorities to take necessary measures.
He further sought an explanation for the delay in submitting an investigation report into a fire at the hospital more than a month ago. The authorities told him that the report has been delayed due to holidays.
Earlier, during his visits to Fulbaria and Tarakanda Upazila Health Complexes, he said the government planned to upgrade both health complexes to 151-bed facilities.
A large-scale tendering process worth around Tk 16,000 crore for the health sector would be launched within the next 15 to 20 days, he said, adding that steps would be taken to ensure the supply of necessary medicines to the community clinics after they are renamed family welfare centres.

After the inspection, the health minister told journalists that the government is working to bring the country’s health sector to a level that meets public expectations and ensures people’s satisfaction, in line with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s directives.
Noting that the government has taken various initiatives to resolve long-standing problems in the health sector, he said, “Cleanliness activities at hospitals are being strengthened, medicine supplies are being increased and adequate stocks of saline have been ensured.”
Sakhawat expressed the hope that significant progress in the health sector would become visible within the next few months.
He also said the government plans to invite tenders worth several thousand crore taka within the next 15 days as part of its efforts to develop and restructure the health sector.
This tender is aimed at improving various healthcare institutions across the country, including upazila health complexes, the minister said.
Besides, he said, initiatives are being taken to establish modern pathological laboratories at upazila-level hospitals so that diagnostic facilities can be expanded at the grassroots level.

item.title: Two killed, 15 injured in bus-truck collision in Brahmanbaria

The committee made the recommendations at its first meeting of the 13th National Parliament at the National Parliamnet with its Chairman Md Akhtaruzzaman Mia, MP, in the chair.

It suggested involving local members of parliament in taking necessary steps to make yarn, dyes and other raw materials more accessible to marginal weavers through weavers' associations or the appointment of dealers, said a press release of parliament secretariat.
The committee further recommended examining the operations of the Bangladesh Handloom Board's office at Ranir Bandar in Dinajpur and verifying whether the land associated with the office had been leased out or allocated through other means before taking necessary action.
At the meeting, the committee reviewed the activities of the Ministry of Textiles and Jute and its subordinate departments and agencies. Officials presented an overview of their operations and briefed the committee on the ministry's initiatives under the government's 180-day program and the progress of ongoing projects.
The committee also recommended conducting all activities of the Ministry of Textiles and Jute in line with the prime minister's election manifesto and taking appropriate and necessary initiatives to implement its commitments.
At the beginning of the meeting, the chairman paid tribute to Shaheed President Ziaur Rahman, former BNP Chairperson and former Prime Minister Begum Khaleda Zia and the martyrs who sacrificed their lives in the Great War of Liberation. He prayed for the salvation of their souls.
He also paid tribute to those killed during the July 2024 movement and expressed deep sympathy for those injured in the movement.
Textiles and Jute Minister Khandakar Abdul Muktadir, MP, State Minister Md Shariful Alam, MP, and committee members S M Faisal, MP, Md Abdullah MP, Rezeka Sultana, MP, Md Afjal Hossain MP, Hafez Muhammad Rabiul Bashar, MP, and Mahabuba Hakim, MP, attended the meeting.

item.title: Madhumati embankment breach sparks erosion fears
item.description:
A 52-metre section of a protective embankment along the Madhumati River has developed a breach near Fukra Launch Ghat in Gopalganj’s Kashiani upazila, raising fears of further erosion and threatening nearby homes, farmland, roads and institutions.
Built about 10 years ago, the 2.5km embankment had helped bring river erosion under control. However, a breach that appeared on September 23 has renewed concerns among residents, who are demanding permanent protection.
Several other sections of the embankment are also at risk, as the soil beneath the structure is suspected to have been washed away.
The Bangladesh Water Development Board (BWDB) began placing sandbags at the site on October 10. Around 5,000 sandbags have been placed to contain the erosion, said Md Koushik Gazi, a work assistant at the BWDB’s Bhatia Para sub-divisional engineer’s office in Kashiani.
He said the river’s narrow, deep channel and a bend near Fukra Launch Ghat had contributed to the problem. As water levels began to recede about a month ago, the current intensified, triggering the breach.
The full extent of the damage would become clear once water levels fell further, allowing officials to assess the condition of the embankment, Gazi added.
BWDB Gopalganj Executive Engineer Md Shawkat Osman said temporary measures were underway to prevent further erosion, while a feasibility study for permanent protection was in progress.
“Once the study is completed, we plan to construct a permanent protective embankment near Fukra Launch Ghat under a project,” he said.
Local residents Md Mintu Munshi and Alamgir Hossain Zakir said erosion had already destroyed homes, farmland and trees in the area. They said nearly two kilometres of land on the Gopalganj side had been eroded, while chars had emerged across the river in Lohagara upazila of Narail.
The renewed erosion has put remaining homes, cropland, roads and educational and religious institutions at risk, they said, urging the authorities to build a permanent embankment.
Abir Alamgir Piyas, a first-year honours student at Ramdia SK Government College, said generations of local residents had lost their ancestral land to river erosion.
“The erosion has started again, putting whatever property we have left at risk. My family and many others are living in fear,” he said, calling for permanent protection.

item.title: Banned Chhatra League, Jubo League activists attack police in Gopalganj, injure 2
item.description:
Leaders and activists of the banned Chhatra League and Jubo League attacked police in Gopalganj on Saturday afternoon, vandalizing a police vehicle and beating 2 police personnel, according to police.
The incident took place around noon in the Raghunathpur ferry terminal area of Gopalganj Sadar upazila. Activists of the 2 organizations were seen taking part in the attack with sticks.
A video of the incident has circulated on social media, with several Chhatra League activists who took part in the procession sharing it on their Facebook accounts.
The video shows processionists carrying sticks from Charpara road in Raghunathpur and arriving at the ferry terminal area. They chanted “Joy Bangla” before attacking and vandalizing a police vehicle on patrol. Police personnel left the scene in the vehicle immediately after the vandalism.
Gopalganj Sadar police station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Md Aminul Islam said: “Police were conducting routine patrols in the Bedgram ferry terminal area under Sadar police station. At that time, several people were marching in support of Sheikh Hasina, led by banned Jubo League leader Milan and Chhatra League leader Mursalin. When police tried to stop them, the processionists attacked the police with sticks. 2 police personnel, including Sadar police station Sub-Inspector Phul Mia, were injured. The police vehicle was also vandalized. The officers then left the scene in the vehicle.”
The OC further said: “The 2 injured police personnel received primary treatment at Gopalganj 250-bed General Hospital. An operation is underway to arrest members of the banned Jubo League and Chhatra League involved in the attack and vehicle vandalism. Additional police have been deployed in the area.”
Senior police officials visited the scene after receiving news of the attack. The area remained tense following the incident.
Police and other law enforcement personnel have strengthened security measures and set up checkpoints at key locations across the district to maintain normalcy following the attack and vandalism.

Bayern coach Kompany in hospital after collapsing
item.description:
Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany was taken to hospital by an emergency medical team on Friday after collapsing during training, the club said.
"Vincent Kompany had to seek medical attention on Friday after collapsing during a training session with FC Bayern's reserve team," Bayern said on their website.
"Kompany is undergoing thorough examinations at the hospital and will remain under medical care."
Kompany, the 40-year-old former Manchester City defender, missed training and a press conference on Tuesday ahead of Bayern's Champions League draw against Arsenal at the Allianz Arena.
"I caught a pretty nasty virus last week, and of course I didn't listen to my body -- and then at some point my body just said, 'enough is enough!'" Kompany said after the Arsenal game.
On Friday, Bayern's sporting director Max Eberl said the health of their coach "is our top priority".
"We at FC Bayern will do everything we can to ensure he recovers quickly. Vinnie is receiving all the necessary medical care and support, as well as all the time he needs. His coaching staff, whom we trust completely, will take over his duties."
English assistant coach Aaron Danks took training and handled the press conference ahead of the Arsenal game.
"It affected his legs at times; he was experiencing some pain. It's just a virus. He needs rest," Danks said on Tuesday.
"The most important thing we're encouraging him to do right now is to rest and take as much time as he needs—no matter how long that may be."
Bundesliga leaders Bayern visit Freiburg, who are third in the table, on Saturday.
Their next Champions League match is on November 3 in Madrid against Atletico.
The Spanish club posted their best wishes on social media.
"We wish you a speedy recovery. We hope to see you here in Madrid, on the bench, in a few days," wrote the Spanish club adding a heart emoji.
Kompany, a centre back, started his career with Anderlecht in his native Brussels. He moved to Hamburg and then to Manchester City as one of the club's last signings before the Abu Dhabi takeover in 2008.
He went on to play 360 games for the club, where he was also captain for eight season as the team became the dominant force in English football.
He played 89 times for Belgium and finished his playing career back at Anderlecht in 2019 where he was player-coach in the first of his three seasons in charge
He took over at Burnley in 2022, leading them to a Championship title in 2023 but the club was relegated the next season with their lowest ever points total.
Bayern, who had just endured a trophyless season and had been unable to persuade Thomas Tuchel to stay, sprung a surprise by paying Burnley to sign Kompany as manager in 2024.
He led the club two the Bundesliga title each of his first two seasons and to a German Cup in 2026. After six games, Bayern lead the table this season on goal difference. In 74 Bundesliga games under Kompany, Bayern have won 57 and lost three.
Kompany completed an MBA at Manchester Business School in 2018.

"He is always friendly, open, and approachable. Yet, he knows exactly what he wants and how he wants it done on the pitch,"

item.title: Summer Athletics 2026: Imranur, Shirin claim 100m gold
item.description:
Bangladesh Navy’s sprinters Imranur Rahman and Shirin Akter dominated the men’s and women’s 100 metres respectively in the 18th Koko National Summer Athletics competition, as fresh promises were made to improve athletes’ accommodation, nutrition and transport facilities.
On the first day of the competition held at National Stadium on Friday, Imranur clocked 10.53 seconds to win the men’s 100m gold, finishing ahead of his fellow Navy sprinter Mohammad Ismail, who took silver in 10.67 seconds. Army’s Tarek Rahman claimed bronze in 10.73 seconds.
Shirin won the women’s 100m title in 12.08 seconds. Army’s Sharifa Khatun finished second in 12.23 seconds, while Navy’s Sumaiya Dewan took third place in 12.33 seconds.
Shirin credited her success to the support of her teammates, coach and sporting organisations.
“Alhamdulillah, by the infinite mercy of Allah, it feels wonderful to finish first,” she said after winning the coveted gold.
She acknowledged the contributions of coach Abdullah Hel Kafi, Bangladesh Navy, Bangladesh Krira Shikkha Protishtan (BKSP), Bangladesh Athletics Federation and Bangladesh Olympic Association to her achievement.
Shirin also expressed hope that the performance would boost her preparations for the upcoming South Asian competitions.
Meanwhile, Imranur stressed the need to improve facilities for athletes, saying initiatives were being taken to address their accommodation, food, nutritional and transport needs.
Efforts are also being made to encourage more athletes from district-level competitions to participate, with greater coordination among the relevant organisations.
Organisers expect improved accommodation, nutritious meals and transport support to encourage wider participation and help identify emerging talent across the country.

Anee: Collective social movement needed to build better society
item.description:
Water Resources Minister and BNP Joint Secretary General Md Shahiduddin Chowdhury Anee on Friday called for a united social movement to protect people's dignity and build a better society, saying the people had suffered significant losses over the past 17 years and did not want to lose anything more.
He made the call while addressing a meeting organised by Life Line Welfare Organization at Ayesha High School field in Totakhil under Chandraganj upazila of Lakshmipur.
Anee urged people to remain united against social problems and work collectively to build a better society, noting that the country had been regained through struggle and sacrifice.
"Do not issue threats of a one-point movement; there is no benefit in making such threats," he said, adding that the BNP had emerged from the streets through movements and struggles and would not be intimidated.
He alleged that Jamaat-e-Islami had colluded with the Awami League and enforced strikes and blockades for 172 days in 1996.
The minister also described Islami Chhatra Shibir as a clandestine organisation that had operated at various universities before August 5, urging people to remain vigilant.
Criticising opposition parties, Anee alleged that they were obstructing the government outside Parliament despite delivering eloquent speeches inside the House.
Political parties, he said, should focus on national and social development rather than confining their activities to rallies and meetings.
Anee also called for collective efforts to counter religious misinterpretations, misinformation and drug abuse, warning that those involved in such activities would not be spared regardless of their influence.
Later, he distributed sewing machines among women.

item.title: Five killed, seven injured in separate road accidents in Faridpur
item.description:
Five people, including a mother and her son, were killed and at least seven others injured in two separate road accidents in Faridpur on Friday.
In the first incident, a sand-laden truck overturned onto an autorickshaw and a private car in the Tetultala area of Kanaipur on the Dhaka-Khulna highway around 3:30pm, killing Sumi Begum, 32, and her son Shaon, 7. Four passengers of the private car were injured.
Senior Station Officer of Faridpur Fire Service Sribas Baroi said the truck reportedly lost control and overturned, causing the accident. The injured were receiving treatment at hospital.
In another accident, three people were killed when a Magura-bound ambulance collided head-on with a Dhaka-bound King Fisher bus near Arkandi Bridge in Madhukhali upazila around noon.
One of the deceased was identified as Rabbi, 21, while the identities of the other two could not be immediately known.
The victims were reportedly students from Magura Sadar who were returning home after attending a Red Crescent blood donation programme in Faridpur.
The injured were taken to nearby hospitals, with two later referred to Faridpur Medical College Hospital for better treatment.
Officer-in-Charge of Karimpur Highway Police Station, said three people were killed in the bus-ambulance collision. Police were working to identify the deceased and determine the cause of the accident.

item.title: 20 fishermen jailed for defying ilish netting ban in Chandpur
item.description:
A mobile court has sentenced 20 fishermen to different terms of imprisonment for catching ilish in the Padma-Meghna sanctuary in Chandpur, defying a fishing ban.
Of them, 13 fishermen were given 10 days in prison each, while the remaining seven received 15 days' imprisonment each. Each fisherman was also fined Tk 1,000, bringing the total fine to Tk 20,000.
The fishermen are residents of different villages in Laxmipur Model union under Chandpur Sadar upazila.
Md Mizanur Rahman, assistant fisheries officer of Sadar upazila, told UNB that a district task force, led by Assistant Commissioner and Executive Magistrate Md. Najmul Huda, conducted the drive from 4:00pm to 9:00pm on Thursday.
During the drive, the team detained 20 fishermen and seized 30 kg of ilish, 35,000 metres of illegal monofilament fishing nets (locally known as current nets), and three engine-run fishing boats.
The seized ilish were distributed among an orphanage and needy people on Friday morning, while the boats were handed over to the Bangladesh Coast Guard for safekeeping.
The seized fishing nets were burnt in the presence of the executive magistrate.
A 22-day fishing ban in a 70-kilometre sanctuary along the Padma-Meghna rivers in Chandpur began on October 8 and will remain in force until midnight on October 29.
During the ban, catching, buying, selling, storing and transporting all types of fish, including ilish, in the designated rivers are prohibited.
District administration officials said violators will face imprisonment and fines under the law.

item.description:

"Out of the total infected, 159 patients were hospitalized in Barisal division, 219 in Chittagong division, 274 in Dhaka division, 131 in Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) and 116 in Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) areas, 147 in Khulna division, 100 in Mymensingh division, 113 in Rajshahi division, 38 in Rangpur division and two in Sylhet division, a Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) statement said.
Since the start of the dengue onslaughts, Bangladesh this year has witnessed so far 371 deaths while the disease inflicted 119,801.
Last year, the dengue claimed 413 lives and inflicted 1,02,861 people in the country while it claimed 575 lives and inflicted 1,01,214 people in 2024.

item.title: Three killed, four injured in Faridpur road crash
item.description:

The accident occurred around 2:30pm on Friday.
Shamim Reza, station officer of Madhukhali Fire Service, said the ambulance was heading towards Magura when it collided head-on with a local bus named King Fisher coming from Magura.
Three people travelling in the ambulance died on the spot, while four others were injured, he said.
Police and fire service personnel rushed to the scene after receiving the information and launched a rescue operation.
The identities of the deceased had not been confirmed at the time of filing this report.

Dhaka's air quality remains 'unhealthy'
item.description:
Dhaka's air quality remained unhealthy on Friday morning, with an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 153 at 9:10am.
With this score, the capital ranked 12th among the world's most polluted cities.
Pakistan's Lahore, India's Delhi and Senegal's Dakar occupied the top three spots on the list, with AQI scores of 344, 244 and 184 respectively.
Earlier, at 9:20 am on Thursday, the city ranked 7th among the world's most polluted cities, recording an AQI score of 165.
An AQI score between 50 and 100 is considered "moderate" with acceptable air quality, while one between 101 and 150 is considered "unhealthy for sensitive groups," and a score between 151 and 200 is classified as "unhealthy."
AQI readings between 201 and 300 are termed "very unhealthy," and anything above 301 is considered "hazardous," posing serious health risks.
The AQI is a daily indicator of air quality, showing how clean or polluted the air is and the possible health effects people may experience.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five major pollutants: particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide, carbon monoxide, sulphur dioxide and ozone.

Sri Lanka stun England with huge chase after Brook's double century
item.description:
Janith Liyanage smashed a six off the penultimate ball as Sri Lanka completed the second-highest successful run chase in ODI history, scoring 430-8 to beat England in Rawalpindi on Thursday.
Needing eight to win off the last over, Sri Lanka lost two wickets to paceman Josh Tongue, but Liyanage kept his cool to achieve an astonishing victory and overshadow Harry Brook's record-setting knock.
The England captain hit the fastest-ever ODI double hundred, making 202 off 116 balls to propel his team to a mammoth 429-4 after they were put in to bat.
South Africa hold the record for the highest ODI chase, knocking off a target of 435 against Australia at Johannesburg in 2006.
Batters thoroughly dominated in Rawalpindi as Brook also hit the first ODI double century by an England player. However, Sri Lanka proved up to the challenge as Pavan Rathnayake scored 130, with Avishka Fernando and Dasun Shanaka both making 97.
Liyanage then led them over the line with a blistering 61 not out off 27 balls.
Sri Lanka slid to 24-2 before Rathnayake and Avishka set about transforming the innings, putting on 166 for the third wicket.
Rathnayake then combined with Shanaka to lift the tempo with a rapid 133-run stand off just 79 balls, to give Sri Lanka genuine hope.
Rathnayake hit 15 fours and three sixes while Shanaka's blazing knock featured eight sixes and six fours, as Sri Lanka delivered a powerful response to Brook's earlier masterclass.
Sri Lankan skipper Kusal Mendis was delighted at victory.
"I'm very happy as a captain," said Mendis. "Everyone believed we can do it. Every day we talk about showing the character in team meetings, and it's about showing we can get any score."
Brook was full of praise for Sri Lanka.
"Incredible game of cricket, both teams were exceptional. They played exceptional cricket to knock off 400," said Brook, downplaying his double hundred.
"It was a nice innings but being on the losing side it has no value whatsoever in my eyes."
Brook clobbered 10 sixes and 21 fours as England posted a first 400-plus ODI total in Pakistan.
He reached 200 in 114 balls, beating the previous fastest double century in ODIs, by Shubman Gill (117 balls) for India against West Indies last month.
Brook was joined in the fireworks by Joe Root, who scored a 66-ball 69 and became the first England batter to complete 8,000 runs, in his 197th one-day international.
Brook was dismissed off the final delivery, caught off paceman Liyanage, but not before helping England add 156 runs in the last 10 overs.
Opener Tom Banton set the tone with a 51-ball 50 and Will Jacks was 66 not out with three sixes and eight fours.
The day looked as if it would surely belong to history-maker Brook, but Sri Lanka had other ideas as the previous highest ODI total at a Pakistan venue of 375-3 was easily surpassed.
Pakistan, who beat Sri Lanka and England in their two games, will face England in Lahore on Sunday in the next match in the tri-series.

item.title: Dhaka-Chittagong rail services resume after 24 hours
item.description:
Train services on the Dhaka-bound line of the Dhaka-Chittagong route resumed at 12:50pm on Thursday, more than 24 hours after the Karnaphuli Commuter Express derailed in Comilla's Laksam.
The Bijoy Express, travelling from Chittagong to Mymensingh, was the first train to cross the accident site after the line reopened.
Omar Faruk Bhuiyan, station master of Laksam Railway Junction, said train services were now operating normally on both lines.
The damaged track was repaired by 7am on Thursday, but services remained suspended on the Dhaka-bound line because a derailed coach was found. During the suspension, trains in both directions used the other line, causing some disruption. The Chattala Express, bound for Dhaka, and the Paharika Express, bound for Sylhet, passed through Laksam at 10:23am and 10:48am, respectively, on Thursday.
The accident occurred around 12:30pm on Wednesday in the outer section of Naoti station, near Azgara Bazar in Laksam, when five coaches of the Karnaphuli Commuter Express and three wheels of its engine derailed. At least seven passengers were injured.
A rescue train from Chittagong reached the site on Wednesday evening. Recovery work was completed around 5am on Thursday, followed by track repairs.
Meanwhile, railway authorities suspended sub-assistant engineer Sarwar Alam over allegations that he failed to inform the control room about repair work underway at the accident site. He was responsible for the Feni region under the Eastern Railway’s engineering department.
A four-member committee has been formed to investigate the accident, Chittagong Divisional Railway Manager Mostafizur Rahman Bhuiyan said on Wednesday night.

item.title: Bangladesh ambassador to stay in Dhaka during PM’s Japan visit
item.description:
Bangladesh’s Ambassador to Japan Md Daud Ali will remain in Dhaka during Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s upcoming visit to Japan, with Ministry of Foreign Affairs Secretary Md Nazrul Islam set to oversee preparations and arrangements in Tokyo.
Sources at the ministry said the ambassador would not accompany the prime minister on the visit. Md Daud Ali is currently in Dhaka on the instructions of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
However, a ministry official told Dhaka Tribune on Thursday that the ambassador was in Dhaka due to illness. Whether he would join the prime minister’s visit to Japan would be known after his leave.
The prime minister is scheduled to visit Tokyo from October 26 to 29.
According to relevant sources, Secretary Md Nazrul Islam will stay in Tokyo in the ambassador’s absence and oversee preparations and arrangements for the prime minister’s visit.
Nazrul Islam left Dhaka for Tokyo on Wednesday, October 21, to carry out the responsibilities assigned to him for the visit. He will remain there until the visit concludes.
According to diplomats, it is unusual for an ambassador to be in Dhaka on the instructions of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs ahead of a prime ministerial visit.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,207 as two die in 24 hours
item.description:
Two more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Thursday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 1,207.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified both of the latest casualties as suspected.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 1,103, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 104, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
Among the two new suspected fatalities, both were recorded in Dhaka.
A total of 995 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Thursday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 217,760.
During the same period, 36 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 23,248.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 193,608 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 185,927 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

item.title: 4,157 killed in nine months as nation marks Road Safety Day
item.description:
Twelve people died in a head-on collision in Natore on Tuesday. According to police and surviving passengers, the bus was being driven by its supervisor while the regular driver slept in the back.
Two days later, Bangladesh is observing National Road Safety Day with the familiar program of seminars, discussions and promises to make its roads safer.
The latest figures offer little reason for reassurance.
At least 4,157 people were killed and 5,391 injured in 4,285 road crashes between January and September this year, according to the Bangladesh Road Transport Authority (BRTA). That is an average of more than 15 deaths every day.
This year’s observance, under the theme “Safe Roads, Prosperous Nation, Bangladesh First,” comes amid persistent concerns over unfit vehicles, unqualified drivers and the failure to enforce existing traffic laws.
The Natore crash brought several of those concerns into sharp focus.
Police and injured passengers said the RP Special Paribahan bus was heading towards Bonpara when its supervisor, Sohel Rana, took over the wheel after a stop at Ishwardi around 3am.
Ramjan Ali, a surviving passenger from Chapainawabganj, said the regular driver left his seat after the break. About an hour later, the bus collided with a truck, killing 12 people and injuring at least 25.
The circumstances of the crash have once again raised questions about who is allowed to drive passenger buses and how effectively transport operators are monitored.
The deaths in Natore are part of a much larger toll.
According to Bangladesh Jatri Kalyan Samity, at least 125,405 people were killed in 72,736 road crashes between 2013 and 2025. Another 176,249 people were left permanently disabled, the organisation said.
Children have been among the worst affected. Road Safety Foundation figures show that 7,963 children died in road crashes between January 2020 and September 2026.
Nearly 3,000 of them were killed in motorcycle crashes, while 2,812 died as pedestrians.
Yet the problems identified by successive governments and road safety experts remain largely unresolved.
BRTA records indicate that around 650,000 vehicles are operating without the required registration, route permits or fitness certificates. More than 75,000 buses and trucks have exceeded their prescribed economic lifespan.
The shortage of qualified professional drivers for heavy and medium vehicles is estimated at around 30%.
Vehicle fitness is another major concern. Around 70% of buses and minibuses in Dhaka and other major cities reportedly lack valid fitness documents.
Driver health also receives inadequate attention. At a BRTA and Dhaka Ahsania Mission health camp in 2023, around 73% of 541 drivers who underwent eye examinations were found to need glasses.
In 2019, the National Road Safety Council identified seven priority areas and made 111 recommendations to improve road safety.
Experts say there has been little visible progress in implementing them.
BUET Assistant Professor Kazi Md Saifun Newaz said the country already has the Road Transport Act 2018 and Road Transport Rules 2022, but legislation alone cannot prevent crashes.
“Everyone knows the causes of road crashes and their remedies. What is missing is consistent and coordinated action,” he said.
“Observing days will not solve anything.”
The BRTA says it has filed more than 110,000 cases through mobile courts and joint enforcement drives in the first nine months of this year, targeting unfit vehicles, invalid licences, speeding and other violations.
But the continuing death toll raises questions about whether these drives are producing lasting improvements.
Bangladesh Jatri Kalyan Samity Secretary General Mozammel Haque Chowdhury blamed institutional inefficiency, corruption and the influence of transport owners’ and workers’ groups for the persistent disorder.
Road Safety Foundation Executive Director Saidur Rahman said the dangers were particularly acute for children on rural roads, where vehicles frequently pass close to homes and enforcement is weak.
“The authorities know the causes and the consequences, but there is no remedy,” he said.
The government has pledged to enact a comprehensive road safety law by December 2027.
The proposed Road Safety Act 2026 includes free emergency treatment for crash victims, legal protection for people who assist the injured, a demerit-point system for traffic offenders and higher penalties for repeat violations.
Road Transport and Bridges Minister Shaikh Rabiul Alam has also reaffirmed Bangladesh’s commitment to the UN target of halving road deaths and serious injuries by 2030.
For now, the country enters another Road Safety Day with thousands of lives lost, longstanding recommendations awaiting implementation and another deadly crash exposing the dangers on its highways.

item.title: Man beaten to death at Dhaka hospital over child theft suspicion
item.description:
A 41-year-old man was beaten to death at Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital in Dhaka on suspicion of being a child kidnapper.
The incident took place in front of the hospital’s children’s ward around 11pm on Wednesday. Police have detained a man in connection with the incident.
Police said Md Alam Sheikh was loitering in front of the children’s ward when relatives of children receiving treatment there became suspicious of him and questioned his presence at the hospital.
As he allegedly failed to provide a satisfactory explanation, several people dragged him downstairs and beat him, leaving him critically injured. He died early Thursday.
Police said they went to the scene after receiving an alert through the national emergency service 999. Alam’s identity was later confirmed through fingerprint verification.
He was from Natore. Police have contacted his family members, who are on their way to Dhaka.
Deputy Commissioner of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s Tejgaon Division, Ibne Mizan said the body had been sent to the morgue of Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College for an autopsy.
He said one person had been detained in connection with the incident. He added that legal action will be taken if the victim’s family files a complaint with the police.

item.title: Shibir says youth detained over PM comment is not a member
item.description:
Islami Chhatra Shibir has denied that Abu Bakar Siddique, 22, detained over a Facebook comment about Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s visit to Rajshahi, is a member of the organization.
Imran Nazir, president of the Rajshahi metropolitan unit of Islami Chhatra Shibir, said: “There is an attempt to put the blame on Shibir whenever something happens. But Abu Bakar Siddique is not one of our members.”
Abu Bakar was detained on Wednesday afternoon at his maternal uncle’s house in Gholharia village in Hatrāmchandrapur, Paba upazila, Rajshahi. His father, Ainal Haque, was also detained during the operation. Both are now in the custody of the Detective Branch (DB) of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP).
Chandrima police station Officer-in-Charge Monirul Islam said police had found no information indicating whether Abu Bakar had previously been arrested or whether any case had been filed against him. His political affiliation was also unknown, he added.
Mahmud Hasan Limon, president of the Chhatra Dal unit at Rajshahi New Government Degree College, said: “I heard from people in the administration that Abu Bakar used to be involved with the Chhatra League. Now, apparently, he is involved with Chhatra Shibir. But I have not seen anything at the college. We did not really know him.”
Shariful Islam, an assistant professor in the History Department of Rajshahi New Government Degree College, said Abu Bakar was a regular student who had taken his first-year final examinations, although the results had not yet been published. He said he had not observed any misconduct by Abu Bakar at the college.
After learning about the Facebook comment, Shariful Islam spoke to several students. According to him, they said Abu Bakar’s father had previously supported the Awami League but had been associating with Jamaat-e-Islami since August 5.
Shariful Islam also said he had heard that Abu Bakar had been involved with the Bangladesh Chhatra League through his family, although he had not observed any such involvement at the college.
The Facebook comment appeared under a photograph of the prime minister posted by a page named “The Beauty of Rajshahi.” The account, bearing the name Abu Bakar Siddique, commented: “What a great opportunity. Only a sniper was missing.”
During his visit to Rajshahi on Tuesday, Tarique Rahman traveled on a Rajshahi University of Engineering and Technology (RUET) bus from the airport to Madrasa Maidan and then to Dharmasabha before returning to the airport. Large numbers of people lined both sides of the road to greet him, and he responded to their greetings.
Following the comment, law enforcement agencies launched an operation to identify the account holder.
According to local residents, a team from the Cyber Crime Unit of Rajshahi Metropolitan Police and Chandrima police station went to Abu Bakar’s house at around 2pm on Wednesday. He was not there, and his family members did not disclose his whereabouts.
At around 4pm, a team from SRB-5 arrived at the house in plain clothes. Unable to find Abu Bakar, the team detained his father for questioning. Ainal Haque subsequently told them that his son was staying at his maternal uncle’s house in Gholharia village.
SRB-5 members then took Ainal Haque to the house and detained Abu Bakar. A mobile phone used by the family was seized, and both were subsequently handed over to the DMP’s Detective Branch.
SRB-5 Commander Lieutenant Colonel Faisal Ishtiaq confirmed the handover, saying: “We have handed both of them over to the DB. They will provide further details about the matter later.”
Abu Bakar lives in the Kechuatail area under Chandrima police station in Rajshahi city. His father, a farmer, has 4 children, with Abu Bakar being the eldest.
On Thursday morning, Monirul Islam searched Abu Bakar’s house. After nearly an hour, police found no evidence worth seizing apart from the packaging of a pen drive.
Police also attempted to recover Abu Bakar’s laptop, but family members said he neither used nor owned one.

item.title: Six law enforcers injured as gunfire targets Sajek tourist convoy
item.description:
Six members of law enforcement agencies were injured in an attack on a tourist convoy amid a road blockade on the Sajek-Baghaihat road in Rangamati’s Baghaichhari upazila on Thursday morning.
The incident occurred in the Ujobaazar area, prompting the army and police to evacuate the tourists to safety.
Rangamati Superintendent of Police Muhammad Abdur Rakib disclosed the details at a press conference at his office around 2:00pm on Thursday.
He said the Sajek Gano Odhikar Rokkha Committee and the Sajek Karbari Association had enforced a road blockade from October 11 to 15. The programme was suspended from October 16 to 21 for Durga Puja, with plans to resume it thereafter.
The blockade left 2,933 tourists stranded in Sajek, the SP said.
To ensure their safe return, a convoy of tourist vehicles left Sajek around 9:00am on Thursday under the security escort of the Bangladesh army and police.
When the convoy reached Ujobaazar around 10:00am, law enforcement personnel held talks with the protesters to facilitate the tourists’ safe passage. The protesters then hurled bricks and stones at the security personnel, injuring six members, Abdur Rakib said.
The protesters were subsequently removed from the road, allowing the convoy to proceed.
Based on intelligence reports, authorities later learned that an armed group affiliated with the United People’s Democratic Front (UPDF) had opened fire targeting the tourist convoy, the SP said.
Law enforcement personnel returned fire to protect the tourists and safeguard public property, he added.
Intermittent exchanges of gunfire between the armed group and law enforcement personnel continued even after the tourists had been moved to safety.
The gunfight lasted from around 11:00am to 1:00pm, after which the situation came under control, Abdur Rakib said.
Md Jasim Uddin, a Mahindra driver on the Sajek route, said they left Sajek around 9:00am under a security escort.
“They were stopped by protesters at Ujobaazar around 10:00am and remained stranded for about 40 minutes. Later, security personnel dispersed the protesters using batons, allowing us to continue,” he said.
He said they reached Khagrachhari around 12:40pm.
Rahul Chakma John, organising secretary of the Sajek Cottage and Resort Owners Association, said around 3,000 tourists had returned from Sajek to Khagrachhari.
On Wednesday, Sajek Karbari Association President Natun Joy Chakma and Sajek Gano Odhikar Rokkha Committee Convener Babudhan Chakma announced in a joint statement that an indefinite road blockade would resume from Thursday.
The organisations alleged that armed members of the Parbatya Chattagram Jana-Samhati Samiti (JSS-Santu Larma) were active in different parts of Sajek.
They also alleged that the armed members had threatened and intimidated local residents, forced some people to leave their homes and seized mobile phones from villagers.
As a result, ordinary Jum farmers were unable to tend to their gardens, the organisations claimed.
They said the blockade would continue until the alleged armed members were removed from the area and measures were taken to ensure the safety and security of local residents.
Natun Joy Chakma said talks were underway with law enforcement agencies but they would not withdraw the blockade unless their three demands were addressed.
He said the blockade had been suspended from October 16 to 21 in observance of Durga Puja.
However, he alleged that the administration did not hold any discussions with them during that period.
He said tourists staying in Sajek had also been given sufficient time to leave, prompting them to resume the blockade as announced.
The indefinite blockade on the Sajek Road was initially launched on October 11 and suspended from October 16 to 21 for Durga Puja. With the blockade resuming on Thursday, concerns have resurfaced over tourist movement and security in Sajek.
According to local accounts, while the Bangladesh Army was escorting around 3,000 stranded tourists to safety, armed members of the United People’s Democratic Front (UPDF), along with women participating in the blockade, allegedly hurled bricks and stones at the tourists in the Gongaram Bazar area of Sajek.
The incident occurred as the tourists were being escorted out of the area amid the ongoing blockade.

item.title: Fire at Rangpur Medical College Hospital injures 40 patients
item.description:
At least 40 patients and their relatives were injured while rushing to evacuate Rangpur Medical College Hospital after a fire broke out due to a short circuit on Thursday morning.
The fire originated from a switchboard near the administrative section of the hospital’s electrical control room on the ground floor around 6:15am.
Firefighters quickly brought the blaze under control, but the hospital remained without electricity for six hours, triggering panic among patients and their attendants.
The power outage disrupted medical services, forcing the suspension of emergency surgeries and other treatments. Although partial power was restored to several wards after prolonged efforts, the nephrology, cardiology, gynaecology and kidney dialysis wards remained without electricity.
According to patients, hospital authorities and fire service officials, panic spread throughout the hospital as patients and their relatives rushed to leave the building. Those staying in wards on the second to fifth floors hurried down the stairs, with many falling and sustaining injuries. At least 40 people were injured in falls during the rush to evacuate the hospital.
As of 4pm, the offices of the hospital director, cardiology department, pathology ward, dermatology and venereology ward, kidney dialysis ward and nephrology ward remained without electricity, leaving patients struggling in the intense heat.
During a visit to the hospital, patients described the chaos surrounding the evacuation.
Shafiul Alam, a kidney patient receiving treatment in the second-floor nephrology ward, was being carried downstairs when his two nephews fell and were injured. Shafiul was also hurt in the incident.
At least 15 patients in the ward were injured while rushing downstairs, with some reportedly trampled in the crowd.
Several infants were also injured as patients and their attendants rushed down the stairs from the third-floor gynaecology ward with newborns.
Mamtaz Begum, a patient in the gynaecology ward, said her baby girl was born five days ago. After hearing about the fire, she rushed downstairs with her newborn and was injured during the evacuation.
Many others used the emergency exit stairs to escape, with several sustaining injuries in the rush.
Deputy Director of Rangpur Medical College Hospital Dr Md Abdul Mokaddem said the fire was caused by a short circuit.
“Efforts are underway to restore electricity to all wards,” he said.
