The Climate Watch to deploy eight journalists at COP31
item.description:
As global attention turns to the 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, Bangladeshi news organization The Climate Watch is preparing to bring South Asia’s climate struggles, demands and stories to the international stage.
Officially launched on November 3, 2024, The Climate Watch will deploy 8 journalists from Bangladesh, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka to cover the UN climate summit, scheduled for November 9-20. The team comprises 5 full-time journalists and 3 regional contributors, marking the publication’s largest international reporting operation to date.
While financial pressures have forced several established Western news organizations to reduce specialized reporting, The Climate Watch is expanding cross-border collaboration and investing in environmental journalism.
Founded in 2022 by award-winning Bangladeshi environmental journalist Shamsuddin Illius, The Climate Watch has developed into a regional platform connecting approximately 100 climate and environmental journalists.
“We are striving to become a voice for South Asia in global climate negotiations. Our countries are among the most vulnerable to climate change, and it is essential that we tell our own stories rather than rely solely on others to tell them for us,” Executive Editor Md Ibrahim Khalilullah said.
At COP31, its journalists will examine climate finance, adaptation, loss and damage, energy transition, biodiversity, displacement and climate justice, linking diplomatic negotiations to the everyday experiences of vulnerable communities.
The publication is also exploring collaborations with Shakti Foundation, Young Power in Social Action (YPSA) and Change Initiative to strengthen its coverage.
The Climate Watch’s investigations have examined deforestation, industrial expansion, groundwater depletion and environmental governance. An investigation into forest destruction around Chittagong’s National Special Economic Zone documented biodiversity losses, with its findings subsequently cited in public-interest litigation.
Its reporting has received international references from The Guardian, The Diplomat, Mongabay, The New Humanitarian and Fiji Sun, alongside academic citations involving Columbia University’s Climate School and the National University of Singapore.
Through its Birds in Climate Crisis initiative, the publication is producing 100 short documentaries on threatened birds, habitat destruction and changing ecosystems.
The outlet also contributed to Dark Side of the Boom, an Earth Journalism Network-coordinated investigation involving 14 newsrooms across 11 countries that examined the environmental consequences of digital infrastructure.
The collaboration received a 2026 Covering Climate Now Journalism Award, a Society of Publishers in Asia (SOPA) environmental reporting award and a special citation associated with the Osborn Elliott Prize.
Having covered COP28, COP29, COP30 and Bonn’s SB64 negotiations, The Climate Watch is also preparing to report on biodiversity negotiations at COP17 in Armenia.
Alongside its reporting, the organization conducts journalist training and pre-COP fellowships with the Center for Participatory Research and Development.
For the relatively young newsroom operating from climate-vulnerable Bangladesh, the COP31 deployment represents an effort to shift South Asia’s position in the global climate conversation from a region whose suffering is frequently reported by others to one increasingly telling its own stories.

item.title: Son of Myanmar’s Suu Kyi says had first call in five years
item.description:
The son of Myanmar’s Aung San Suu Kyi said he spoke Thursday to the detained former democratic leader for the first time in more than five years.
“Today, I was finally able to speak with my mother, Daw Aung San Suu Kyi, after more than five years. Hearing her voice again means more than words can express,” Kim Aris said in a post on Facebook.
Suu Kyi is under house arrest in the capital, Naypyidaw, according to Myanmar authorities, where she has been sequestered since being unseated in a 2021 military coup.
AFP could not immediately reach Aris -- who lives in the United Kingdom -- and it was not clear how he spoke to his mother, who won the 1991 Nobel Peace Prize for efforts to bring democracy to Myanmar.
However, he posted images accompanying his Facebook post which appeared to show him standing outside the Myanmar embassy in London.
“I am deeply grateful to everyone who has stood by my mother and me. I believe your voices helped make this moment possible,” Aris wrote.
“But my mother is 81 and remains unjustly detained. One conversation is not regular family access.”
Myanmar’s military held Suu Kyi in almost total seclusion for five years following the February 2021 coup, which ended a tentative decade-long experiment with democracy.
But in recent months authorities have increasingly advertised the loosening of her detention and published photographs of her taking private meetings, as supporters have demanded “proof of life” of the octogenarian.
On Monday, authorities in Myanmar said she received a package from Britain’s King Charles III, including two books about soil and a “sealed diplomatic communication” from the monarch.
Buckingham Palace did not comment on the contents of the communication.
Myanmar authorities said Suu Kyi was moved from a prison in Naypyidaw to house arrest in April, and in August they published images of her meeting the nation’s Red Cross representative.
After ruling Myanmar as military chief for five years, Min Aung Hlaing -- who ousted Suu Kyi in the 2021 coup -- was earlier this year installed as civilian president.
Analysts describe the election putting him in elected office as a charade, and say he may be loosening restrictions on Suu Kyi in a bid to court international legitimacy.

item.title: Matthew McConaughey sparks 2028 presidential speculation with call for independent candidates
item.description:
Oscar-winning actor Matthew McConaughey has reignited speculation about a possible run for the US presidency in 2028 after releasing a six-minute video urging voters to give independent candidates a greater role in American politics.
Released on October 18, ahead of the 2026 midterm elections, the video encourages voters to take independent candidates seriously rather than dismiss them as protest candidates or spoilers. McConaughey, however, did not announce any plans to run for office or endorse a candidate or political party.
“Independent does not mean you’re middle of the road. Independent is the original road,” he said, presenting political independence as an alternative to the traditional Republican-Democratic divide.
According to The Telegraph, McConaughey also argued that independently elected representatives could encourage compromise in a closely divided Congress and hold both major parties accountable. He urged voters to examine candidates’ positions and determine whether their views aligned with their own beliefs.
The video has prompted renewed discussion about the actor’s political ambitions, although McConaughey has neither confirmed nor ruled out a presidential bid.
His potential entry into politics has been a subject of speculation for several years. In 2021, he considered running for governor of Texas but ultimately decided against entering the race. In July 2024, he described himself as being on a “learning tour” while exploring the possibility of public office. He later said he would not pursue a political campaign at that time.
McConaughey’s latest remarks have also attracted criticism from commentators and social media users who questioned whether independent candidates could split the vote and influence closely contested elections.
The discussion comes amid growing identification with political independence in the United States. According to Gallup, 45% of Americans identified as political independents in 2025, a record high at the time.
For now, McConaughey’s video has renewed questions about his political future, but the actor has yet to announce any plans to enter the 2028 presidential race.

item.title: Gazipur’s ‘Ulka cinema hall’ to shut down in November
item.description:
Ulka, a long-running single-screen cinema hall at Gazipur Chowrasta, is set to close permanently in November as falling attendance, mounting losses and rising operating costs make it increasingly difficult to keep the business afloat.
Mohammad Rafiq Uddin, managing director of the cinema hall, confirmed the decision, saying ticket sales from current releases are no longer sufficient to cover even electricity bills.
“The hall is struggling to survive. We are incurring losses continuously. The films currently screening cannot even cover the electricity bill,” he said.
Rafiq Uddin said films with compelling stories and established stars continue to attract audiences. However, relying on releases concentrated around the two Eid festivals is not enough to sustain a cinema hall throughout the year.
He pointed to the audience response to films starring Shakib Khan, suggesting that more releases featuring the actor outside the Eid seasons could help single-screen cinemas remain viable.
Unusually high electricity bills have added to the financial strain, according to Rafiq Uddin. With operating expenses becoming increasingly difficult to manage, the owners have decided to shut down rather than continue accumulating losses.
Audience numbers have also declined sharply, hall authorities said. Some screenings attract only a handful of moviegoers, leaving ticket revenue insufficient to cover staff salaries and routine operating expenses.
The planned closure comes as Kamruzzaman’s Sneher Bondhon is screening at the venue. Starring Joy Chowdhury and Mou Khan, the film was released in 14 cinemas on October 16.
Its promotional campaign included appearances on an open-roof bus in Dhaka. However, reports from the exhibition circuit indicate that the film has struggled to attract audiences.
The closure will further narrow cinema-going options in Gazipur, an industrial district with a large working population. Local industry sources said four cinemas were operating in the district around a year to 18 months ago.
Once Ulka closes, only Barsha and Jhumur cinemas are expected to remain open in the district. Both venues are reportedly facing financial difficulties, raising further concerns about the future of single-screen cinema in the area.
Ulka’s shutdown highlights the challenges facing traditional cinema halls in Bangladesh, where declining attendance and rising operating costs continue to put pressure on venues that have long provided relatively affordable big-screen entertainment.

item.title: Chiranjit Biswas wins ‘Best Male Actor’ at Tasveer Film Festival

item.title: Jubo Dal leader hacked to death in Narayanganj
item.description:
A Jubo Dal leader was hacked to death in Sonargaon upazila of Narayanganj on Wednesday night.
The incident took place in the Char Kishoreganj area around 10pm, said Sonargaon police station Officer-in-Charge Mohammad Abdul Barek.
The deceased, Fakir Zahir Rahman, 40, was the son of Abdur Rahman of Kalapaharia union in neighbouring Araihazar upazila. He was a joint convener of the upazila Jubo Dal and president of the union unit of the organization.
The OC told the media that although Zahir was originally from Araihazar, he had been living in a rented house in Munshiganj Sadar for several years. He also owned a pharmacy in Char Kishoreganj.
Citing preliminary findings, the OC said: “As he did every day, he was returning home after closing his pharmacy on Wednesday night. On the way, unidentified assailants hacked him with sharp weapons and left him injured on the road.”
Local residents later rescued him and took him to Munshiganj General Hospital, where he died while undergoing treatment.
The police official said the body was recovered and sent to the morgue of Narayanganj General Hospital for an autopsy.
The identities of those involved and the motive behind the killing were not immediately known. Police are investigating the incident, the OC added.

item.title: Bangladesh improves in rule of law index but trails several African nations
item.description:
Bangladesh has made a slight improvement in its overall rule of law score but continues to rank below several African countries, including Kenya, Zimbabwe and Nigeria, according to the Rule of Law Index 2026 released on Wednesday.
Bangladesh ranked 123rd among 143 countries and jurisdictions in the World Justice Project (WJP) index, behind Zimbabwe (122nd), Nigeria (120th), Sierra Leone (110th), Liberia (103rd), Kenya (100th) and Ghana (62nd).
Its score increased by 0.6% to 0.393 out of 1, up from 0.391 in 2025, making Bangladesh the world's 15th-biggest improver and South Asia's top gainer. Its ranking improved by two places from 125th, although its score remained below the global average of 0.55.
The index assesses countries across eight factors: constraints on government powers, absence of corruption, open government, fundamental rights, order and security, regulatory enforcement, civil justice and criminal justice.
Bangladesh improved in only three factors — constraints on government powers, absence of corruption and regulatory enforcement — while its performance declined in the other five.
Fundamental rights remained the country's weakest area, with Bangladesh ranking 133rd and scoring 0.30, placing it among the 11 lowest-ranked countries.
The indicator assesses the protection of fundamental human rights under international law. Civil justice was the second-weakest area, with Bangladesh ranking 132nd and scoring 0.36. The indicator measures access to and the effectiveness of the civil justice system in resolving grievances.
Bangladesh ranked 124th in regulatory enforcement, with a score of 0.40, and 117th in criminal justice, scoring 0.32. In the absence of corruption category, which measures bribery, improper influence and the misappropriation of public resources, it ranked 113th with a score of 0.35.
The country ranked 111th in constraints on government powers, which measures accountability under the law, with a score of 0.38.
Open government was Bangladesh's highest-ranked factor at 106th, with a score of 0.41. It assesses government transparency, accountability mechanisms and public participation in policy deliberations.
Bangladesh ranked 107th in order and security, scoring 0.63. The factor measures how effectively a society protects individuals and property.
Despite the annual improvement, Bangladesh's overall rule of law score declined by 0.8% between 2021 and 2026, falling from 0.40 to around 0.39, according to the WJP's country profile.
Six of the index's eight factors deteriorated over the five-year period. Civil justice recorded the sharpest decline at 4.2%, followed by open government at 2.8%, fundamental rights at 1.5%, regulatory enforcement at 0.9%, criminal justice at 0.7% and absence of corruption at 0.2%.
Constraints on government powers and order and security improved by 2.3% and 0.6%, respectively.
Human rights activist and Supreme Court lawyer Barrister Jyotirmoy Barua attributed the deterioration partly to the worsening law and order situation.
"We had expected that an elected government would be able to turn things around to some extent, as the interim government had failed to maintain or restore control over the law and order situation," he said.
"However, the elected government has been trying to bring the entire situation under control at once, and the pressure associated with this has contributed to instability. Law enforcement is also closely linked to the justice system, and our overall performance in these areas has deteriorated," he added.
Nepal remained South Asia's top performer, ranking 71st globally with a score of 0.52, followed by Sri Lanka at 74th and India at 88th. Bangladesh ranked ahead of only Pakistan (131st) and Afghanistan (142nd) in the region.
Denmark topped the 2026 index, followed by Norway, Finland, Sweden and Luxembourg. Venezuela ranked last, preceded by Afghanistan, Haiti, Cambodia and Nicaragua.
The index drew on data from more than 215,000 households and 3,400 surveys of legal practitioners and experts across 143 countries and jurisdictions. The data were collected between February and August 2026.
The WJP highlighted the links between the rule of law and economic prosperity. Countries with GDP per capita above the global average of $14,406 scored at least 0.68 on the index, while those with inflation below the global median of 3.23% scored at least 0.60. The findings indicate an association between the rule of law, price stability and economic performance.

item.title: Fire destroys mosque, warehouses, shops in Gazipur
item.description:
A fire destroyed a mosque, several shops and warehouses in Sreepur, Gazipur, early Thursday.
The blaze broke out around 3:30am at the Sakhawat and Akhtar market complex in the No 2 C&B Bazar area of Channapara, within Sreepur municipality.
Four Fire Service units brought the fire under control after nearly two hours of efforts.
The fire gutted Rafiqul Islam’s sanitary goods shop, Falan Miah’s poultry shop, Shafiq’s textile scrap (jhut) and cotton warehouses, a scrap-metal shop and Baitul Jannat Jame Mosque.
Nurul Karim, station officer at Maona Fire Service, said they received information about the fire at 3:55am. Two units from the Maona Fire Service rushed to the scene and began efforts to extinguish the blaze.
As the fire spread rapidly, another unit from Sreepur Fire Station and a unit from Rajendrapur Modern Fire Station joined the operation.
The four units brought the fire under control at 5:48am, after nearly two hours of efforts.
No casualties have been reported.
The cause of the fire and the extent of the damage will be determined following an investigation, the fire service official said.

item.title: Dhaka ranks 7th among world’s most polluted cities
item.description:
Dhaka ranked 7th among the world's most polluted cities on Thursday morning, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 157 at 9:20am.
The air quality was classified as "unhealthy", meaning the concentration of pollutants in the air had reached a level that could pose health risks to the general population, according to the AQI scale.
Lahore in Pakistan ranked first with an AQI score of 294, while Delhi in India ranked second with a score of 235, followed by Jakarta in Indonesia third place with an AQI score of 174.
According to AQI standards, a reading between 101 and 150 is considered "unhealthy for sensitive groups", while 151 to 200 is classified as "unhealthy". A reading between 201 and 300 is considered "very unhealthy", while levels above 301 are deemed "hazardous", posing serious health risks.
The AQI provides daily updates on air quality, indicating how clean or polluted the air is and highlighting potential health impacts.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five major pollutants: particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulfur dioxide (SO2) and ozone.
Dhaka has long struggled with air pollution, with air quality typically deteriorating during winter and improving during the monsoon season.
The World Health Organization estimates that air pollution causes around seven million deaths globally each year, mainly from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,205 as one die in 24 hours
item.description:
One child died with measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours ending at 8am on Wednesday, bringing the country’s combined tally of confirmed and suspected measles-related deaths to 1,205 this year.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) classified the latest fatality as the suspected measles death.
With this, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 1,101, while confirmed deaths from measles have remained the same at 104.
A total of 997 new suspected measles cases were reported during the 24-hour period, taking the cumulative number of suspected cases nationwide to 216,765.
Meanwhile, 13 new confirmed measles cases were recorded, pushing laboratory-confirmed infections to 23,212.
Since March 15 this year, a total of 192,695 patients with suspected measles have been hospitalised across the country, of whom 185,110 have recovered, according to the DGHS.

item.title: Harmony: Diplomatic community joins Durga Puja celebrations in Bangladesh
item.description:
Members of the diplomatic community in Bangladesh joined Durga Puja celebrations at temples and pandals in Dhaka and beyond, extending greetings to the Hindu community and highlighting the country’s rich cultural heritage, religious diversity and spirit of communal harmony.
The Hindu community says participation of members of the diplomatic community in this year’s festivities underscored the importance of cultural engagement and respect for religious diversity in Bangladesh, where festivals play a vital role in strengthening social bonds and promoting understanding among communities.
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has said all citizens of Bangladesh enjoy equal rights regardless of their religious identity, stressing that being Bangladeshi matters more than belonging to a majority or minority community.
“Majority or minority is not the issue. The only thing that matters is that you are Bangladeshi,” he said while visiting the JM Sen Hall puja mandap in the port city on the occasion of Durga Puja on Tuesday, noting that people of different faiths fought together in the 1971 War of Liberation without distinguishing between Muslims, Hindus, Buddhists and Christians.
Indian High Commissioner to Bangladesh Dinesh Trivedi took part in celebrations at several venues across the capital, including Jagannath Hall at the University of Dhaka, Dhakeshwari National Temple, Ramna Kali Mandir and the Gulshan-Banani Sarbajanin Puja Foundation.
He exchanged greetings with devotees, students and organisers, sharing in the festive spirit of the occasion. Sharadiya Durga Puja concludes today (Wednesday) with Bijoya Dashami.

Deputy High Commissioner Pawan Badhe also attended the Aarti Competition at Dhakeshwari Temple, where performers of different age groups presented the traditional Dhanuchi dance to the rhythmic beats of the dhak.
Other diplomatic missions also conveyed their greetings and joined the festivities, celebrating the traditions and cultural vibrancy of Bangladesh’s Hindu community.
US Ambassador to Bangladesh Brent T. Christensen joined the celebrations at Sarbajanin Puja Mandap in Amlapara, sharing the warmth, colour and joy of the festivities with members of the Hindu community. He extended his greetings in Bengali, saying, “Sobaike Sharadiya Subeccha.”
Ambassador of Switzerland to Bangladesh Reto Renggli attended Durga Puja celebrations at the Kumudini Welfare Trust in Tangail, describing the festival as an important reflection of Bangladesh’s rich social, cultural and religious diversity.
The Royal Norwegian Embassy in Dhaka wished everyone a happy Durga Puja, expressing hope that the festival would serve as a reminder of the values of peace, harmony, inclusiveness and mutual respect that bring communities together.
“As people across Bangladesh come together to celebrate Durga Puja, we send our warmest wishes to all and hope the festival serves as a reminder of the values of peace, harmony, inclusiveness, and respect that bring communities together,” said the Embassy.
Norwegian Ambassador Håkon Arald Gulbrandsen, High Commissioner of Canada Ajit Singh, Ambassador of Sweden Nicolas Weeks and the Embassy colleagues joined the festivities and experienced the warmth, traditions, and vibrant cultural heritage that make Durga Puja such a special occasion. “May this festive season bring joy, peace, and prosperity to all.”
Swedish Ambassador Nicolas Weeks attended the Durga Puja celebrations in Banani, Dhaka, offering his greetings to the community.
"Wishing everyone a very Happy Durga Puja! In the spirit of inclusion, peace, and harmony, may this festival bring happiness and prosperity to all,” Ambassador Weeks said.
The Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands, meanwhile, extended its warm wishes to the Hindu community in Bangladesh and around the world, hoping the festival would bring peace, happiness, harmony and prosperity.
The Embassy of France in Bangladesh also wished everyone celebrating a joyful and peaceful Durga Puja.
The Australian High Commission in Dhaka said they had the privilege of joining festivities across the country and experiencing the warmth and hospitality that make this celebration so special.
The High Commission said Durga Puja is a reflection of the power of culture to bring people together and strengthen connections across communities.
Durga Puja, the largest religious festival of Bangladesh’s Hindu community, is marked by days of worship, cultural performances and community gatherings at temples and temporary pandals across the country.
Beyond its religious significance, the festival offers an opportunity for people from different backgrounds to come together in a shared celebration of culture, tradition and coexistence.

item.title: Bride tortured, killed over wedding gifts in Sherpur
item.description:
A 20-year-old newlywed woman died at her husband’s home in Sherpur’s Nalitabari upazila early Wednesday, just six days after her marriage.
The deceased, Lima Akter, died at her husband’s home in Paikhatla village of Rupnarayankura union in the early hours of October 21.
Lima’s family alleged that she was tortured and killed over her in-laws’ dissatisfaction with the gifts and other items brought from her parental home for the wedding, reports Bangla Tribun.
Police detained her husband, Ekramul Haque, 22, and mother-in-law, Farida Begum, 50, for questioning.
Lima was the daughter of Saidul Islam of Majhiyail village in Dhara union of Mymensingh’s Haluaghat upazila. She married Ekramul on October 15 in a family-arranged ceremony, with the denmohor set at Tk1.7 lakh.
According to family members, Lima visited her parents’ home with her husband on Sunday and returned to her in-laws’ house on Tuesday afternoon.
Relatives said a dispute broke out between the couple after Lima’s in-laws expressed dissatisfaction with the gifts and other items brought from her parents’ home.
Lima’s family alleged that she was tortured at her in-laws’ house that night.
Around 3:00am, Ekramul called Lima’s brother-in-law, saying she had fallen ill. About an hour later, her in-laws took her to Nalitabari Upazila Health Complex, where doctors declared her dead.
Lima’s relatives said they noticed injury marks on her body at the hospital and informed police.
Police went to the hospital, took custody of the body and sent it for the necessary legal procedures.
Dr Fahad Rahman, resident medical officer at Nalitabari Upazila Health Complex, said Lima had died before she was brought to the hospital.
Lima’s relatives alleged that the dispute over the gifts escalated and that she was physically assaulted and strangled to death.
However, the exact cause of her death has not yet been established and will be determined through investigation and autopsy.
Ekramul, however, denied the allegations.
He said he went to sleep at night and woke up to find the door of their room open. He then went outside and found Lima hanging by her scarf from the sunshade of a nearby semi-pucca house.
He claimed that he brought her down and informed his brother about the incident.
Nalitabari police Sub-Inspector Abdul Hannan said injury marks were found on the victim’s body. Her husband, Ekramul Haque, and mother-in-law, Farida Begum, have been detained for questioning in connection with the incident.
The body has been sent to the Sherpur morgue for an autopsy to determine the exact cause of death.
Police said further details about the cause of death will be known after the autopsy report is received and the investigation is completed.

item.title: Dilip Agarwala placed on 4-day remand in July attempted murder case
item.description:
A Dhaka court on Wednesday placed Diamond World Managing Director Dilip Kumar Agarwala on a four-day remand in a case over an armed attack on protesters and the shooting of Abdur Zabbar in the Anti-Discrimination Student Movement in capital’s Uttara area in August 2024.
The court also granted him a one-day remand on Tuesday in a separate money laundering case filed with Gulshan Police.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Sarah Farzana Haque passed the order on Wednesday after hearing arguments from both sides.
Investigation officer and Uttara West police Sub-Inspector Md Sumon Mia produced Agarwala before the court and sought a 10-day remand for questioning.
State prosecutor Shamsuddoha Sumon argued in favour of the remand, alleging that Agarwala had financed the Awami League and served as a central leader of the party. He further alleged that Agarwala had worked to thwart the student movement and was involved in shooting protesters.
Defence lawyer Anwarul Kabir Babul opposed the remand and sought bail, arguing that Agarwala was abroad at the time of the incident and could not, therefore, have been involved.
The lawyer also said Agarwala had resigned from the Awami League five years earlier. He questioned the need for remand, noting that the case had been under investigation for a year without any evidence of Agarwala’s involvement being established.
After hearing both sides, the court granted a four-day remand.
According to the case documents, students and members of the public gathered peacefully beside BNS Centre on the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway in the Uttara West Police Station area on August 5, 2024, during the Anti-Discrimination Student Movement.
The accused allegedly launched an armed attack on the protesters and opened indiscriminate fire on the instructions of the prime accused and others.
A protester, identified as Abdur Jabbar in the case, was shot and sustained severe injuries to the lower part of his spine. He received prolonged treatment at Dhaka Medical College Hospital before filing the case with Uttara West Police Station on March 27, 2025, after recovering.
In the remand petition, the investigation officer said preliminary evidence suggested that Agarwala had been present at the scene and participated in the attack in collusion with other accused.
The officer said Agarwala needed to be interrogated to uncover the circumstances of the incident, recover the firearms allegedly used in the attack, identify other suspects and facilitate their arrest.
Agarwala is listed as the 31st accused in the case.
Earlier on Tuesday, a court granted him a one-day remand in a separate money laundering case involving allegations of trading gold and diamonds worth around Tk6,781.9 crore through smuggling.
Detective Branch (DB) police arrested him from the capital’s Gulshan area on October 19 in connection with that case.

item.title: Death toll from Sudan army strike in disputed territory rises to 153
item.description:
The death toll from a drone strike Monday on a market in an area disputed between Sudan and South Sudan has risen to 153 and is likely even higher, a local official told AFP on Wednesday.
Authorities in Abyei district said the strike on the Amiet market involved the use of multiple munitions and was carried out by the Sudanese army.
“The number of casualties is 153 and it may increase any time from now because some victims burned to ashes and the rescuers are doing their best to gather all the bodies in Amiet Market,” said Yohana Akol, interim information minister for Abyei Special Administrative Area.
He said the victims included Sudanese, South Sudanese, Ethiopians and Somalis, and a further 19 have been hospitalized, with more on the way.
Images shared with AFP showed bombed-out buildings and vehicles.
“A swarm of drones was hovering over the Amiet Market and they bombed part of the market and surroundings and there were so many casualties,” a witness told AFP by phone, speaking on condition of anonymity for security reasons.
“Some of business places are still on fire and there were people burned beyond recognition inside,” the witness added.
Another witness said fuel depots were severely damaged.
On Sunday and Monday, strikes across Sudan killed more than 100 people. The country is in the grips of a brutal war between the regular army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) that began in April 2023.
Abyei district is claimed by both Sudan and South Sudan, which split from its northern neighbor in 2011 following decades of conflict.
Parts of the district are controlled by a faction of the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement-North (SPLM-N), a splinter from the organization that fought for Juba’s independence.
Juba’s foreign ministry said it had summoned the Sudanese ambassador over the attack, which it condemned “in the strongest terms possible.”
The United Nations also condemned the attacks, saying escalating drone strikes were “part of a deeply concerning pattern.”

item.title: Does Pakistan-Taliban conflict create a strategic opening for India?
item.description:
Pakistan and Afghanistan right now are locked in a cycle of escalating tension. Repeated border clashes have strained ties between the two nations.
The current round of tensions began in February 2026, when Pakistan launched strikes into Afghanistan targeting Taliban militants. At one point in March, Pakistan’s defense minister said the country was at “open war” with Afghanistan. Periodic bouts of violence have continued since then, with the latest Pakistani strikes targeting the Afghan Taliban’s “terrorist hubs” reported earlier in October.
At the heart of the dispute is Pakistan’s accusation that the Taliban authorities in Kabul allow the Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), a militant group, to target Pakistan from Afghan territory. Kabul denies providing the group with sanctuary.
As the two neighbors trade strikes, the escalating conflict “presents a significant diplomatic and strategic opportunity for India,” Shanthie Mariet D’Souza, an Afghanistan expert and founder of the India-based Mantraya Institute for Strategic Studies, told DW.
D’Souza argues the confrontation has weakened Pakistan’s traditional influence in Afghanistan and encouraged the Taliban to broaden its external relations.
“India can respond by expanding diplomatic engagement, humanitarian assistance, development projects and trade, while seeking assurances that Afghan territory will not be used by anti-India militant groups,” she said.
However, D’Souza cautioned against interpreting the opening as a fundamental realignment.
“There is no ideological alignment between India and the Taliban,” she said. Afghanistan under Taliban rule is likely to pursue a diversified foreign policy rather than align exclusively with New Delhi.
India also lacks the geographical advantages, economic leverage and security presence needed to replace Pakistan’s influence, she notes. “The scenario of the Taliban becoming a strategic ally remains far-fetched.”
Former Indian ambassador to Afghanistan Amar Sinha warned against viewing the conflict simply as an opportunity for New Delhi to gain at Pakistan’s expense.
“The issues have very little to do with India,” Sinha told DW, arguing that India was not seeking strategic advantage from the fighting. He also pointed to the consequences of Pakistan’s military actions for Afghan civilians.
“Yet the rupture has made Kabul’s search for alternative partners more pressing,” he added.
For India, that creates an opening, but not necessarily a strategic alignment, Sinha notes. The Taliban can seek Indian assistance while maintaining relations with China, Russia, Iran and Gulf states, preserving its autonomy rather than exchanging dependence on Pakistan for dependence on India.
Gautam Mukhopadhyaya, another former Indian ambassador to Afghanistan, sees the deterioration in relations between Pakistan and the Taliban as an opportunity for India to recover some of the strategic ground it lost when the Taliban returned to power in 2021.
“The crisis has allowed strategic openings for India,” Mukhopadhyaya told DW. He warned, however, that New Delhi’s own treatment of Afghans could undermine its efforts to build a durable relationship.
He pointed to restrictions affecting Afghans seeking Indian visas for education, scholarships, work and medical treatment.
“For all practical purposes, India’s security establishment treats Afghans as proxy Pakistanis and ‘terrorists’ by default,” he said.
Former Afghan partners had been left “disappointed, even bitter,” Mukhopadhyaya added. “A strategic relationship built on the sands of oppression is not a sound foundation.”
India has restored air freight links between Kabul and Delhi and between Kabul and Amritsar in northwestern India in December 2025.
Bilateral trade between India and Afghanistan stood at about $908 million (€807 million) in the 2025-26 fiscal year, while trade between Pakistan and Afghanistan fell sharply amid repeated border closures.
On October 14, Taliban Foreign Minister Amir Khan Muttaqi stressed the importance of relations with India during talks with Indian charge d’affaires Yatin Patel, signaling Kabul’s interest in expanding economic cooperation.
But air freight is expensive, and India cannot easily replace Pakistan as a transit route.
New Delhi has sought to use Iran’s Chabahar port to improve access to Afghanistan and Central Asia, but regional instability and complications surrounding Iran have constrained those ambitions.
D’Souza cautioned that “the ongoing conflict in Iran” limits India’s ability to use Chabahar as a crucial trade and connectivity hub.
Gulshan Sachdeva, a professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University specializing in Afghanistan and Eurasian connectivity, highlighted similar obstacles.
“In the last few decades, Islamabad has obstructed Kabul’s efforts to gain access to the vast Indian market. However, political instability in Afghanistan and sanctions on Iran have undermined these efforts,” Sachdeva told DW.
“Afghanistan’s potential as a connector between regional markets remains considerable, but the infrastructure and political conditions needed to realize it are far from assured,” he added.
Sachdeva also sees Russia and China as better positioned to shape Afghanistan’s wider economic integration. Alternative routes may become more attractive to India, but they are not commercially viable overnight.
Pakistan has portrayed arch-rival India’s growing engagement with the Taliban as a security threat. On October 7, Pakistani diplomat Muhammad Jawad Ajmal accused India at the United Nations of providing the Taliban with material and logistical support.
“Under the guise of humanitarian aid, they have been actively supporting the Taliban regime with material and logistical support for carrying out terrorist attacks against Pakistan,” Ajmal said.
The allegation reflects Islamabad’s position and has not been established as fact.
Pakistan has accused India of supporting the TTP and the Balochistan Liberation Army, a militant organization.
India rejects accusations of backing militant activity, while the Taliban denies allowing Afghan territory to be used for attacks against Pakistan.
Ayesha Siddiqa, a Pakistani expert on military and security affairs at King’s College London, offered a more nuanced assessment of Pakistan’s position.
“India has stepped into a space and is trying to exert its influence and feed anti-Pakistan groups intelligence,” she told DW.
Siddiqa added that Pakistan’s establishment continues to view the crisis through “a singular security lens.”
“Islamabad feels physically squeezed from both sides,” she said, adding that closer Kabul-New Delhi ties could create “a dangerous two-front security trap” for Pakistan.
India may gain more room to operate in Afghanistan as ties between Kabul and Islamabad deteriorate. But the Taliban is unlikely to put all its eggs in New Delhi’s basket.

item.title: Tourists urged to leave Sajek as road blockade resumes Thursday
item.description:
Tourists staying in Sajek have been urged to leave the area by Wednesday as the Sajek Gono Odhikar Rokkha Committee and Sajek Karbari Association have announced a fresh road blockade from Thursday over the non-implementation of their three-point demands.
The announcement was made in a joint statement issued around 4pm on Wednesday by Sajek Karbari Association President Notun Joy Chakma and Sajek Gono Odhikar Rokkha Committee Convener Babudhan Chakma.
The blockade had been suspended from Friday to Wednesday at the request of the Durga Puja celebration committees of Baghaichhari and Machalong markets to allow the Hindu community to celebrate its largest religious festival.
The two organizations initially enforced an indefinite road blockade on October 11. The programme was later relaxed twice following assurances from the administration.
However, the groups have announced a fresh blockade, saying their three-point demands remain unfulfilled.
According to the joint statement, emergency vehicles, including fire service vehicles, ambulances and hearse vans, will be exempt from the blockade. Vehicles carrying emergency medicine supplies and newspapers, as well as those used by journalists for news gathering, will also be allowed to pass.

item.title: Three Bangladeshis who fled Myanmar scam compound to return home Thursday
item.description:
Three Bangladeshis who fled a scam compound in Myanmar and took refuge in Thailand are scheduled to return home on Thursday.
They are expected to arrive in Dhaka at 4:20pm on US-Bangla Airlines flight BS-218, according to the scheduled itinerary.
The returnees are Md Saidur Rahman, Robiul and Md Sohel Rana.
Anirban Survivor Voice Foundation took the initiative to repatriate them following complaints from the victims and their families. On August 24, the organisation applied to the Wage Earners’ Welfare Board under the Ministry of Expatriates’ Welfare and Overseas Employment, seeking assistance in bringing them home.
In response, the board’s Director Md Saidur Rahman issued a letter instructing the first secretary (labour) at the Bangladesh Embassy in Bangkok to take the necessary steps.
The letter called for measures to secure the release and repatriation of eight Bangladeshis staying at a safe house under the referral mechanism of Thailand’s Mae Sot Immigration Office.
Of the eight, three are scheduled to return home on Thursday, while legal procedures are underway to repatriate the remaining five.

Three of a family critically burned in Tongi gas cylinder explosion
item.description:
Three members of the same family, including a woman and a teenage girl, suffered severe burn injuries in a gas cylinder explosion in Tongi, Gazipur, on Wednesday morning.
The victims were admitted to the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery in Dhaka, where their conditions were described as critical.
The incident occurred around 6am in an area near Cherag Ali Market under Tongi West police station.
One of the victims, Lalchan, 60, suffered burns to 95% of his body and is receiving treatment in the hospital's emergency department.
Tanisha, 16, a student, sustained burns to 86% of her body and has been admitted to the Female High Dependency Unit (FHDU). Nasima, 50, suffered burns to 85% of her body and is also receiving treatment in the emergency department.
Sultan Mahmud Sikdar, resident surgeon at the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery, said the victims' conditions were critical due to the extensive burns. Hospital staff were making every effort to save them.
Preliminary assessments suggest that the explosion occurred when accumulated gas from a leaking cylinder ignited.

item.title: PM Tarique returns to Dhaka after visiting puja mandaps in three divisions
item.description:
Tarique Rahman returned to Dhaka early Wednesday after visiting Sharadiya Durga Puja mandaps in Rangpur, Rajshahi and Chittagong.
He arrived at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport at 1:10am aboard a military aircraft.
He left Dhaka at 9am on Tuesday, Maha Navami, a significant day of the Durga Puja festival, to visit puja mandaps in the three divisions.
During the visits, he exchanged greetings with members of the Hindu community.
Devotees welcomed him warmly, expressing their joy through cultural performances.

item.title: Bijoya Dashami Wednesday as Durga Puja concludes with idol immersion
item.description:
Sharadiya Durga Puja, the largest religious festival of the Hindu community, concludes on Wednesday with the immersion of idols on the occasion of Bijoya Dashami.
After five days of rituals and festivities, Goddess Durga is set to return to her heavenly abode at Kailash, leaving devotees with a sense of melancholy at puja mandaps across the country.
Devotees have been gathering at puja mandaps since morning to mark Bijoya Dashami. As they bid farewell to the Goddess, they are offering prayers for peace, prosperity and well-being for their families, society and the nation.
According to schedules released by the Mahanagar Sarbajanin Puja Committee and Dhakeshwari National Temple authorities, the Dashami Bihita Puja and Darpan Bisarjan, the symbolic immersion of the deity’s reflection, are scheduled to be completed by 9:57am.
The day's key rituals include Devi Baran and Sindur Khela. Before the immersion, married women bid farewell to the Goddess by applying vermilion to her and offering sweets, praying for their husbands' longevity and the happiness, well-being and prosperity of their families.
They then apply vermilion, first touched to the Goddess's feet, to one another's foreheads and cheeks. The ritual is accompanied by dance, music and the exchange of sweets. Unmarried women and other devotees also join the festivities.
According to the schedule, Devi Baran is set to begin at 11:30am, followed by a voluntary blood donation program at noon.

Intern doctors at RMCH halt work over five-point demand
item.description:
Intern doctors at Rajshahi Medical College Hospital launched a 24-hour work stoppage at 8am on Wednesday, pressing for a five-point set of demands, including addressing shortages of medical supplies and improving security.
The work stoppage has disrupted medical services at the hospital, causing hardship for patients, many of whom have travelled from distant areas, and their relatives.
The protesting doctors said essential medicines and medical supplies were in short supply in the hospital’s inpatient wards. They also complained of difficulties caused by the unrestricted entry of patients’ relatives into the wards and alleged negligence by Ansar personnel responsible for security. They further claimed to have faced organized threats.
The interns said the hospital’s observation room and casualty department were currently non-functional, increasing the pressure on inpatient wards. They said limited staffing and inadequate medical supplies had made it difficult to provide proper care.
According to the protesters, the hospital administration had repeatedly assured them that the problems would be addressed but had taken no effective steps. They said the work stoppage was a last resort.
Dr S M Tapu, president of the Intern Doctors’ Society at Rajshahi Medical College Hospital, said a press conference would be held on Wednesday afternoon to outline the demands, explain the situation and announce their next course of action.

item.title: Dhaka ranks 9th among world’s most polluted cities
item.description:
Dhaka ranked 9th among the world's most polluted cities on Wednesday morning, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 162 at 10:05am.
The air quality was classified as "unhealthy", meaning the concentration of pollutants in the air had reached a level that could pose health risks to the general population, according to the AQI scale.
Lahore in Pakistan ranked first with an AQI score of 272, while Delhi in India ranked second with a score of 249, followed by Jakarta in Indonesia third place with an AQI score of 183.
According to AQI standards, a reading between 101 and 150 is considered "unhealthy for sensitive groups", while 151 to 200 is classified as "unhealthy". A reading between 201 and 300 is considered "very unhealthy", while levels above 301 are deemed "hazardous", posing serious health risks.
The AQI provides daily updates on air quality, indicating how clean or polluted the air is and highlighting potential health impacts.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five major pollutants: particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulfur dioxide (SO2) and ozone.
Dhaka has long struggled with air pollution, with air quality typically deteriorating during winter and improving during the monsoon season.
The World Health Organization estimates that air pollution causes around seven million deaths globally each year, mainly from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.

PSG late show downs Barca in Champions League, Liverpool fight back in 7-goal thriller
item.description:
Holders Paris Saint-Germain made it three wins from three in this season's Champions League, beating Barcelona 4-2 thanks to late goals from Vitinha and Fabian Ruiz on Tuesday, while Liverpool clinched a dramatic comeback victory over Villarreal.
Phil Foden scored a hat-trick as Manchester City thrashed AEK Athens 5-1, while there were also much-needed wins for Roma and Napoli.
PSG kept their place at the top of the league-phase table, but could yet count the cost of injuries suffered by Ousmane Dembele, Marquinhos and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia at the Parc des Princes.
"We don't feel superior to any team but we trust in ourselves, in everyone who starts and who comes off the bench," Paris midfielder Ruiz told Movistar. "There's still a long way to go."
Barcelona twice levelled against the two-time defending champions, but were ultimately well beaten as they slipped to their first defeat of the season.
"We tried to play how we want to play, we pressed them very high. There were a lot of fantastic things on show today," said Flick, whose team had won their previous 11 games in all competitions this term.
Kvaratskhelia hit the post, Dembele hobbled off and Ferran Torres was denied by Barca goalkeeper Joan Garcia in a fast-paced opening.
PSG took a deserved lead in the 38th minute as Desire Doue collected the ball outside the area and thumped a shot into the bottom corner.
Garcia made another excellent save shortly after the break from Achraf Hakimi, before Xavi Espart burst through to level for Barca against the run of play.
Kvaratskhelia and Marquinhos both pulled up injured within seconds of each other and had to leave the field.
The home team continued to press, though, and Lucas Hernandez restored their advantage 18 minutes from time with a brilliant header.
Lamine Yamal powered past Warren Zaire-Emery to equalise again seven minutes later.
But Vitinha hammered home from outside the box in the 81st minute and Ruiz's tap-in gave Luis Enrique's team a second straight 4-2 Champions League win after seeing off Man City by the same scoreline last week.
Liverpool battled back from two goals down to also maintain their 100-percent record by edging out Villarreal 4-3 at Anfield.
Liverpool fell behind in the fourth minute when Georges Mikautadze pounced on a terrible error from Virgil van Dijk, before Villarreal defender Sergi Cardona strolled through their defence to make it two.
Alexis Mac Allister pulled one back for the hosts nine minutes before half-time by heading in Kostas Tsimikas's corner.
Andoni Iraola's men were level in first-half added time through Ronald Araujo's back-post header after Cardona inexplicably left Rio Ngumoha's cross.
Mac Allister completed the turnaround by firing in from Ngumoha's square pass, and half-time substitute Florian Wirtz's first goal of the season gave the Reds some breathing space.
Tani Oluwaseyi set up a nervy finish for Iraola, but Liverpool held on.
"We are facing very good teams. It's good to come back but we've started losing too many goals this season," Iraola told Amazon Prime.
At the Etihad, Elliot Anderson put Manchester City in front with his first goal for the club, before Phil Foden made it two goals in as many games after scoring against Ipswich at the weekend.
AEK halved the deficit early in the second half through Stavros Pilios, only for Rayan Cherki to sweep in City's third in the 57th minute.
Foden later fired in his second and third goals in a comprehensive victory, despite Erling Haaland being rested after picking up a knock at the weekend.
"Slowly, but surely. Still got a long way to go, but I am going in the right direction," Foden told TNT Sports of his gradual return to form.
Roma eased to their first Champions League win since 2019 as the capital club brushed aside pointless Slovan Bratislava 4-0 at the Stadio Olimpico.
All four Serie A clubs in the competition lost last week, but Napoli made it two wins from two on Tuesday for the Italian sides.
Massimiliano Allegri's men were twice pegged back by Bodo/Glimt but eventually got the better of the Norwegians in a 4-3 thriller, as Scott McTominay scored a brace.
Atletico Madrid played out a 1-1 draw with Stuttgart in Germany, despite playing much of the second half with 10 men.
Borussia Dortmund ended a run of four straight away defeats in the Champions League with a 2-1 win over Sabah in Baku.

Gazette on Special Solar Power Installation Ordinance, 2026 issued
item.description:
The government has issued the Special Solar Power Installation Ordinance, 2026, allowing the establishment of solar power projects with a maximum capacity of five megawatts to accelerate the expansion of solar energy systems.
The gazette notification was issued on Monday.
The ordinance allows solar power projects on rooftops, courtyards, unused land and tea gardens, as well as floating and agrivoltaic systems.
It also prescribes imprisonment and fines for theft, vandalism, illegal connections and obstruction of solar power systems.
Solar power systems with a maximum capacity of five megawatts will be considered "special solar power systems" under the ordinance. However, large-scale ground-mounted solar power projects will remain outside its scope.
A tripartite agreement among the consumer, service provider and competent authority will be required for installing a special solar power system, following a government-prescribed standard contract template. The agreement will specify site-use rights, equipment standards, e-waste management, manufacturers' take-back schemes for discarded equipment, electricity tariffs and net-metering facilities.
A National Policy Council, headed by the prime minister, will be formed to oversee solar power expansion and policy coordination. Ministers or state ministers and senior secretaries from relevant ministries, including finance, law and power, will be members of the council.
District Technical and Coordination Committees, chaired by deputy commissioners (DCs), will also be formed, with superintendents of police, local engineers and district-level heads of power agencies as members. The committees will submit reports to the council every three months.
Meanwhile, Upazila Technical and Coordination Committees, led by upazila nirbahi officers (UNOs), will supervise field-level activities and report to the district committees every month.
The ordinance prescribes penalties for various offences to protect solar power systems. Theft of electricity or equipment, as well as buying, selling or possessing stolen goods, is punishable by up to three years' imprisonment, a fine of Tk50,000, or both.
Vandalizing or damaging solar panels or equipment carries a penalty of up to five years' imprisonment or a fine of up to Tk5,00,000. Illegal connections without written authorisation from the competent authority and obstructing personnel engaged in the installation, inspection or maintenance of solar power systems are punishable by up to three years' imprisonment or a fine of up to Tk5 lakh.
The ordinance also bars civil or criminal cases or other legal proceedings against the government, competent authorities or their officials and employees for actions taken in good faith under the ordinance, even if such actions cause or are likely to cause harm.

item.title: President accepts Ishraque Hossain’s resignation
item.description:
President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has accepted the resignation of State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain.
The Cabinet Division issued a gazette notification in this regard on Tuesday.
The notification, signed by Cabinet Secretary Nasimul Gani by order of the President, stated that the President had accepted the resignation of Ishraque Hossain, State Minister for Liberation War Affairs.
It also stated that the resignation would take effect immediately.
Earlier, on Monday, lawmaker Ishraque Hossain announced at a press conference that he was voluntarily resigning from the Cabinet. He clarified his position by outlining the circumstances surrounding an anti-drug drive in Gandaria in the capital and his carrying of a licensed firearm.
He announced his decision to step down from the post of state minister at the same press conference.
The gazette notification issued the following day formally made his resignation effective.

item.title: Dengue: 5 more die, 1,366 hospitalized in 24hrs
item.description:
Five people died of dengue, and 1,366 new patients were hospitalized across the country in the 24 hours leading up to Tuesday morning.
With the latest fatalities, the dengue death toll has risen to 357 in the country this year, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
Of the new deaths, two were reported in the Dhaka North City Corporation area and Barisal division each and one was recorded in Rangpur division, it said.
Of the total fatalities, 53.1% were female and 46.9% were male.
Since January 1 this year, hospitals across the country have admitted 115,617 dengue patients. Of them, 109,316 have recovered.

item.title: Dilip Agarwala put on one-day remand in money-laundering case
item.description:
A Dhaka court on Tuesday placed Diamond World Managing Director Dilip Kumar Agarwala on one-day remand in a case filed over alleged laundering of Tk 678 crore.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Md Ariful Islam passed the order when Sub-Inspector Md Ashraful Hasan of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) of police, also the investigating officer of the case, produced him before the court with a three-day remand prayer.
Earlier on Monday evening, detectives arrested Dilip Agarwala from the Banani area of the capital in the case filed by the CID on November 18 last year for allegedly laundering around Tk678 crore through smuggling gold and diamonds.
The Financial Crime Unit of CID filed the case against Dilip with Gulshan Police Station under the Money Laundering Prevention Act, said Jasim Uddin Khan, special superintendent of police (Media) of CID.
On September 29, 2024, the CID began an investigation against Dilip Agarwala after reviewing Diamond World Limited’s financial transactions, documents and bank accounts.
During the investigation, they found that the company procured smuggled gold and diamonds in the country.
According to the case statement, Dilip Agarwala had long been involved in money laundering and smuggling under the guise of gold and diamond business both at home and abroad as the proprietor of Diamond World and Diamond World Limited.
During the investigation, it was found that the company legally imported gold bars, jewellery, loose diamonds and other items worth Tk38,47,48,011.52 from abroad through letters of credit from September 6, 2006 to February 8, 2024.
During the same period, it also acquired gold and diamonds worth Tk6,78,19,14,014 from the local market through purchase and exchange.
However, the company failed to show valid documents to the CID regarding the source or suppliers of these materials.
Police earlier arrested Dilip Agarwala on September 3, 2024. On October 1, 2025, he was released on bail.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,204 as three die in 24 hours
item.description:
Three more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Tuesday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 1,204.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all three of the latest casualties as suspected.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 1,100, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 104, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
The three new suspected fatalities were reported across three divisions; Dhaka, Mymensingh, and Chittagong with one death each.
A total of 1,217 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Tuesday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 215,768.
During the same period, 42 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 23,199.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 191,761 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 184,168 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

item.title: 30 Bangladeshis return home after release from Cambodia detention centre
item.description:
Thirty Bangladeshi nationals who were released from an immigration detention centre in Phnom Penh, the capital of Cambodia, returned home on Tuesday.
They arrived at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka at around 12:15pm on a Thai Airways flight.
The returnees are Mohammad Harun Or Rashid, Mohammad Abdul Wadud, Mohammad Tarlib Hasan Titul, Sumit Chandra Das, Rakib Hossain, Bappi Das, Mohammad Labon Sheikh, Mohammad Abdur Rahman, Mohammad Billal Hossain, Mohammad Mostafa, Nur Nabi, Mohammad Emon Ali, Mohammad Barkatullah, Mohammad Rubel Mia, Ali Ahmed, Zahidul Islam, Shamsul Alam, Mohammad Abdur Rahman, Abu Jaher Sabuj, Shawon, Nahid Dhali, Raju Hossain, Mohammad Tayeb Ali Sheikh, Saimon Bhuiyan, Mohammad Rashedul, Mohammad Akash Ahmed, Mohammad Shimul Ali, Ashikur Rahman, Mohammad Alamin PK and Mohammad Kabir.
The Bangladeshis had travelled to Cambodia in search of jobs but became stranded at various scam centres in the country.
They registered to return home after the Cambodian government offered them the opportunity to leave without paying fines.
Accordingly, they arrived at Phnom Penh Airport on September 3. However, during immigration checks, Cambodian immigration police detained 32 Bangladeshis over various complications, including irregular immigration status.
Two were subsequently released, while the remaining 30 were held at the immigration detention centre.
Following an application by an organization named Anirban Survivor Voice Foundation, the first secretary of the labour wing at the Bangladesh Embassy in Bangkok was asked to take the necessary steps to secure the detainees’ release and facilitate their early return home.
After the required procedures were completed in phases, the 30 Bangladeshis returned to Bangladesh on Tuesday.

item.title: PM to visit Japan from October 26 to 29
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman will pay an official visit to Japan from October 26 to 29 at the invitation of his Japanese counterpart Sanae Takaichi to strengthen bilateral ties and expand economic cooperation.
The governments of Bangladesh and Japan formally announced the visit simultaneously on Tuesday.
“During the visit, the prime minister will hold high-level bilateral talks with Takaichi at her office on October 27,” Foreign Secretary Asad Alam Siam told journalists at a curtain raiser media briefing at the foreign ministry.
The Japanese premier will also host a luncheon in his honor, he added.
The foreign secretary said that the visit is expected to deepen the existing strategic partnership, attract fresh Japanese investment, expand trade and accelerate ongoing development projects.
Discussions will focus on the effective implementation of the Economic Partnership Agreement (EPA), signed in February 2026, expanding access for Bangladeshi products to the Japanese market and strengthening business engagement.
The two sides will also explore wider cooperation in renewable energy, agriculture, science and technology, digital transformation, skills development and human resource development.
The prime minister is scheduled to deliver the keynote address at the Japan-Bangladesh Economic Forum and meet Japanese business leaders.
His tentative program includes engagements with the Japan-Bangladesh Parliamentary Friendship League and the chairman of the Japan-Bangladesh Committee for Commercial and Economic Cooperation.
Meetings are also being planned with the president of the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA), the governor of the Japan Bank for International Cooperation (JBIC), the president of the Japan External Trade Organization (JETRO) and the chairman of the Sasakawa Peace Foundation.
The proposed itinerary includes visits to an LNG terminal and power plant in Futtsu City, Chiba, the headquarters of UNIQLO and a Toyota factory in Nagoya.
Announcements concerning memoranda of understanding or cooperation in agriculture, fisheries, human resource development, skills enhancement, civil aviation, trade, environmental conservation and local government modernization may be made during the visit, said the foreign secretary.
Detailed discussions are planned on Japanese support for establishing factories in Bangladesh, generating employment and developing human resources in line with the prime minister’s priorities.
Beyond bilateral matters, the two sides are expected to discuss regional and international peace and stability, a sustainable and peaceful solution to the Rohingya crisis and stronger cooperation in addressing the energy crisis.
The prime minister will be accompanied by his spouse, Dr Zubaida Rahman, ministers, advisers, senior government officials and other delegation members.
The delegation will travel on Biman Bangladesh Airlines flights.
Japan, one of the first countries to recognize Bangladesh following independence, remains a major development partner, supporting infrastructure, human resource development and capacity building.
Its cooperation includes major projects such as the metro rail, Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport’s Third Terminal and infrastructure development in Matarbari.

item.title: PM donates Tk 10 lakh to Dharmasabha Temple in Rajshahi
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman visited Dharmasabha Temple in the Miapara area of Rajshahi city and donated Tk 10 lakh on Tuesday afternoon after attending a public rally at Madrasa Ground.
At Dharmasabha, the prime minister held an exchange of views with leaders of the Puja Celebration Council from 5pm to 5:30pm. During the meeting, he handed over a cheque for Tk 10 lakh to Rajshahi Dharmasabha President Bishwanath Sarkar.
During the exchange of views, Tarique said people of all religions in Bangladesh were citizens of the country and that everyone's cooperation was needed to build a prosperous and developed Bangladesh.
He called on all citizens, regardless of religion or ethnicity, to come forward to help build the country. He also exchanged greetings with Hindu attendees and extended his Sharadiya greetings.
During the visit, leaders of the Bangladesh Hindu Buddhist Welfare Front requested that the prime minister build a model temple in Rajshahi.
Security was tightened around Dharmasabha Temple ahead of the prime minister's visit and meeting with local representatives.
After visiting the temple, the prime minister left for Shah Makhdum Airport in Rajshahi at 5:37pm before departing for Chittagong.

item.title: Minister: Religion should not be used to create political divisions
item.description:
Posts, Telecommunications and Information Technology and Science and Technology Minister Faqir Mahbub Anam has said religion should not be used to create political divisions, urging people of all faiths to work together to advance Bangladesh.
“Everyone has their own religion, but the country belongs to all of us,” he said while attending a programme in Dhanbari of Tangail on Tuesday.
The minister distributed cash assistance from his personal fund among 36 Durga Puja mandaps and saris from the prime minister’s relief and welfare fund among members of the Hindu community.
He called for celebrating all religious festivals peacefully to strengthen communal harmony and urged people to refrain from creating divisions through politics. Supporting members of the Hindu community in times of need, he added, was a shared responsibility.
The programme was chaired by Dhanbari upazila BNP President Principal MA Azizur Rahman. Local BNP leaders, Hindu community representatives and other dignitaries attended.
Earlier, the minister inaugurated a newly built visitor room at Madhupur Upazila Parishad and planted a sapling at Dhanbari Upazila Parishad as part of a nationwide programme to plant 25 crore trees.

item.title: Tk9.33cr drain project stalled for six months, commuters suffer in Chapainawabganj
item.description:
Construction of a 2.1km drain in Shibganj municipality of Chapainawabganj has remained stalled for six months due to objections from local residents, leaving thousands of commuters, students and traders suffering.
The Tk9.33 crore project, stretching from Academy Mor to Debinagar, has been held up, with rainwater accumulating in road potholes, disrupting traffic and business activities.
The road serves several important institutions, including a police station, hospital, government high school and college, upazila parishad, sub-registry office, Sonali Bank branch, insurance offices, an orphanage, madrasa and mosques. Thousands of people use the route every day.
Excavated sections along the roadside have made movement hazardous. The prolonged suspension of work has also sparked frustration among residents, who are demanding the project's early completion.
According to municipal sources, construction began around two years ago under the Inclusive Urban Governance and Infrastructure Improvement Project (IUGIIP) to address waterlogging. Of the planned 2.1km drain, around 300 metres remain unfinished.
The municipality said work had been suspended for six months after three local residents obstructed excavation on municipal land.
Contractor Jahangir Alam said the project had been nearing completion when the objections halted progress.
“Construction cannot proceed because three local residents are obstructing excavation on the land designated by the municipality. The remaining work can be completed quickly if the municipal authorities take the necessary steps,” he said.
Two residents, Mahbub and Alim, named as having obstructed the work, could not be reached for comment.
Another resident, Saidul Islam, said four to five feet of municipal land fell within his homestead. He said they had objected to the work because they wanted the drain shifted slightly away from the boundary wall to protect their houses.
Shibganj Municipality Administrator and Upazila Nirbahi Officer Mazharul Islam said parts of several houses and a mosque fell within the land designated for drain construction.
He said the authorities would hold discussions with residents to resolve the dispute and complete the remaining work as soon as possible.
However, with construction still stalled on the busy road, commuters and businesses continue to bear the brunt, with no clear timeline for an end to their suffering.

PM Tarique calls for unity of all faiths to build desired Bangladesh
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Tuesday called on people of all faiths to work together to build their desired Bangladesh, saying the country belongs to Muslims, Hindus, Buddhists and Christians alike.
“Just as people of all religions united to free the country in 1971, we want to build Bangladesh together, with people of all faiths,” he said while addressing a roadside rally at Paglapir point on his way to Rangpur to visit a Durga Puja mandap on Maha Navami.
“From today, let us pledge that this country belongs to all of us — Muslims, Hindus, Buddhists and Christians. We will all work hard together to build the country into the Bangladesh we aspire to see,” the prime minister said.
Tarique said people had entrusted the BNP with the responsibility of running the country following the February 12 parliamentary election.
Since taking office, the government has been trying to stand beside people from all walks of life, he said.
As part of those efforts, the government has waived agricultural loans of up to Tk10,000 for farmers, introduced the Family Card and the Farmers’ Card program, he said.
The government has also introduced monthly allowances for imams, muezzins and religious leaders of other faiths, Tarique added.
He said the government is trying to support people in all professions and sections of society.
Referring to Durga Puja, the biggest religious festival of the Hindu community, the prime minister said he wanted people of all faiths to join hands in building the country.
Earlier, Tarique left Saidpur Airport for Rangpur by road after arriving from Dhaka by a military aircraft.
Hundreds of BNP leaders, activists and supporters lined both sides of the road, including at Taraganj and Paglapir, to greet him.
He waved back from his motorcade and briefly addressed gatherings at the two points.

item.title: Armed robbers loot 50–60 vehicles on Cox’s Bazar road
item.description:
A group of armed robbers looted passengers at gunpoint on the Eidgaon-Eidgarh-Baishari road in Cox’s Bazar in broad daylight on Monday, targeting at least 50 to 60 vehicles, mostly CNG-run auto-rickshaws and motorcycles.
The incidents took place in two phases at a spot known as Himchhari Dhala, along the hilly road through Eidgaon and Ramu upazilas. The robbers reportedly looted cash, mobile phones and other valuables from more than 100 passengers.
According to witnesses, the robberies occurred around 8am and noon and continued for approximately two and a half hours.
Victims said 10 to 12 armed, masked men intercepted vehicles, held passengers at gunpoint and dragged them into a nearby forest, where they were beaten and robbed. They said there was no police patrol in the area during the incidents.
Md Rabiul Islam, a manager at the Eidgarh branch of a non-governmental organisation, said he was travelling by motorcycle from Eidgaon Bazar to Eidgarh with a companion around noon, carrying Tk120,000.
When they reached Himchhari Dhala, 10 to 12 armed, masked men stopped their motorcycle and took them into the forest, where they were beaten. The robbers searched them and seized the cash, two mobile phones and various documents before releasing them.
Rabiul said the robbers held more than 100 passengers travelling in 50 to 60 auto-rickshaws and motorcycles hostage for nearly two hours.
Police arrived at the scene around 3pm and launched an operation but could not arrest anyone. He also said there had been no police patrol on the road during the robberies.
Abdul Hakim, an accountant at a private organisation’s Eidgarh branch, said he was travelling with two others in an auto-rickshaw from Eidgaon Bazar to Eidgarh Bazar when robbers held them at gunpoint and took them into the forest.
The robbers beat them and stole Tk150,000 and a bank cheque book, he said.
Hakim said robberies were frequent on the road and kidnappings for ransom were also common, but effective measures to ensure passengers’ safety were lacking.
Mohammad Tareq, a resident of Eidgarh who was also targeted, said he was travelling from Eidgaon to Eidgarh in a CNG-run auto-rickshaw with four other passengers around 6:30am on Monday.
When the vehicle reached Himchhari Dhala, robbers intercepted it and snatched his mobile phone. Fearing for his life, Tareq jumped from the moving auto-rickshaw and escaped.
ATM Sifatul Mazdar, officer-in-charge of Eidgaon police station, said local miscreants had set up roadblocks, looted vehicles and fled into the forest.
“Multiple police teams are conducting operations to apprehend them, though no arrests had been made as of this evening,” he said.
He added that patrols had been intensified in the dense forest areas along the 17-kilometre Eidgaon-Eidgarh-Baishari road.
