Teenager’s body recovered from pond near PM Tarique’s rally venue
item.description:
Police recovered the semi-decomposed body of an 18-year-old, Rafsan bin Abdullah, from a pond in Rajshahi on Tuesday morning, about half a kilometre from the historic Madrasa Ground, where Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is scheduled to address a public rally.
Rafsan had been missing since leaving home on Monday morning. His body was found floating in a pond south of the Shah Makhdum Institute Public Library around 9am on Tuesday.
Tarique is scheduled to attend the rally, organised by the BNP’s city and district units, as the chief guest at Madrasa Ground at 3pm.
Deputy Commissioner Gaziur Rahman, spokesperson for Rajshahi Metropolitan Police (RMP), said Rafsan lived in the city’s Hosseiniganj Betpatti area. His father is Abdullah Zaki Rubel.
He said an initial examination found no visible signs of injury on the body. Rafsan was wearing shorts but no shirt, and the body had begun to decompose.
The body was sent to the morgue at Rajshahi Medical College Hospital for an autopsy.
Police said their preliminary assessment suggested that Rafsan might have drowned after entering the pond to bathe. His family said he did not know how to swim.
However, the exact cause of death will be determined after the autopsy report is received, police said.

item.title: Unicef chief calls for investment in children, action to end child marriage
item.description:
Unicef Executive Director Catherine Russell has called for urgent investment in children in Bangladesh following a three-day visit that included meetings with families in Korail, Dhaka’s largest informal settlement, and Rohingya refugees and host communities in Cox’s Bazar.
Russell urged action on three fronts: ending child marriage and keeping girls in school; fulfilling the government’s commitment to invest 5% of gross domestic product (GDP) in education and health; and protecting access to quality education for Rohingya and host-community children.
In Korail, Russell heard from children and parents about poverty, disrupted education and limited access to basic services. Adolescent girls shared their ambitions and the pressures that can force them to leave school and marry.
“I met a 14-year-old girl named Bushra, who told me how community leaders at a Unicef-supported child protection hub had worked with Bushra’s father to save her from early marriage,” Russell said.
“Keeping girls in school and providing them with the health, education and protection services they need will deliver a brighter future for them, for their communities, and for Bangladesh.”
Nearly half, or 47.2%, of women aged 20-24 in Bangladesh were married before the age of 18, according to the Bangladesh Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey 2025.
Child marriage pushes girls out of school, fuels early pregnancy and limits their opportunities throughout life. Unicef has called for girls to complete secondary education and for loopholes in national law that permit child marriage to be addressed.
Russell met senior officials, including Shama Obaed Islam, state minister for foreign affairs. She expressed appreciation for the government’s commitment to increasing the budgets for education and health services, stressing the importance of turning pledges into action.
“Budgets reflect priorities,” Russell said. “Investing in children’s quality education, health, nutrition and protection is investing in Bangladesh’s future.”
In Cox’s Bazar, home to one of the world’s largest refugee camps, Russell met Rohingya children and families and visited Unicef-supported learning activities.
Recognising Bangladesh’s generosity in hosting Rohingya refugees, Russell urged the international community to continue supporting both refugees and host communities.
At a Unicef-supported learning centre, she heard from students and teachers about the importance of education and vocational skills. Beyond learning, education helps protect children from exploitation, trafficking, child marriage and recruitment by armed groups.
“Rohingya children have lost so much to violence, displacement and uncertainty. They cannot lose their education too,” Russell said. “The world must invest in them, and in the communities that welcomed them.”
Across Bangladesh, Unicef works with the government and partners to strengthen the systems and services on which children and families depend. Its support includes access to quality education, primary health care, immunisation, nutrition, safe water, sanitation and child protection services.
Unicef also works to prevent child marriage and violence against children, empower adolescent girls, strengthen social protection and promote greater public investment in children. Through research, policy advocacy and support for national and local institutions, it seeks to ensure essential services reach children most at risk of being left behind.
In Cox’s Bazar, Unicef and its partners provide life-saving and essential services to Rohingya refugee children and families, including malnutrition prevention and treatment, safe drinking water, sanitation, education, health care, child protection and psychosocial support. The organisation also supports vulnerable host communities.
As humanitarian funding declines, sustained international support is critical to protecting essential services, preserving progress and ensuring that refugee and host-community children are not left behind.

item.title: PM leaves Dhaka to visit Durga Puja mandaps in 3 districts
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman left Dhaka for Rangpur on Tuesday morning to visit Durga Puja mandaps outside the capital on Maha Navami, the ninth day of the Hindu community’s Sharadiya festival.
He left Tejgaon Airport at 9am by a military aircraft, Prime Minister’s Press Secretary Saleh Shibly told UNB.
“The prime minister has left for Rangpur. He will visit the puja mandap at Radha Gobinda Temple and exchange greetings with devotees there,” he said.
Tarique is scheduled to visit puja mandaps in Rangpur, Rajshahi and Chittagong districts before returning to Dhaka at night, Shibly said.
He said the government has taken all necessary measures to ensure the smooth celebration of Durga Puja across the country.
“The government’s policy is that religion belongs to each individual, but everyone has the right to security. The allocation has been increased, holidays have been extended, and all kinds of support are being provided to puja mandaps,” the press secretary said.
A number of senior BNP leaders and government officials are accompanying the Prime Minister, including BNP Standing Committee member Gayeshwar Chandra Roy, Women and Children Affairs Minister Prof AZM Zahid Hussain, BNP Acting Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi, Culture Minister Nitai Roy Chowdhury and State Minister for Local Government Mir Shah Alam.
Others in the entourage include Prime Minister’s Adviser Rehan Asif Asad, Special Assistant Bijon Kanti Sarkar, BNP Special Secretary Belayet Hossain Mridha, Hindu Religious Welfare Trust Vice-Chairman and MP Nipun Roy Chowdhury, BNP Assistant Organising Secretary Jayanta Kumar Kundu, Press Secretary Saleh Shibly and Additional Press Secretary Atikur Rahman Rumon.
According to the itinerary, Tarique will travel from Saidpur Airport to Rangpur’s Radha Gobinda Temple after arriving in Saidpur at 10am.
He is scheduled to leave Saidpur for Rajshahi at 12:30pm and visit the Dharmasabha Temple’s puja mandap at around 1:15pm.
After a brief stop at Rajshahi Circuit House, he will attend a public rally at Haji Muhammad Mohsin Government High School ground at 3pm.
The prime minister will then fly to Chittagong, where he is scheduled to visit the puja mandap at JM Sen Hall in Rahmatganj at 5:30pm. After a brief stop at Chittagong Circuit House, he is scheduled to leave Shah Amanat International Airport for Dhaka at 7:45pm and arrive at Tejgaon Airport at 9:15pm.

Cantonment board services added to MyGov platform
item.description:
Citizen services provided by all cantonment boards have been brought under the MyGov platform through an initiative of the Directorate of Military Lands and Cantonments to establish a technology-driven, transparent and citizen-friendly service system.
The initiative was implemented under the overall supervision of the Cabinet Division, with support from the Aspire to Innovate (a2i) Program and the Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Division.
Under the previous system, service recipients had to visit cantonment board offices in person to obtain services. Applications, document submissions, fee payments and certificate collection were handled manually, often requiring multiple visits and resulting in additional expenses, time and inconvenience.
To reduce travel, time, expenses and inconvenience for citizens, a pilot project was initially launched by incorporating 2 citizen services of the Dhaka Cantonment Board into the MyGov platform. Following the successful pilot, steps were taken to digitize services at the remaining 14 cantonment boards.
As part of the process, 3 service analysis workshops were held in March 2026, with officials and employees from the 14 cantonment boards participating. A total of 63 types of citizen services were reviewed and analyzed, and 19 basic services were identified for digitization. Subsequently, 185 online application forms were developed for these services across different cantonment boards.
In June and July 2026, 7 region-based validation workshops were held to verify and finalize the online application forms, service fees, service workflows and templates.
In August and September, 140 officials and employees, including Cantonment Executive Officers from all cantonment boards, received practical training. This completed the necessary preparations for managing services and conducting operations through the digital platform.
Currently, 185 online application forms covering 19 basic services are publicly available on the MyGov platform. Citizens can apply online from home, pay applicable service fees and receive certificates or services containing QR codes.
They can also monitor the progress of their applications online and provide feedback on the services.
Cantonment boards can receive, verify, investigate, process and dispose of applications online through the same platform. This is expected to accelerate administrative activities, reduce paperwork and strengthen transparency and accountability in service management.
As part of the current government's priorities for simplifying services and digital transformation, the inclusion of cantonment board citizen services on the MyGov platform has opened a new avenue for integrated, technology-driven service management.

item.title: PM urges officials to keep Dhaka clean for their own children
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Monday urged city corporation officials and employees to work sincerely to make the capital clean, healthy and liveable, at least for the sake of their own children, saying waste and poor sanitation are among Dhaka’s biggest problems.
“Forget about everyone else. Let us build a healthy environment and a healthy city for our own children. Let us all work together towards that goal,” he said.
The prime minister made the call while exchanging views with officials and employees during a visit to Dhaka South City Corporation’s (DSCC) Nagar Bhaban headquarters, said the PM’s Deputy Press Secretary Hasan Shiplu.
Emphasizing the need to keep the city clean for the sake of children's future, Tarique said no parent would want their children to grow up in a dirty, germ-ridden and unhealthy environment.
Children do not stay only around their homes; they also go to schools, colleges, playgrounds and other parts of the city, he said, adding that efforts to keep Dhaka clean must extend beyond individual neighborhoods.
“Your children will not stay only in your neighborhood. They will move around the whole of Dhaka. So, let us all try together. If we make an effort, we can do it,” Tarique said.
About waste and poor cleanliness issues in the capital, he said the problems could not be solved in a day or even in seven days, but sincere and sustained efforts by everyone could gradually improve the situation.
Addressing city corporation officials and employees, the prime minister said they are directly or indirectly involved in resolving the problem.
“It may take time, but if you keep trying, change will come. You must have that confidence. The most important thing is the willingness to act,” he said.
Tarique also urged officials to take greater responsibility for identifying and resolving problems, saying he regularly looked for problems wherever he went and contacted the relevant people to address them.
“If you also observe problems in this way and take steps to solve them, change is certainly possible,” he said.
Citing London as an example, the prime minister said many parts of the British capital were also littered during the 1960s and 1970s. Still, sustained efforts and public awareness gradually improved the situation.
Many people who visited clean and well-maintained cities abroad might have wished Dhaka could be like them, he said, adding that regret alone would not bring change unless people also fulfilled their responsibilities.
Referring to a recent conversation with a senior official of a South Korean company that has been doing business in Bangladesh for a long time, Tarique said the official told him that Dhaka’s cleanliness improved somewhat compared with the past.
“He did not say there has been a big change. He said it has improved somewhat. That means change is possible. If we all work together, we can do even better,” the Prime Minister said.
He also said he regularly monitor the condition of roads and waste management across the city.
Some road dividers are being rebuilt, while condition at some waste transfer stations has improved to a certain extent, he said, stressing the need to continue such initiatives.
Tarique urged officials and employees to practice self-criticism alongside criticism of others.
“You may criticize me, but you must also examine yourselves. Think about how properly you are performing your duties and how much effort you are making,” he said.
Earlier, the prime minister visited the emergency operations centre at Nagar Bhaban, where he reviewed websites displaying weather information, earthquake updates from the United States Geological Survey (USGS), wind speed, flood forecasts and air quality.
He also enquired about how the information was monitored and how officials tracked emergency situations.
Tarique monitored the city's cleanliness activities through a Facebook Live broadcast and watched a video on the development and various activities of Dhaka South City Corporation.
State Minister for Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives Mir Shahe Alam, DSCC Administrator Abdus Salam, Dhaka North City Corporation Administrator Shafiqul Islam Khan Milton, and Local Government Division Senior Secretary Shahidul Hasan were present.

item.title: Govt trains aspiring entrepreneurs to improve agro-processing skills
item.description:
The government is providing training to help young people become entrepreneurs by improving their agricultural product processing, business management skills and market access.
The initiative is being implemented in 208 upazilas across all 64 districts under a project of the Department of Agricultural Marketing (DAM) under the Ministry of Agriculture. So far, 6,875 people have received training, while the project aims to train around 7,000 more entrepreneurs this year.
The initiative is being implemented under the Programme on Agricultural and Rural Transformation for Nutrition, Entrepreneurship and Resilience in Bangladesh (PARTNER). Its objectives include creating entrepreneurs in various agriculture-based sectors, adding value to agricultural products, and expanding opportunities for processing and exports.
The project aims to ensure that women account for 60% of the entrepreneurs developed under the initiative, while men will make up the remaining 40%.
Project officials said training is being provided to develop entrepreneurs in various sectors, including agriculture, seeds, nurseries, mushrooms, vermicompost, jute products and dairy products. Alongside technical training, the initiative focuses on strengthening business skills, management knowledge and market linkages.
Dr Muhammad Abdullah Al Faruk, agency program director of the PARTNER-DAM component of the Department of Agricultural Marketing, said the initiative was underway in 208 upazilas across all 64 districts.
He said the training was designed to improve entrepreneurs' business management skills and connect them with markets.
After completing the training, entrepreneurs are also receiving incubation support, he said. Incubation support organisations are working to identify the challenges entrepreneurs face in running their businesses and help them find solutions.
The project also plans to provide financial assistance to trained entrepreneurs to purchase agricultural product processing equipment. Under the proposed arrangement, the project will subsidise 70% of the equipment costs, while entrepreneurs will bear the remaining 30%.
The support is expected to create opportunities for small entrepreneurs to launch and expand agricultural product processing businesses.
Another key objective of the project is to improve coordination among stakeholders involved in agricultural marketing. To this end, 767 Market Actors Business Schools have been established in different agricultural production areas under the Department of Agricultural Marketing. Of these, 227 focus on potatoes. The project plans to establish another 335 schools this year.
Dr Al Faruk said the schools were being established around the dominant agricultural products of particular areas.
The initiative brings farmers, traders, entrepreneurs, cold storage owners, transport operators and other market stakeholders under a common platform. This is expected to make it easier to identify challenges and opportunities in the supply chains of specific agricultural products, he said.
The project is also working to improve the value chains of potatoes, mangoes, jackfruits, tomatoes and aromatic rice.
It aims to strengthen coordination among stakeholders at different stages, from production and collection to storage, processing and marketing. Initiatives are also underway to form Value Chain Promotional Bodies for the five products.
Project officials said the guidelines for these bodies had already been approved by the ministry.
Meanwhile, Agriculture, Fisheries and Livestock Minister Mohammed Aminur Rashid has stressed the importance of research, innovation and modern technology in increasing productivity across agriculture-based sectors.
He said research, innovation and the development of a skilled workforce were essential to advancing the agriculture, fisheries and livestock sectors. The government aims to develop skilled human resources in agriculture through training, he added.
Abul Kalam Azad, the project's coordinator, said entrepreneurs could create employment opportunities for others while becoming self-reliant themselves.
Initiatives to develop entrepreneurs could play an important role in making agriculture a modern and respected profession, he added.

item.title: UN agency slashes Gaza food aid over funding, warns needs persist
item.description:
The World Food Program said Monday it would end monthly assistance to 500,000 people in Gaza due to a funding shortfall, despite acute needs in the war-battered Palestinian territory.
With the cutbacks, 1.1 million Palestinians in Gaza -- still about half the population -- will be receiving either food or cash assistance each month from the UN agency, in reduced amounts.
The World Food Program said its efforts had mitigated the effects during a famine last year in Gaza -- a description of the situation disputed by Israel -- and warned that conditions had not improved to the point that it can take away aid.
“People are not safe. Airstrikes continue on a daily basis. People continue to be displaced,” Shaun Hughes, the WFP country director, told AFP at the agency’s office in east Jerusalem.
“Almost everybody remains without a permanent home to live in. And the humanitarian conditions are brutal,” he said.
According to the latest assessments, 1.4 million people -- or two-thirds of Gaza’s population -- are still “acutely food insecure” and need humanitarian assistance to survive, he said.
In August last year, the UN’s Integrated Food Security Phase Classification said that Gaza was suffering famine conditions. Israel, which has blockaded the territory and attacked it relentlessly since the October 7, 2023 resistance campaign on it by Hamas, described the finding as a lie.
The famine classification was lifted in December, two months after a US-brokered ceasefire was announced in Gaza. Israel has kept striking Gaza since then, vowing to kill anyone involved in the October 7 resistance campaign.
Since the ceasefire, the WFP has been able to step up assistance and had been reaching between 1.5 million and 1.8 million people every month.
“This has been a lifeline. But now, rather than being able to sustain and scale up that assistance, we’re actually having to reduce it,” Hughes said.
“And that’s not because we don’t have humanitarian access to deliver food; that’s because we don’t have funding.”
In addition to reducing the number of people who receive rations, the WFP has been forced to shrink the content.
Families receiving food assistance will now get only one food parcel instead of two and a smaller bag of wheat flour, the WFP said in an operational note.
The 75,000 families who receive assistance in cash will see the amount reduced from 1,250 to 750 shekels ($400 to $240) per month.
The WFP is funded by governments as well as private donors. It has seen a sharp drop in resources, including after President Donald Trump returned to power in the United States and drastically slashed contributions to UN agencies as well as bilateral aid.
The agency says it needs about $450 million over the next six months for its operations in Gaza and the West Bank, but in 2026 it has only received about half the usual financing for the Palestinian territories.
In September, the agency also reduced by half the number of aid recipients in the West Bank, which Israel has occupied since 1967, from 400,000 to 200,000.
“Now is not the time in the history of Palestine and Gaza to turn away from what is happening in Gaza,” Hughes said.
The WFP says that conditions have moderately improved in Gaza but noted that needs could rise again with the onset of winter.
Israel has allowed more goods into Gaza under the terms of the Trump ceasefire but still imposes heavy restrictions, turning away shipments of anything that is seen as having potential military use -- a policy that has included blocking even prosthetic limbs, according to the United Nations.
Israel has ramped up longstanding criticism of the United Nations since the Gaza war, accusing the world body of bias and perpetuating dependency among Palestinians.

Maha Ashtami celebrated with Kumari Puja, Sandhi Puja
item.description:
Maha Ashtami, the third day of the six-day Sharadiya Durga Puja festival, is being celebrated across the country on Monday with due religious fervour and festivity.
Maha Ashtami Kalparambha and Bihit Puja were held this morning at temples across the country, including Dhakeshwari National Temple. Devotees later offered anjali (prayers) and received charanamrito (sacred water). Maha Prasad was also distributed among devotees.
Sandhi Puja was held from 7:55am to 8:43am, marking the transitional moment between Ashtami and Navami.
According to Hindu mythology, the ritual commemorates the moment when Goddess Durga assumed the form of Chamunda to slay the demon brothers Chanda and Munda.
Kumari Puja, a traditional ritual in which a young, unmarried girl is worshipped as an embodiment of Goddess Durga and the divine feminine, was held at some temples across the country.
In the capital, Kumari Puja was held at Ramakrishna Math and Ramakrishna Mission Dhaka at 9:30am.
During the ritual, an unmarried pre-pubescent girl, generally aged between one and 16, is worshipped as the living embodiment of the divine feminine and Goddess Durga.
Devotees offer water, clothes, flowers, and gold and silver ornaments at the feet of the Kumari as part of the special ritual.
Puja mandaps across the country have been bustling with devotees and visitors since last Friday, when the six-day festival began with the ceremonial invocation of Goddess Durga on Maha Shashthi.
Vibrant decorations, traditional dhak beats, the ringing of kashor and ghonta, conch-shell blasts and ululation have added to the festive atmosphere.
Devotees have been visiting puja pandals across the country to offer prayers and enjoy the celebrations.
A total of 33,851 puja mandaps have been set up across the country this year, including 258 in the capital, according to the Bangladesh Puja Udjapan Parishad. The number has increased by nearly 1,500 compared to last year.
The Gulshan-Banani Puja Foundation is hosting one of the most elaborate celebrations at Kamal Ataturk Park in Banani. Makeshift pandals at Kalabagan ground and Khamarbari have also emerged as major attractions for visitors in the capital, with large structures and eye-catching lighting displays drawing crowds.
Maha Navami will be celebrated tomorrow with religious fervour and enthusiasm. Devotees will gather at temples and mandaps to offer anjali, while major concluding worship rituals and the offering of bhog will mark the day.
Bijaya Dashami will be celebrated on Wednesday, marking the farewell to Goddess Durga. Devotees will take the idols in processions to designated rivers, ponds and other water bodies for immersion, known as Bisarjan.
In the capital, a large number of Durga Puja celebrations are being held in the old parts of the city, including Tantibazar and Shakharibazar.
Ramna Kali Mandir, Siddheshwari Kali Mandir, Dhaka University's Jagannath Hall and Uttara Sarbajanin Mandir are also witnessing large numbers of visitors every day during the festival.

NCC Bank launches ‘China Desk’ to strengthen banking services for Chinese businesses
item.description:
With the aim of providing integrated banking services to Chinese business enterprises and investors operating in Bangladesh, NCC Bank PLC has launched a specialized China Desk named ‘NCC China Connect’.
The main objective of this initiative is to accelerate bilateral trade, investment and business growth between Bangladesh and China.
The China Desk was inaugurated on Wednesday, October 14, at the ‘China National Day Celebration 2026’ held at the Grand Ballroom of Radisson Blu Hotel, Dhaka, organized by the Bangladesh China Chamber of Commerce and Industry (BCCCI) in collaboration with NCC Bank.
The event was held on the occasion of the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People’s Republic of China.
The chief guest at the event was State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam, MP.
Special guest was Liu Yuyin, Chargé d’Affaires of the Embassy of the People’s Republic of China in Bangladesh.
Members of BCCCI, chairman of NCC Bank Mohammed Nurun Newaz Salim, vice-chairman Abdus Salam, director & past chairman Amjadul Ferdous Chowdhury, director & chairman of the executive committee Khairul Alam Chaklader, director Md Moinuddin, director Mohammed Sazzad Un Newaz, director & past vice-chairman Tanzina Ali, directors Syed Asif Nizamuddin, Shamima Newaz, Morshedul Alam Chaklader, Nahid Banu, independent director Meer Sajed-Ul-Basher, and independent director & chairman of the audit committee Md Amirul Islam.
Managing director M Shamsul Arefin, additional managing director M Khurshed Alam, Md Zakir Anam & Mohammed Jamal Uddin Mazumder, deputy managing directors Mohammed Mizanur Rahman & Md Habibur Rahman along with senior officials of the bank and leaders of Chinese businesses in Bangladesh also attended.
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam, MP, highlighted the importance of Bangladesh-China relations in expanding trade, investment and economic cooperation.
She expressed hope that initiatives such as NCC Bank’s China Desk would facilitate business activities between the two countries and further strengthen bilateral economic relations.
Special guest Liu Yuyin welcomed the initiative to launch a specialized banking platform for Chinese business enterprises in Bangladesh. He hoped that this Desk would play a role in expanding bilateral trade and investment, increasing business connectivity and further strengthening the economic partnership between Bangladesh and China.
NCC Bank chairman Mohammad Nurun Newaz Salim said that the launch of the China Desk reflected the bank’s commitment to supporting Chinese business enterprises and expanding bilateral trade and investment between Bangladesh and China.
NCC Bank managing director M Shamsul Arefin said: “China is Bangladesh’s largest trading partner and one of the most important sources of investment. Through ‘NCC China Connect’, we want to provide integrated and specialized banking services to Chinese business enterprises, which will accelerate trade, investment and sustainable growth between the two countries. Operated under our Multinational Corporate Banking Division, this Desk will serve as a central point of contact for Chinese entrepreneurs. Through it, along with support in Mandarin, various services will be provided, including trade finance, working capital, project financing, foreign exchange transactions, bank guarantees, cash management and digital banking. Using correspondent banking relationships with 30 banks in China and a network of nearly 400 correspondent banks worldwide, we are committed to facilitating and expediting cross-border foreign trade transaction settlement with China. In addition, we are also working to create opportunities for Chinese trade transactions settlement in the Chinese currency Renminbi (RMB).”

item.title: Home Ministry to form committees in all upazilas to curb juvenile gangs
item.description:
The Home Ministry has decided to form committees in all upazilas across the country to curb juvenile gang activities.
The respective upazila nirbahi officer (UNO) will serve as chairperson, while the officer-in-charge (OC) of the local police station will be the member secretary.
The decision was announced in a statement signed by Home Ministry Public Relations Officer Faisal Hasan on Monday.
The initiative aims to coordinate the efforts of local administrations and police to prevent juvenile gang activities at the grassroots level, Faisal said.
However, the ministry did not disclose the names or positions of other committee members, the activities they will undertake, or a deadline for forming the committees.

item.title: Pakistan envoy, opposition leader discuss West Asia conflict
item.description:
Pakistan High Commissioner Imran Haider met Bangladesh’s Leader of the Opposition Shafiqur Rahman on Monday, discussing the West Asia conflict, regional developments and bilateral relations between the two countries.
During the meeting, Shafiqur Rahman appreciated Pakistan’s peacebuilding efforts to resolve the conflict in West Asia. He emphasized the need for sustained dialogue and diplomacy to end the war and alleviate the suffering of affected people.
Haider reiterated Pakistan’s commitment to peace in the region and beyond, thanking the opposition leader for the exchange.
He also briefed Shafiqur Rahman on the progress of bilateral cooperation in health, education, trade, culture and people-to-people contacts.
Both sides expressed satisfaction with the positive momentum in Pakistan-Bangladesh relations.
